    Salesforce Release Notes







The Spring ’26 release helps companies to accelerate their journey to becoming an Agentic Enterprise by
combining human expertise and AI agents — giving every team the insights, automation, and tools they
need to deliver better customer experiences with confidence.

What's New This Release

•• Release Resource Hub. Demos, webinars, and more ways to explore all our latest innovations.
• Admin Release Countdown Blog. Important dates to mark on your calendar for Spring '26.
   Release Overview Deck (ROD). Create internal training for your users, review setup screens, and learn
• how to use features.
• Release Matrix. Quickly see which features immediately affect your users.
• Spring '26 Pre-release Signup. Sign up for a pre-release org to get early access to the new features.
• Spring '26 Release Highlights Module. Get the release Trailhead badge.
   Release in a Box. Use this kit to prepare for the new release and share with your users.

Release Readiness Essentials

• Release Readiness Trailblazers. Access resources and experts for all things release readiness. To help us
   track and respond to your feedback, use a hashtag that indicates the release, such as
• #Spring26Feedback.
   Trust Status Maintenance Site. See sandbox and other release dates and times. To see your
• maintenance dates, select Instances and your instance.
   Sandbox Refresh Calculator, Preview Video, and Preview Instructions. Plan if and when to refresh your
   sandboxes. Learn how to navigate the sandbox preview process. Get early access to new features in
• your sandbox.
• Certification Release Maintenance Schedule. Keep your certification updated in Trailhead.
   Prepare for Salesforce Releases. Use Trailhead to create your release strategy.

Release Notes Tips

• Use the table of contents to browse through release notes by product. You can also search and filter to
• zero in on the news that matters the most.
   Your browser’s settings determine the language that you see. To change the website language, scroll to
• the bottom of this page and use the language switcher in the website footer.
   Salesforce Known Issues are listed separately.

     Note Until the new release is available to you, links from release notes to Salesforce Help,

Release Notes for Features Released Monthly
For some products, Salesforce releases features and enhancements more frequently than three times
per year.

How and When Do Features Become Available?
Some features affect all users immediately after the release goes live. Consider communicating these
changes to your users beforehand so that they’re prepared. Other features require direct action by an
administrator before users can benefit from the new functionality.
Salesforce Overall
Learn about new features and enhancements that affect your Salesforce experience overall.
Release Updates
Salesforce periodically provides release updates that improve the performance, logic, security, and
usability of our products. The Release Updates page provides a list of updates that can be necessary
for your organization to enable. Some release updates affect existing customizations.
Agentforce Platform
Supercharge your workforce efficiency with predictive and generative AI.
Analytics
Analytics enhancements include new and updated features for Tableau Next, Lightning reports and
dashboards, Data 360 reports and dashboards, CRM Analytics, Intelligent apps, and Tableau.
Automation
Compose intelligent workflows with Flow Builder and Flow Orchestration. Integrate across any system
with Flow Integration. Get help from AI to optimize and automate your supply chain business
processes with Agentforce Supply Chain.
Commerce
Commerce enhancements include features for B2C Commerce, B2B Commerce, Omnichannel
Inventory, and Order Management.
Customization
Complete Setup tasks more efficiently with the help of an AI assistant with Setup with Agentforce
(beta). Import and export translation files more easily with enhancements to the Translation
Workbench.
Data 360
Data 360 features and changes are released as often as monthly, so check back again soon for the
latest solutions. Changes included in the Spring 2026 release are generally listed under February.
Deployment
Whether you’re an admin using point-and-click tools or a developer writing code, these enhancements
help you deploy your changes to a target org.
Development


 2

Salesforce Release Notes

  Whether you’re using Lightning components, Visualforce, Apex, or Salesforce APIs with your favorite
  programming language, these enhancements help you develop amazing applications, integrations,
  and packages for resale to other organizations.
  Experience Cloud
  Make your Aura and LWR site pages more discoverable to AI-powered search engines and improve the
  precision of AI-generated answers with generative engine optimization. Create richer HTML content for
  Aura and LWR sites and enjoy greater design flexibility on LWR sites with expanded HTML allowlists
  and more readily available standard LWR components. Updates to Salesforce files make it easier for
  users to manage, delete, upload, and download files. The ability to create custom property types and
  editors for Aura and LWR sites is now generally available.
  Field Service
  See what’s new in Agentforce Field Service, formerly Field Service, to help your team deliver on
  performance and customer service.
  Hyperforce
  Products and features from Data 360, Marketing Cloud, Platform, MuleSoft, and Tableau Cloud are
  now available in more Hyperforce regions. Hyperforce Assistant introduced a new way to find hard-
  coded references. The Hyperforce public IP ranges now include addresses for inbound connections, in
  addition to existing outbound addresses. Prepare for IPv6 if you use IP allowlists.
  Industries
  Learn about new features and enhancements across the Industries clouds.
  Marketing
  Personalize every moment of engagement across the customer lifecycle and drive growth for your
  business with the latest features and enhancements from Salesforce Marketing apps.
  MuleSoft
  Use the MuleSoft Anypoint Platform suite of products to connect and integrate apps, systems, and
  data across your enterprise. Streamline operations by building and automating processes with clicks
  instead of code. You can design, develop, govern, and share APIs and integration apps and host them
  in the cloud or on-premises.
  Mobile
  The Salesforce mobile app now uses single sign-on for faster logins and notifications that lets you work
  on tasks. Create mobile and offline ready Lightning Web components with Mobile MCP tools.
  Omnistudio
  Validate your workflows built with Omniscripts and Flexcards end-to-end by using the UI Test
  Automation Model (UTAM) framework. For a fast, scalable experience, add Omnscripts and Flexcards
  to Lightning Web Runtime (LWR) Experience Cloud sites (pilot). Get immediate help with an
  Omnistudio component or element with the Omnistudio Assistance AI Agent (pilot). With accessibility
  improvements for Omniscripts and Flexcards, create inclusive workflows and solutions for customers
  and users with disabilities. Filter empty records in Omnistudio Data Mapper Extract and Turbo Extract
  components with the Is Null operator.
  Partner Cloud
  Start managing the full partner lifecycle in one place with tools built directly into Salesforce. Use
  Partner Cloud to recruit, onboard, enable, and co-sell with partners while giving them secure access to
  the data and workflows they need. Bring together key capabilities like deal registration, incentives,


    3

Salesforce Release Notes

training, and performance tracking so your team can scale indirect sales and improve partner
relationships. Partner Cloud helps you do more with the partners you already have—faster, and with
less manual work.
Revenue Management
Learn about new features and enhancements for Agentforce Revenue Management.
Sales
Learn about the latest features and updates to grow your pipeline and increase the efficiency of your
sales teams. Sales Cloud is now Agentforce Sales. You may see references to Sales Cloud in our
application and documentation.
Salesforce CMS
Previously known as Sidebar Extensions, Extensions in CMS have an improved development workflow.
Build extensions to add more productivity tools to your CMS content workflow, such as third-party
generative AI tools or tone and grammar editors. When you work with external content providers, you
can now choose which providers are available to your workspace and where to save files from these
systems.
Salesforce Flow Release Notes Have Moved
You can now find Salesforce Flow release notes in the Automation section of the release notes.
Salesforce for Slack Integrations
Use Slack and Salesforce together to connect with customers, track progress, collaborate seamlessly,
and deliver team success from anywhere.
Security, Identity, and Privacy
Redirections end for legacy host names, including instanced host names in API calls. Connected app
creation is disabled by default for all Salesforce orgs. Salesforce Backup & Recover is now a native app.
And, Privacy Requests fulfill your customers' Right to Be Forgotten requests.
Service
Service Cloud is now Agentforce Service. You may see references to Service Cloud in our application
and documentation. Learn about the latest features from Service to supercharge productivity across
your organization. Service features are released as often as monthly, so check here for the latest
information.
Other Salesforce Products and Services
Get the latest information on these new features.
Legal Documentation
We made seasonal updates to Salesforce Legal Documents.
Previous Release Notes
Find information about previously announced features in the release note archive.

Salesforce Overall

Learn about new features and enhancements that affect your Salesforce experience overall.

 General Enhancements
 Spring ’26 gives you more reasons to love Lightning Experience.
 Archive App
 Manage growing data volumes and improve system performance by autoarchiving old or inactive data.
 Keep only important and reliable information in production.
 Salesforce Foundations
 Define audience segments directly from the Lead and Contact lists you’re already using. Use the new
 Email Builder Lite to create and send batch emails to your Sales contacts and leads. Tableau
 dashboards are now in the Marketing App.
 Salesforce Data Pipelines
 Securely access your Amazon Redshift data by using a virtual private connection. Take advantage of
 OAuth functionality in your Microsoft Azure SQL Database connection.
 Salesforce Scheduler
 Get a faster, more secure, and more efficient Salesforce Scheduler experience with enhancements that
 include Scheduler flow components in LWR sites, increased service resource capacity for
 appointments, and a simplified flat list view for waitlist participants.
 Trust Site Enhancements
 The Trust site is the single place to see the status of Salesforce services and products, upcoming
 availability impacting activities, and availability-related communications.

General Enhancements

Spring ’26 gives you more reasons to love Lightning Experience.

 Verify Your Email Domain Ownership
 To avoid disruption in email sent from Salesforce, verify the domains that you own with a DomainKeys
 Identified Mail (DKIM) key or an authorized email domain. As part of our ongoing efforts to strengthen
 the security of our email services, email domain verification is now mandatory. Salesforce no longer
 delivers emails from unverified domains, even if the email addresses are verified.
 Prepare for Shorter Certificate Lifespans


 113

Salesforce Release Notes Salesforce Overall

  If you use features that rely on certificates, prepare to update the related certificates more frequently.
  An upcoming industry-wide change decreases the maximum allowed Transport Layer Security (TLS)
  certificate lifespan over the next 3 years. Also, Salesforce plans to stop public certificate rotation
  announcements.
  Get Ready for IPv6
  To help mitigate the IP address scarcity of IPv4, Salesforce is working behind the scenes to support
  IPv6. If you use an IP allowlist to restrict network traffic or you restrict access to Salesforce via IP
  address, consider implementing a preferred alternative. Otherwise, prepare to update your allowlists
  to include IPv6 addresses.
  Update Your mTLS Certificates
  If you use publicly trusted certificates for mTLS (Mutual Transport Layer Security) and the Public Root
  CA (certificate authority) is in the Chrome Trusted Root List, transition to separate certificate
  hierarchies. Google Chrome is enforcing policy changes that limit the use of those certificates to TLS
  (Transport Layer Security) server authentication only.
  Elevate Your Salesforce Go Experience with Smarter Filters and Enhanced Search
  Tailor your Salesforce Go home page to focus on the features that matter most to you by rearranging
  or removing specific sections. When you filter your view by cloud, add a subvertical filter to see which
  feature sets and features apply to specific verticals within the cloud. Also, use enhanced search to spot
  the differences between features and feature sets with the same names.
  Capture Employee Details for Unified Employee License Holders
  Designate employees who have the Unified Employee license as employee users and capture more
  details for your reports, such as employee status and number.
  Styling Change to Highlighted and Selected Content
  To meet the Web Content Accessibility Guideline (WCAG) 1.4.11 standard for non-text accessibility, we
  changed the styling of highlighted and selected content throughout the Lightning UI. Previously, we
  applied our own styling to show when content was highlighted or selected, but have determined that
  the styling didn’t meet this WCAG standard. Now when you highlight or select content, the Lightning
  UI uses the styling applied by the user agent, which is your browser or device. The user agent
  determines the color contrast ratio.
  Styling Change to Read-Only Checkboxes
  When you view a record, read-only checkboxes no longer specify the disabled attribute, so screen
  readers can now announce the state and value of the checkboxes. Read-only checkboxes now display
  with hover text "True" or "False".
  Enable Accessibility Enhancements for Page Headers and Modal Windows When Zoom Is Greater
  Than 200% (Release Update)
  To help meet Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2 for Resize and Reflow, enable
  Lightning Experience to adapt the behavior of page headers and modal windows when viewed at high
  magnification. This is the beginning of our effort to comply with WCAG 2.2 Resize and Reflow
  guidelines. Expect accessibility enhancements to other UI elements in future release updates.
  Enable Accessibility Enhancements for Cards, Docked Containers, Menu Lists, and Panels (Release
  Update)
  To help meet Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2 for Resize and Reflow, enable
  Lightning Experience to adapt the behavior of cards, docked containers, menu lists, and panels when

Salesforce Release Notes Salesforce Overall

   viewed at high magnification. This release update is dependent on the Enable Accessibility
   Enhancements for Page Headers and Modal Windows When Zoom Is Greater Than 200% release
   update. Make sure to enable that update first.
   Enable Accessibility Enhancements for Date Pickers, Popovers, Bottom Utility Bars, Record Headers

   To help meet Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2 for Resize and Reflow, enable

Verify Your Email Domain Ownership

To avoid disruption in email sent from Salesforce, verify the domains that you own with a DomainKeys
Identified Mail (DKIM) key or an authorized email domain. As part of our ongoing efforts to strengthen
the security of our email services, email domain verification is now mandatory. Salesforce no longer
delivers emails from unverified domains, even if the email addresses are verified.

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience and Salesforce Classic in all editions except
Salesforce Free Suite and Database.com. This change has no impact on trial orgs.

This change doesn't affect emails sent through Gmail™ and Office 365® (Outlook) integrations or via
Einstein Activity Capture tool (“Inbox”). Emails that end in @gmail.com, @hotmail.com, or
@outlook.com are also exempt from the domain-level verification requirement. And domain verification
isn’t required for Marketing Cloud or Marketing Cloud Advanced emails.

When: In existing orgs, Salesforce generated a temporary allowlist of email-sending domains used over
several weeks in January and February 2026.

These changes take effect shortly after your org gets Spring '26, patch 11.

• Verification is required for all new email-sending domains, regardless of whether you add the domain


    115

Salesforce Release Notes Salesforce Overall

• to a new or existing org.
• Verification is required for existing email-sending domains that aren’t allowlisted.
• In sandboxes, verification of the allowlisted domains is required starting April 7, 2026.
   In all other orgs, including production, verification of the allowlisted domains is required starting April
   27, 2026.

For more information, see these knowledge articles: Determine Your Temporarily Allowlisted Email-
Sending Domains, Mandatory Sending-Email Domain Verification Timeline, and Spring ’26 Email-Sending
Domain Verification Requirement.

Why: This change affects emails sent from Salesforce and related automations with an email-sending
domain that Salesforce doesn't own, including system-generated emails.

For example, if your users' email addresses are in the format name@example.com , verify that you own
 example.com . Similarly, Salesforce can't send system-generated emails from an organization-wide
address with an unverified domain, even if the individual email address is verified.

How: Verify each of your email-sending domains. Each domain and subdomain requires separate
verification via an active DKIM key. If you can’t use a DKIM key, configure a verified entry in the
Authorized Email Domains list in Setup.

To minimize disruption, enable a substitute email address for unverified domains. From Setup, in the
Quick Find Box, enter Deliverability, and then select Deliverability. Select Use a substitute email
address for unverified domains, and save your changes. That setting is available when email domain
verification is required in your org.

   Salesforce Help:Set Up Secure DKIM Keys

Prepare for Shorter Certificate Lifespans

If you use features that rely on certificates, prepare to update the related certificates more frequently. An
upcoming industry-wide change decreases the maximum allowed Transport Layer Security (TLS)
certificate lifespan over the next 3 years. Also, Salesforce plans to stop public certificate rotation
announcements.

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience, Salesforce Classic, and the Salesforce mobile app in
all editions. As we reach each milestone, the lifespans apply to all new certificates that a public
Certificate Authority (CA) signs, regardless of whether you, Salesforce, or a third party purchases the
certificate. Existing certificates keep their expiration dates, and self-signed certificates aren't subject to
the new lifespans.




    116

Salesforce Release Notes Salesforce Overall

When: In August 2025, the Certification Authority Browser Forum (CA/Browser Forum) announced a
phased approach to shorten the lifespan for new TLS certificates. That lifespan decreases from 398 days
to 200 days on March 15, 2026, to 100 days on March 15, 2027, and to 47 days on March 15, 2029.

As certificates rotate more frequently, Salesforce plans to stop the existing announcements for certificate
changes for first-party (1P) production orgs through the Certificate Changes Trailblazer Community
group. There's no specific target date for the end of those announcements. Salesforce plans to announce
that date at least 90 days in advance.

Why: Salesforce complies with the guidance of the CA/Browser Forum, the organization that sets most
Web Public Key Infrastructure (WebPKI) rules. Their TLS Server Baseline Requirements change regularly.
Those requirements are outside of Salesforce control, and certificate vendors are bound by the same
rules.

How: Review your certificate use and plan to rotate the certificates that you own more frequently and
stop using certificate pinning.

To receive notifications about upcoming certificate expirations for certificates that are stored in your org,
assign the Expired Certificate Notification permission to specific admins. To automate the creation and
update of self-signed and Certificate Authority-signed certificates in Salesforce, use the Certificate
Metadata API type.

See Also
  Salesforce Help: Certificates in Salesforce
  Salesforce Help: Set Expired Certificate Notification Permission
  Metadata API Developer Guide: Certificate

Get Ready for IPv6

To help mitigate the IP address scarcity of IPv4, Salesforce is working behind the scenes to support IPv6.
If you use an IP allowlist to restrict network traffic or you restrict access to Salesforce via IP address,
consider implementing a preferred alternative. Otherwise, prepare to update your allowlists to include
IPv6 addresses.

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience and Salesforce Classic in all editions.

When: Today, IPv6 is supported only for the Salesforce Content Delivery Network (CDN) for Experience
Cloud sites. With full IPv6 support, users and integrations can connect to Salesforce via an IPv6 address.
We’re announcing this upcoming change to give you time to update your allowlists.

There’s no specific target date for full IPv6 support. Salesforce plans to roll out IPv6 support in stages,
starting with Salesforce Government Cloud orgs. Government Cloud customers, check the IP Addresses
to Allow for Government Cloud Plus Knowledge Article for that information in early 2026.

Check future release notes for the specific timing for each stage. For other stages, Salesforce plans to
provide the IPv6 addresses to allow at least 2 months before IPv6 is fully supported in the affected orgs.




    117

Salesforce Release Notes Salesforce Overall

Why: IP address restrictions can exist both in and outside Salesforce.

In Salesforce, an IP address allowlist range can include either IPv4 or IPv6 addresses but not both types.
When Salesforce supports IPv6 for your org, IPv4 allowlists remain active, and users can only log in via an
IPv6 address that their profile allows. To make sure that your users can continue to access Salesforce
after this change, for each profile with a login IP range, add one or more login IP ranges with those users’
IPv6 addresses.

Outside Salesforce, your company can restrict network traffic. An example is an allowlist that determines
which IP addresses your users can access or which IP addresses can access your network. If those
allowlists don’t include Salesforce IPv6 addresses when Salesforce supports IPv6, users can experience
disruption, and integrations can fail.

How: If you use IP allowlists, consider a preferred alternative, such as domain allowlists or Service Name
Indication (SNI).

If you continue to restrict access to Salesforce by IP address, update your allowlists in Salesforce. There’s
no correlation between an IPv6 address and an IPv4 address. To determine your users’ IPv6 addresses,
work with your network team.

If you continue to restrict network traffic via IP address, plan to update those allowlists to include
Salesforce IPv6 addresses when those addresses are available.

See Also
  Salesforce Help: Set Trusted IP Ranges for Your Organization
  Salesforce Help: Restrict Login IP Addresses in Profiles

Update Your mTLS Certificates

If you use publicly trusted certificates for mTLS (Mutual Transport Layer Security) and the Public Root CA
(certificate authority) is in the Chrome Trusted Root List, transition to separate certificate hierarchies.
Google Chrome is enforcing policy changes that limit the use of those certificates to TLS (Transport Layer
Security) server authentication only.

Where: This change applies to certificate-based authentication and API client certificates that enforce
TLS mutual authentication in Lightning Experience and Salesforce Classic. Certificate-based
authentication is available in Personal, Enterprise, Performance, Unlimited, Developer, and
Database.com editions.

When: Google Chrome enforces these policy changes on March 15, 2027. However, some customers
have reported related issues upon certificate renewal.

Why: Google Chrome Root Program Policy v1.7 prevents the purchase and use of dual-use certificates
that are issued by Public Root CAs in the Chrome Trusted Root List. The new policy requires dedicated
Public Key Infrastructure (PKI) hierarchies for different certificate purposes. In other words, the policy
separates certificates that identify websites (Server Authentication) from certificates that identify clients
or users (Client Authentication).


    118

Salesforce Release Notes Salesforce Overall

How: Although Google is making this change, we’re announcing it here so that you can prevent
disruption, including issues with access to Salesforce. Review the Upcoming Mandatory Changes to
Public Key Infrastructure (PKI) knowledge article and complete the recommended steps. That article
includes the guidance that Salesforce can provide about this change.

® Note Salesforce Customer Support can’t troubleshoot issues related to this change beyond sharing
     the information published in that knowledge article.
See Also
  Knowledge Article: Upcoming Mandatory Changes to Public Key Infrastructure (PKI)

Styling Change to Highlighted and Selected Content

To meet the Web Content Accessibility Guideline (WCAG) 1.4.11 standard for non-text accessibility, we
changed the styling of highlighted and selected content throughout the Lightning UI. Previously, we
applied our own styling to show when content was highlighted or selected, but have determined that the
styling didn’t meet this WCAG standard. Now when you highlight or select content, the Lightning UI uses
the styling applied by the user agent, which is your browser or device. The user agent determines the
color contrast ratio.

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience.

Why: Meeting accessibility standards helps your UI support all of your users.

Styling Change to Read-Only Checkboxes

When you view a record, read-only checkboxes no longer specify the disabled attribute, so screen



120

Salesforce Release Notes Salesforce Overall

readers can now announce the state and value of the checkboxes. Read-only checkboxes now display
with hover text "True" or "False".

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience.

Why: Meeting accessibility standards helps your UI support all of your users.

How: In Lightning Experience, the change applies to record pages that use LWC. When you view a
record, fields and checkboxes are read-only.

A read-only checkbox on a record page displays these behaviors.

• If selected, a read-only checkbox displays a gray checkmark only. Previously, a read-only checkbox
   that's selected displays a checkmark enclosed in a disabled gray checkbox.
• If not selected, a read-only checkbox displays as an empty checkbox with a dotted icon . Previously,
• a read-only checkbox that's not selected displays a disabled gray checkbox.
   If required, a read-only checkbox displays without an asterisk because it can’t be checked or
   unchecked.

On a list view, checkboxes in a column also display with the updated styling.

     Note Record pages that use Aura components, such as the record pages for Campaign and Task,
     continue to display read-only checkboxes with a gray border when selected and when not
     selected .

Enable Accessibility Enhancements for Page Headers and Modal Windows
When Zoom Is Greater Than 200% (Release Update)

To help meet Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2 for Resize and Reflow, enable Lightning
Experience to adapt the behavior of page headers and modal windows when viewed at high
magnification. This is the beginning of our effort to comply with WCAG 2.2 Resize and Reflow guidelines.
Expect accessibility enhancements to other UI elements in future release updates.

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience in all editions.

When: Salesforce enforces this update in Summer ’26. To get the major release upgrade date for your
instance, go to Trust Status, search for your instance, and click the Maintenance tab.

Why: With this update, content is visible for users who view Salesforce via a browser at 200%
magnification or greater.

Without this update, you can have trouble seeing the content on a page when you zoom in over 200%.
The page headers can block content as you scroll. In modal windows, buttons and other content can
display outside the viewport, requiring horizontal scrolling, which can make modal windows unusable.


    121

Salesforce Release Notes Salesforce Overall

These changes help you support users who want to zoom 300% to 400%. The page header scrolls with
the page and doesn’t block the content. In modal windows, buttons and content display within the
viewport and the window is fully functional.

How: To review this update, from Setup, in the Quick Find box, enter Release Updates, and then
select Release Updates. For Enable Accessibility Enhancements for Page Headers and Modal Windows
When Zoom Is Greater Than 200%, follow the testing and activation steps.

Enable Accessibility Enhancements for Cards, Docked Containers, Menu
Lists, and Panels (Release Update)

To help meet Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2 for Resize and Reflow, enable Lightning
Experience to adapt the behavior of cards, docked containers, menu lists, and panels when viewed at
high magnification. This release update is dependent on the Enable Accessibility Enhancements for Page
Headers and Modal Windows When Zoom Is Greater Than 200% release update. Make sure to enable
that update first.

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience in all editions.

When: Salesforce enforces this update in Winter ’27. To get the major release upgrade date for your
instance, go to Trust Status, search for your instance, and click the Maintenance tab.

Why: With this update, content displays correctly in cards, docked containers, menu lists, and panels for
users who view Salesforce via a browser at 200% magnification or greater.

Without this update, these parts of the Salesforce UI aren’t compliant with WCAG 2.2 guidelines for
Resize and Reflow. Content potentially displays only partially.

These changes help you support users with visual impairments.

• Cards, docked containers, menu lists, and panels are accessible and usable at 1280px page width and
• 400% magnification.
   The header content in these UI elements isn’t clipped. Instead, it wraps to the next line.

How: To review this update, from Setup, in the Quick Find box, enter Release Updates, and then
select Release Updates. For Enable Accessibility Enhancements for Cards, Docked Containers, Menu
Lists, and Panels, follow the testing and activation steps.

Scheduler enabled.

Add More Service Resources to Appointments

Salesforce Scheduler now supports adding up to 20 mandatory service resources to a single
appointment in appointment booking flows. Now, when scheduling an appointment in the user
interface, you can add more service resources and find the right slot. This change supports complex
scheduling scenarios, such as tribunals, court hearings, panel reviews, team presentations, and so on.

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience in Enterprise and Unlimited editions with Salesforce
Scheduler enabled.

How: To enable this feature, contact Salesforce Customer Support.

Easily View Waitlist Participants With a Flat List

More efficiently manage large waitlists with a flat waitlist of participants. This change improves the
readability of waitlists by grouping and displaying waitlist participants in a single list ordered by check-in
time. When enabled, you can also use custom appointment groups. Previously, participants were always
grouped by work type group.

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience in Enterprise and Unlimited editions with Salesforce

Release Updates

Salesforce periodically provides release updates that improve the performance, logic, security, and
usability of our products. The Release Updates page provides a list of updates that can be necessary for
your organization to enable. Some release updates affect existing customizations.

Every time a release update is created, it gets scheduled to be enforced in a future release. We announce
each update and its schedule here as soon as that schedule is known, but occasionally, updates are
postponed or canceled. If that happens, we let you know in the section that describes that specific
release update.

Often, release updates provide a Test Run option so you can enable an update and examine any changes
to your org, including changes to customizations, before that update’s Complete Steps By date. You can
view attachments in the Salesforce mobile app, but you can’t edit them.




    133

Salesforce Release Notes Release Updates

To view release updates, from Setup, in the Quick Find box, enter Release Updates, and select Release
Updates.

Enforced with This Release

These updates are scheduled to be enforced this release.

Escape the Label Attribute of <apex:inputField> Elements to Prevent Cross-Site Scripting in
Visualforce Pages (Release Update)
        To prevent malicious code from executing in cross-site scripting (XSS) attacks on your Visualforce
        pages, this release update escapes the label attribute of your <apex:inputField> tags. First
        available in Spring ’23, this update is enforced in Spring ’26.

Update References to Legacy Host Names (Release Update)
        Prevent disruption for your customers and end users when the temporary redirection of legacy
        (non-enhanced) Salesforce host names ends. With this release update, those redirections end in
        all orgs. First available in Spring ’25, this update is enforced in Spring ’26.

Scheduled to Be Enforced in Summer ’26

These updates are scheduled to be enforced in Summer ’26. The list can include new, previously
announced, and previously postponed release updates.

Enable Accessibility Enhancements for Date Pickers, Popovers, Bottom Utility Bars, Record Headers
(Release Update)
        To help meet Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2 for Resize and Reflow, enable
        Lightning Experience to adapt the behavior of date pickers, popovers, bottom utility bars, and
        record headers when viewed at high magnification. This release update is dependent on the
        Enable Accessibility Enhancements for Page Headers and Modal Windows When Zoom Is
        Greater Than 200% release update.

Enable Accessibility Enhancements for Page Headers and Modal Windows When Zoom Is Greater
Than 200% (Release Update)
        To help meet Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2 for Resize and Reflow, enable
        Lightning Experience to adapt the behavior of page headers and modal windows when viewed at
        high magnification. This is the beginning of our effort to comply with WCAG 2.2 Resize and
        Reflow guidelines.

Migrate to a Multiple-Configuration SAML Framework (Release Update)
        If you see this release update, your Salesforce instance is using our original single-configuration
        SAML framework, which supports single sign-on (SSO) with only one identity provider. We’re
        giving you a final reminder that with the Summer ’26 release, we’re no longer supporting the
        single-configuration SAML framework. To make sure that your SSO configurations don’t break,



    134

Salesforce Release Notes Release Updates

        migrate to our newer multiple-configuration SAML framework, which supports SSO with multiple
        identity providers instead of just one. If you don't migrate, your SAML single sign-on
        configurations will stop working when this release update is enforced in Summer ’26.

Salesforce-Managed X (Formerly Twitter) Authentication Provider Retirement (Release Update)
        The Salesforce-managed app for the X (formerly Twitter) authentication provider is being retired.
        This update breaks any single sign-on (SSO) configurations that use the Salesforce-managed X
        app. To avoid disruptions, create a custom X app and update your SSO configurations.

Use Visualforce PDF Rendering Service with Apex Blob.toPdf() (Release Update)
        With this update enabled, the Apex Blob.toPdf() method for PDF rendering uses the same
        rendering service as Visualforce. The Visualforce PDF rendering service offers improvements such
        as additional fonts and multibyte character support. This change makes PDF rendering more
        consistent on the Salesforce Platform.

Scheduled to Be Enforced in Winter ’27

These updates are scheduled to be enforced in Winter ’27. The list can include new, previously
announced, and previously postponed release updates.

Adopt Authorized Email Domains (Release Update)
        If you previously worked with Salesforce Customer Support to disable email change verifications,
        set up authorized email domains instead. Salesforce is retiring the existing exemption process for
        disabling this feature, and authorized email domains provide the same benefit.

Enable Accessibility Enhancements for Cards, Docked Containers, Menu Lists, and Panels (Release
Update)
        To help meet Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2 for Resize and Reflow, enable
        Lightning Experience to adapt the behavior of cards, docked containers, menu lists, and panels
        when viewed at high magnification. This release update is dependent on the Enable Accessibility
        Enhancements for Page Headers and Modal Windows When Zoom Is Greater Than 200%
        release update.

Retirement of OAuth 2.0 Username-Password Flow for Connected Apps (Release Update)
        In Winter ’27, we'll stop supporting the OAuth 2.0 username-password flow for connected apps.
        This update will break all connected app integrations that use this flow. For better security,
        update your integrations to use the OAuth 2.0 web-server flow or the OAuth 2.0 client
        credentials flow instead.

Update Instanced URLs in API Traffic (Release Update)
        To prevent disruption when Salesforce ends support for API traffic that uses an incorrect
        instanced URL, make sure that API traffic to your org uses the org’s My Domain login URL. First
        available in Summer ’25, this release update was scheduled to be enforced in Spring ’26, but we

Salesforce to Salesforce Is Being Retired (Release Update)
        Salesforce to Salesforce is being retired in Spring ’27. Salesforce has more powerful and
        integrated solutions that align with modern business needs. To prevent disruption when
        Salesforce ends support for the Salesforce to Salesforce product, make sure that you migrate
        your integrations to one of these recommended solutions: Partner Cloud, Data Cloud One,
        MuleSoft Anypoint, or MuleSoft for Flow.

Update Apex Code and Flows for Changed Sharing Recalculation Behavior (Release Update)
        To optimize performance after large-scale updates to groups or roles, Salesforce now performs
        some sharing recalculations asynchronously. If Apex code and flows require that share records be
        updated immediately, the code and flows can break when this release update is enforced.
        Update Apex classes, tests, and flows that update group membership or roles if they rely on
        synchronous sharing recalculation. This update is available starting in Spring ’26.

announced, and previously postponed release updates.

SOAP API login() Call in SOAP API Versions 31.0 Through 64.0 Is Being Retired (Release Update)

        be supported and no longer be available.

Bring the power of assistive and autonomous AI to your business with Agentforce.

  The New Agentforce Builder Is Now Generally Available
  Build powerful, predictable agents with the new Agentforce Builder in Agentforce Studio, now
  generally available. With Agent Script at its core, you can combine logical expressions and natural
  language prompts to create agents that follow sophisticated, multi-step workflows. With in-depth
  agent previews, trace, and debugging, you can release those agents to production with confidence.
  And with AI assistance built right into the text editor-inspired interface, you can get help at any stage.
  Convert Audio to Text with Speech To Text Action


                                    140

Salesforce Release Notes Agentforce Platform

  Use the Speech To Text action to convert audio files into text during agent interactions and automated
  workflows. Agents can accept an audio file ID and return a transcript for use in conversations or
  downstream automation. The action supports multiple languages and common audio formats such as
  MP3, WAV, FLAC, OGG, OGA, AMR, MPEG, MPGA. The Speech To Text action is available in the
  Agentforce Builder, Flow, REST, and Apex.
  Improve Web Search Results By Using Allowed Domains
  The Search The Web agent action now supports specifying allowed domains to filter web search
  results. You can enter up to 10 allowed domains to limit search results to approved websites. Allowed
  domains are configured per action and don’t affect Trusted URLs defined in Salesforce Setup. If no
  domains are specified, web searches follow the default provider behavior and are not restricted by
  domain. For existing agents, admins must re-add the Search The Web agent action in the Agentforce
  Builder to access the allowed domains setting.
  Build Complex Agents Faster with the Latest Enhancements to Canvas View (Beta)
  In the new Agentforce Builder, Canvas view now includes powerful features that were previously only
  available in Script view. We also introduced new features and improvements that streamline the agent
  development process.
  Connect Agents to Enhanced Chat v2 in Agentforce Builder (Beta)
  You can now add the Enhanced Chat v2 connection to an Agentforce Service agent in the new
  Agentforce Builder. This connection gives the agent context and structure that helps it deliver
  conversational messages on Enhanced Chat v2 deployments. You can also create and view your
  agent’s Enhanced Chat channels and Enhanced Chat v2 deployments on the connection's routing
  page. Previously, Messaging was the only connection available in the new Agentforce Builder and you
  couldn’t remove it from agents.
  Create Employee Agents in the New Agentforce Builder (Beta)
  The new Agentforce Builder now supports Agentforce Employee agents, so you can build agents that
  support your customers and your employees. Previously, you could only create Agentforce Service
  agents, and you could only create them from scratch. Now when you create an agent, you can choose
  the default Agentforce Employee Agent template and get a head start with prebuilt topics and actions.
  Plus, any agents you build in the new Agentforce Builder appear in the agent list views in the
  Agentforce Studio app and Agentforce Agents Setup pages. No matter where you open them, they
  open in the new Agentforce Builder.
  Build High-Quality Agents with Validation Enhancements in the New Agentforce Builder (Beta)
  In the new Agentforce Builder, we’ve added validation checks to agent actions, so you can be
  confident that your agent has all of the tools it needs to do its jobs. Plus, we’ve made it easier to get
  the error messages you need to make quick fixes.
  Migrate Your Agents’ Connected Apps to the External Client App Framework
  With the Spring '26 release, you can no longer create connected apps. For the best customer
  experience, migrate your connected apps to external client apps. External client apps provide
  enhanced security, streamlined packaging, and a more robust framework for your apps. Existing
  connected apps and connected apps for Slack in the legacy Agentforce Builder aren’t impacted.

  Additional Analytics Metrics

    - The default Agentforce Service agent template is now supported in the new builder, so you can get
     started with out-of-the-box topics and actions for customer-facing use cases. Previously, you could

     variables).
    - We’ve made it easier to copy and paste content to and from the Canvas. Plus, we’ve added support
     for more keyboard shortcuts, including familiar favorites (Ctrl or Cmd+c to copy) and some handy
•    new ones (Ctrl or Cmd+a+a to select the contents of an entire block of instructions).
   Welcome messages: Agent welcome messages now support context variables, so you can personalize
•  how your agents greet your customers and employees. Learn more.
   Agent previews: In the Interaction Details panel of a preview conversation, you can show or hide
   system events in the trace view. System events are hidden by default, so you can focus on your agent’s
   actions, reasoning, and responses. Plus, when you click into an event, you can expand the JSON for

Convert Audio to Text with Speech To Text Action

Use the Speech To Text action to convert audio files into text during agent interactions and automated
workflows. Agents can accept an audio file ID and return a transcript for use in conversations or
downstream automation. The action supports multiple languages and common audio formats such as
MP3, WAV, FLAC, OGG, OGA, AMR, MPEG, MPGA. The Speech To Text action is available in the
Agentforce Builder, Flow, REST, and Apex.

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience in Enterprise, Performance, Unlimited, and
Developer Editions with Foundations or Agentforce 1 Editions.

When: This change is available starting from February 17, 2026.

How: In Agentforce Builder, in the Conversation Preview, enter convert speech to text, provide the
Audio File ID when prompted, and click Submit.

See Also
  Salesforce Help: Agentforce Platform | Speech To Text

Improve Web Search Results By Using Allowed Domains

The Search The Web agent action now supports specifying allowed domains to filter web search results.
You can enter up to 10 allowed domains to limit search results to approved websites. Allowed domains
are configured per action and don’t affect Trusted URLs defined in Salesforce Setup. If no domains are
specified, web searches follow the default provider behavior and are not restricted by domain. For
existing agents, admins must re-add the Search The Web agent action in the Agentforce Builder to access
the allowed domains setting.

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience in Enterprise, Performance, Unlimited, and
Developer Editions with Foundations or Agentforce 1 Editions.

When: This change is available starting from February 17, 2026.

How: In Agentforce Builder, open the Search The Web agent action and click Edit Action. In the Inputs
section, locate the Allowed Domains, and enter up to 10 comma-separated domains.

Build Complex Agents Faster with the Latest Enhancements to Canvas View
(Beta)

In the new Agentforce Builder, Canvas view now includes powerful features that were previously only
available in Script view. We also introduced new features and improvements that streamline the agent
development process.

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience in Enterprise, Performance, Unlimited, and
Developer Editions with Foundations or Agentforce 1 Editions.

 ® Note The new Agentforce Builder is a beta service that is subject to the Beta Services Terms at
     Agreements - Salesforce.com or your written Unified Pilot Agreement, and applicable terms in the
     Product Terms Directory. Use of this beta service consumes usage types per the Agentforce and
     Generative AI Usage and Billing documentation and is at the Customer’s sole discretion.

When: This change is available starting the week of January 5, 2026.

Why:

• When you add an action to a topic, the action is automatically added to the topic’s reasoning actions.
   Previously, you had to manually reference the action in your topic before the agent could use it.


    146

Salesforce Release Notes Agentforce Platform

• Create, add, and manage variables on the Variables page in Canvas view. Also, you can create a
   variable that's set to an action output in a topic’s actions available for reasoning (reasoning actions).
• Previously, you could only create, add, and manage variables in Script view.
   Add filters in the Topic Selector and in a topic’s reasoning actions. When a topic or action has a filter,
   your agent can use it only when the filter conditions are met. Previously, you could only create filters in
• Script view.
   Add follow-up actions in a topic’s reasoning actions. Follow-up actions let you tell an agent what to do
   immediately after an action runs. For example, you can have the agent chain actions or transition to a
• specific topic. Previously, you could only define follow-up actions in Script view.
   Add agent-level instructions on the System Messages page in Canvas view. Agent-level instructions
   apply to all of an agent’s reasoning and interactions. You can use them to define an agent’s tone,
• persona, style, and goals.
   The Filter from agent action setting on agent action outputs has been renamed to Include in agent
   context, to better reflect its functionality in the new Agentforce Builder. When the setting is enabled,
   the output is added to the agent’s conversation history and made available for reasoning. Disable the
   setting for any underlying reference action outputs you don’t want to use with your agent.

Build High-Quality Agents with Validation Enhancements in the New
Agentforce Builder (Beta)

In the new Agentforce Builder, we’ve added validation checks to agent actions, so you can be confident
that your agent has all of the tools it needs to do its jobs. Plus, we’ve made it easier to get the error
messages you need to make quick fixes.

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience in Enterprise, Performance, Unlimited, and
Developer Editions with Foundations or Agentforce 1 Editions.

     Note The new Agentforce Builder is a beta service that is subject to the Beta Services Terms at
     Agreements - Salesforce.com or your written Unified Pilot Agreement, and applicable terms in the
     Product Terms Directory. Use of this beta service consumes usage types per the Agentforce and
     Generative AI Usage and Billing documentation and is at the Customer’s sole discretion.

When: This change is available starting the week of January 5, 2026.

Why:

• When you save a change to an action, Agentforce Builder lets you know if the underlying flow, prompt
   template, or other reference action is missing, or if there’s an issue with the names or data types of the
• action’s inputs and outputs.
   When an agent has errors, you now see information about the errors in Canvas view as well as Script
   view. For more detailed error information, switch to Script view. Previously, errors were only available in
• Script view.
   In Script view, you no longer have to go to the Agent Definition page to see detailed error information.
   Previously, Agent Script was broken into sections in Script view, so your agent’s complete script and
   any errors were only available on the Agent Definition page. Now, your agent’s script is presented in a


    149

Salesforce Release Notes Agentforce Platform

   single, continuous view. You can scroll to any block or error, and you can use the Explorer panel to
   jump to different blocks.

Migrate Your Agents’ Connected Apps to the External Client App Framework

With the Spring '26 release, you can no longer create connected apps. For the best customer experience,
migrate your connected apps to external client apps. External client apps provide enhanced security,
streamlined packaging, and a more robust framework for your apps. Existing connected apps and
connected apps for Slack in the legacy Agentforce Builder aren’t impacted.

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience in Enterprise, Performance, Unlimited, and
Developer editions.

When: This change is available in early January 2026.

How: To create an external client app from a connected app, open the connected app in App Manager
and then click Migrate to External Client App. In Agentforce Builder (beta), connect the external client
app to your agent using the Messaging connection. After you create an external client app from a
connected app, the connected app is read-only in App Manager.

Existing connected apps and external client apps with these OAuth scopes appear in the External Apps
list in the Messaging connection.

•• Access chatbot services (chatbot_api)
• Access the Salesforce API Platform (sfap_api)
   Manage user data via APIs (api)

Evaluate AI Performance with New RAG Metrics and Enriched Analytics

Measure the quality, accuracy, and relevance of your agent's responses with three new Retrieval-
Augmented Generation (RAG) evaluation metrics. The new Answer Faithfulness, Answer Relevance, and
Context Relevance metrics added to the Analytics Foundation Data Model give you a trust score of your
AI agent's interactions. Metadata labels for Agent topics and Agent types were also added to the
semantic model builder.

Where: This change applies to Agentforce in Lightning Experience in Enterprise and Unlimited editions
with the Einstein for Sales, Einstein for Platform, or Einstein for Service add-on.

When: These changes are available starting the week of February 9, 2026.

Why: To monitor and quantify your AI agent's customer support quality, you need to know how
accurately AI agents are answering customers questions and requests:

• Average Answer Faithfulness Score: Measures how well the agent adheres to your grounded source
• data (like Knowledge Base articles).
   Average Answer Relevance Score: Measures how well the response addresses the customer's
• question or request.
   Average Context Relevance Score: Measures if the agent retrieved the correct data source to answer
   the question.

How: To start using these metrics, in Setup, toggle on Audit and Feedback and Knowledge/RAG Quality
Data and Metrics.

Connect Agents to Your Knowledge Sources in the New Agentforce Builder

Build agents grounded in your unique business data with the predictability that your business demands.
Now, you can use the Answer Questions with Knowledge action via an Agentforce Data Library in the
new Agentforce Builder. Agents built in the new Agentforce Builder can access the knowledge you’ve
added to their assigned data library, ensuring they provide the most accurate and up-to-date responses.

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience in Enterprise, Performance, and Unlimited editions
with Agentforce for Service, Agentforce for Sales, Foundations or Agentforce 1 editions. Agentforce Data
Library requires Data Cloud. Intelligent Context isn’t available in Data Cloud 1 orgs.

® Note The new Agentforce Builder is a beta service that is subject to the Beta Services Terms at
     Agreements - Salesforce.com or your written Unified Pilot Agreement, and applicable terms in the
     Product Terms Directory. Use of this beta service consumes usage types per the Agentforce and
     Generative AI Usage and Billing documentation and is at the Customer’s sole discretion.

When: This feature is available in December 2025.

How: The new Agentforce Builder makes it possible to build more complex, more reliable agents in a text
editor-inspired interface.

From the App Launcher, find and select Agentforce Studio, and then click Agents. There are two steps to
ground your Agents on your knowledge: 1) add a data library that contains the knowledge you want your
agents to use, and 2) add the Answer Questions with Knowledge action. To add a data library to a new or
existing agent, in the Explorer click Data, then select Data Library. A Data Library tab opens in the canvas
and your available data libraries appear in the dropdown list. Select a data library and, to show citations,
select Show sources. To create a data library, go to Agentforce Data Library in Setup.

Route Agentforce Voice Calls Using SIP

Take advantage of the internet’s cost-effective and flexible virtual connection. Route calls to an
Agentforce Service agent using Session Initiation Protocol (SIP). This protocol transmits calls over the
internet. Previously, you could route these calls with a Public Switched Telephone Network (PSTN) phone
number only.

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience in Enterprise, Performance, Unlimited, and
Developer Editions with Foundations or Agentforce 1 Editions.

When: This feature is available starting from February 26, 2026.

How: To set up Agentforce Voice with SIP, in the Agentforce Voice setup page, click the SIP tab. This tab
walks you through the setup steps.

Opt Out of Allowing Salesforce Access to Customer Data

You can now use a self-service toggle in the Setup UI to opt out of allowing Salesforce to access
Customer Data in your org. Previously, opting out required customers to submit a support case.

Allowing access gives Salesforce consent to use Customer Data, as defined in our Main Services
Agreement (MSA), in your org for the following purposes:

•• Train global predictive AI models for use by the services and features to which you have access
• Improve the services and features to which you have access
   Conduct research into and development of new services and features

     Note Access to Customer Data is on by default unless you’re using Government Cloud or your
     organization has already decided not to share Customer Data with Salesforce.

If you turn off Salesforce access to Customer Data in your org:

• No new data is shared. Salesforce retains your collected data for up to 30 days, after which it’s deleted
• and can’t be recovered.
   No Salesforce employee will view your Customer Data outside of a support case, a pilot, or as
   otherwise described in your legal agreements.

Where: These changes apply to Lightning Experience in Enterprise, Performance, Unlimited, and
Developer Editions.

When: Consent management for data sharing is available starting February 4, 2026.

How: In Setup, go to Einstein Setup and turn on Einstein if it’s not already enabled. Go to Opt Out of
Customer Data Access and turn consent on or off.

purchased a subscription to Agentforce Voice Minutes. Contact your Account Executive for more details

Measure Agent Outcomes With Task Resolution

The Task Resolution metric, which scores agent outcomes for agents created with the new Agentforce
Builder, is generally available. Tune and improve your agent’s effectiveness based on knowing how well it
understands and resolves a user’s task. Deliver more meaningful outcomes that satisfy the user’s intent
as expressed in a given conversation.

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience in Enterprise, Performance, Unlimited, and
Developer editions with Foundations or Agentforce 1 editions. Setup for AI agents is available on the
desktop site.

When: The Task Resolution metric is available starting February 20th, 2026.

How: Confirm that Einstein Audit and Feedback is turned on in your org. If not, follow the instructions in
Set Up Einstein Generative AI Audit and Feedback. Then, build your agent using the new Agentforce
Builder (Beta). Once your agent is operational in a production or sandbox environment, outcomes are
automatically scored (Fully Resolved, Partially Resolved, and Unresolved) across all agent types. Scores
and accompanying explanations are streamed directly to a Data Model Object (DMO) in Data 360. Build
your own Data 360 dashboards and reports and run queries to spot trends, interpret results, and remedy
agent issues.

Deploy Agents to Slack Quickly with the Slack Connection

To connect an Agentforce Employee agent to Slack, simply add the Slack connection to it in the new
Agentforce Builder. The Slack connection also gives the agent context and structure that helps it craft
conversational messages specifically for Slack. Previously, you had to install the Slack connected app and
add it to the Messaging connection.

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience in Enterprise, Performance, Unlimited, and
Developer Editions with Foundations or Agentforce 1 Editions.

When: This change is available starting the week of March 9, 2026.

How: Before you get started, set up Einstein generative AI and enable Agentforce. Also, connect your
Salesforce organization to Slack.

To add the Slack connection to an Employee agent, open the agent in the new Agentforce Builder. On
the Explorer panel, click and then select Add Connection. On the Add Connections window, select
Slack and then click Add to Agent.

Deliver Emails in the New Agentforce Builder

You can now add the Service Email connection and the new Marketing Email connection to an
Agentforce Service agent in the new Agentforce Builder. The Service Email connection helps your agent
craft and deliver personalized emails with Email-to-Case, and the Marketing Email connection helps with

Messaging email channel.

  Article Answers for Einstein Bots now retires on September 30, 2026. Previously, retirement was

  enhanced bots to Generative Knowledge Answers.

  Bridge the data gap between your home orgs and Data Cloud One companion orgs. Previously,

Connect Your Companion Org Data to Agents via the Agentforce Data
Library

Bridge the data gap between your home orgs and Data Cloud One companion orgs. Previously,
connecting companion org data for an agent via an Agentforce Data Library required building a custom
retriever and performing significant manual setup. Now, we’ve automated the process to instantly
prepare your cross-org data for AI use.


    169

Salesforce Release Notes Agentforce Platform

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience in Enterprise, Performance, Unlimited, and
Developer editions with Foundations or Agentforce 1 editions. Setup for AI agents is available on the
desktop site.

When: This change is available in March 2026.

How: When you create and save a file or knowledge based data library in your companion org, the
system automatically generates all the necessary AI-ready assets in your home org. This includes data
streams, a data lake object, a data model object, a search index, and the retriever itself. The data library
status shows as Ready after the index is received in the companion org and the retriever is created.
Indexing typically takes around 20-25 minutes, depending on the volume of your data.

When the library is ready, AI agents operating in the companion org can immediately draw on data to
answer user questions and perform tasks. This feature only supports companion orgs linked to the
default data space.

See Also
  Salesforce Help: Create a Data Library

Einstein Development

Develop custom solutions with our suite of generative AI tools, including the Models API, Agentforce,
Prompt Builder, and Einstein Studio.

  Accelerate Custom Lightning Type Creation for Agentforce with the Lightning Types MCP Tool
  (Developer Preview)
  The Lightning Types Model Context Protocol (MCP) tool in the Salesforce DX MCP Server provides a
  dynamic way to create and enhance your custom Lightning types. Salesforce DX MCP Server uses large
  language models (LLMs) to generate the necessary LightningTypeBundle metadata files, including
  schema.json, editor.json, and renderer.json. You use these custom Lightning types to generate the
  custom Lightning Web Component (LWC) responses that you’re looking for. This feature supports
  Agentforce Employee agents in Lightning Experience and Agentforce Service agents via Enhanced Chat
  v2. You can also define structured outputs in Prompt Builder with these Lightning types.

Accelerate Custom Lightning Type Creation for Agentforce with the Lightning
Types MCP Tool (Developer Preview)

The Lightning Types Model Context Protocol (MCP) tool in the Salesforce DX MCP Server provides a
dynamic way to create and enhance your custom Lightning types. Salesforce DX MCP Server uses large
language models (LLMs) to generate the necessary LightningTypeBundle metadata files, including
schema.json, editor.json, and renderer.json. You use these custom Lightning types to generate the
custom Lightning Web Component (LWC) responses that you’re looking for. This feature supports
Agentforce Employee agents in Lightning Experience and Agentforce Service agents via Enhanced Chat
v2. You can also define structured outputs in Prompt Builder with these Lightning types.




    170

Salesforce Release Notes Agentforce Platform

(beta).

     Note The Lightning Types MCP tool feature is available as a developer preview. Feature isn’t
     generally available unless or until Salesforce announces its general availability in documentation or
     in press releases or public statements. All commands, parameters, and other features are subject to
     change or deprecation at any time, with or without notice. Don’t implement functionality developed
     with these commands or tools.

When: This feature is available starting the week of February 9, 2026.

How: Access the Lightning Types MCP tool, which works with your integrated development environment
(IDE), through Agentforce or other MCP clients of your choice. The Salesforce DX MCP Server is
preconfigured in Agentforce Vibes Extension. To interact with the tool, turn on the server in Agentforce,
which is a part of Agentforce Vibes Extension. After the server is running, interact with it by using natural
language prompts to create, enhance, and get guidance on your custom Lightning types.

Monitor Token Usage and Response Time in Prompt Builder

Understand how your prompt runs with the centralized Performance Insights panel. View generation
metrics such as response time, token usage, and masked values in one place while testing your prompt
templates.

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience in Enterprise, Performance, and Unlimited editions
with the Einstein for Sales, Einstein for Service, or Einstein Platform add-on.

When: This change is available starting the week of March 9, 2026.

Why: Use the panel to analyze latency, review total token usage (input and output), and see which fields
are masked before sending data to the model. You can also drill into metrics like response time to see a
breakdown of the steps contributing to overall generation time, including data retrieval, prompt
hydration, summarization, masking, and response generation. This visibility helps you optimize
performance and better estimate token-related costs.

How: In Prompt Builder, run Preview on a prompt template. Then open the Performance Insights panel
to Preview settings to view response time, token usage, and masked values. Click a metric to see a
detailed breakdown within the panel.



See Also
  Salesforce Help: Evaluate Prompts with Performance Insights

Structure Prompt Template Output with Custom Lightning Types

Define structured, predictable prompt responses by using custom Lightning types to control output fields
and data types.

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience in Enterprise, Performance, and Unlimited editions
with the Einstein for Platform, or Einstein/Agentforce add-ons.

When: This feature is available starting the week of January 5, 2026.

Why: Previously, configuring JSON responses without an output schema relied solely on prompt
instructions. Defining a custom schema guarantees that the output matches the required format,
enabling reliable integration with automated systems.

How: In Template Settings, select a response format. Create a custom Lightning type in the builder if the
one you need doesn’t exist. You can review the generated response in the selected format by clicking
Save & Preview.

Who: Available to users with the Prompt Template Manager permission set.

     Concierge Supports Multiple Semantic Models in Dashboards

Concierge Supports Multiple Semantic Models in Dashboards

In a Tableau Next dashboard with multiple semantic models, asking a questions in Concierge
semantically matches the user's utterance to the most suitable semantic model. When you are editing
the dashboard, you can search for data and metrics from multiple semantic models marked as ready for
use with Concierge.

This capability makes it possible for analysts to leverage multiple semantic models for a single agent
conversation. The agent handles the complexity of selecting the right model for each conversation turn,
creating a more fluid experience across different topics without manual intervention.

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience with Data Cloud. Tableau Next is available in
Enterprise, Performance, and Unlimited editions.

When: Available starting in February 2026.

How: In Tableau Next, create a dashboard with metrics and visualizations from multiple semantic data
models. In the dashboard, open Concierge (analytics agent) and ask questions.

 New Features for Data in Tableau Next

 Bring in data from any source and inspect it to ensure data integrity. Create a single source of truth for
 reliable, governed, reusable models, and streamlined data management.

  Scale Data Ingestion with Enhanced Large File Support
  You can now handle large-scale data imports more efficiently with increased file limits. The maximum


                        186

Salesforce Release Notes Analytics

  file size is now 2 GB with 100 columns for CSV files, and 100 MB with 500 columns for XLSX files.
  These expanded limits apply to file uploads from your local machine, enabling you to import massive
  and complex datasets without external data preparation tools.
  Boost Query Performance for External Data with Data Acceleration
  Improve the speed and reliability of external Data Lake Objects by using data caching to store
  frequently accessed information. Data acceleration acts as a high-speed local accelerator for federated
  data, copying it into a temporary cache to process it with minimal latency. Select between full or
  incremental refreshes to keep your data current and ready for high-demand querying.
  Get Your Data Connections with the Tableau Next Connector Catalog
  Create and manage your library of data connectors with the new Connector Catalog. This feature
  provides a view of all supported connectors, including Snowflake, and Google BigQuery, alongside
  their specific connection features. Easily identify which connectors have existing active connections
  and maintain a cleaner data environment.
  Locate Data Tables Quickly with Enhanced Connection Search
  Find specific schemas and tables within a data source by using keyword searches. Search results
  maintain their folder hierarchy and automatically expand parent schemas to provide immediate
  context for your data. This search capability eliminates manual scrolling in high-volume data
  environments and makes sure that you can access every available table instantly.
  Update Existing Data Lake Objects Directly in Your Workspace
  You can now manage data visibility and system speed in your workspace. This update supports actions
  such as reassigning data sources to different data spaces and renaming fields that align with business

Boost Query Performance for External Data with Data Acceleration

Improve the speed and reliability of external Data Lake Objects by using data caching to store frequently
accessed information. Data acceleration acts as a high-speed local accelerator for federated data,
copying it into a temporary cache to process it with minimal latency. Select between full or incremental
refreshes to keep your data current and ready for high-demand querying.

Where: This change applies to Tableau Next in Enterprise, Performance, and Unlimited editions.

How: Open an existing Data Connection in your workspace then select the source data to update. Click
Create Data Lake Object.



Click Edit to turn on acceleration. To cache data, select Full Refresh and select how often by using the
Frequency menu.

For an incremental refresh, select a date field in the Record Modified Field and frequency. Click Refresh
data now to start accelerating data. When you’re finished, click Update Acceleration.

New Features for Semantics in Tableau Next

Tableau Semantics, the the AI-powered semantic layer, maps your raw data to business-friendly terms
and logic, the key to building reusable models and metrics that provide contextual, consistent, trusted
insights.

  Refine Agent Accuracy with More Business Preferences
  You can now add up to 50 business preferences to your semantic model. This gives you more flexibility
  to define your organization's unique terminology and data logic. While this increase from 20 allows for
  more granular guidance, remember that preferences add tokens to the agent's prompt. Because larger
  prompts can increase response times, we recommend prioritizing concise, high-value instructions to
  minimize latency.
  Build and Navigate Complex Models With the Improved Semantic Builder Canvas

  incorrect logic or return Null. This change ensures data integrity and closer alignment with Data 360

Use New Behaviors in Some Tableau Semantics Functions

Now certain DATE functions, if given invalid input, return a query failure rather than attempt to fix
incorrect logic or return Null. This change ensures data integrity and closer alignment with Data 360 and
improves performance. Check existing content to see if you must take action.

Where: This change applies to Tableau Next in Enterprise, Performance, and Unlimited editions.

How: Calculations that use invalid functions can cause query failures. Review existing calculated fields to
prevent breaking changes. Make sure that they don’t rely on the "rounding" behavior of the date/time
function.

Updated Date Functions

•  MAKEDATE
    - Previously: Invalid input rounds to the nearest valid date, such as MAKEDATE(2025-03-32) returned
    2025-04-01
    - Now: Query failure


    192

Salesforce Release Notes                                             Analytics

•   MAKETIME
     - Previously: Invalid input rounds to the nearest valid time, such as MAKETIME(19, 4, 61) returned
         1899-12-30T19:05:01
•    - Now: Query failure
    DATE and DATETIME
     --  Previously: Invalid input returns Null
         Now: Query failure

See Also
    Salesforce Help: Calculated Field Formula Functions

Use New Behaviors in More Tableau Semantics Functions (Release Update)

Certain number functions (ASIN, POWER, ACOS, LOG, COT, and LN), if given invalid input, return a query
failure rather than return Null. In addition, Regex functions use the RE2 library rather than ICU. Check
existing content to see if you must take action to prevent breaking changes before these updates are
released.

Where: This change applies to Tableau Next in Enterprise, Performance, and Unlimited editions.

When: Salesforce enforces this update in March 2026. To get the major release upgrade date for your
instance, go to Trust Status, search for your instance, and click the maintenance tab.

Why: These changes ensure data integrity and improve performance.

How: Calculations that use invalid inputs cause query failures (number functions) or different handling of
certain regex functions. Review existing calculated fields to prevent breaking changes.

Updated number functions

•   ASIN, POWER, ACOS, LOG, COT, and LN
     --  Previously: Invalid input returns Null
         Now: Query failure

Updated regex functions

Empty string handling. The RE2 engine handles empty strings and "zero-width" matches differently than
the previous library. In RE2, an empty pattern is considered a match at every possible position (including
the start of the string).

                              Updated Regex Functions
   Calculation                Old Behavior (ICU)                 New Behavior (RE2)

   REGEXP_REPLACE('', '()',   '' (i.e. empty string)             'newstring'
   'newstring')

   REGEXP_REPLACE('', '',     '' (i.e. empty)                    'newstring'
   'newstring')


                              193

 Calculation                     Old Behavior (ICU)            New Behavior (RE2)

 REGEXP_REPLACE('tableau', '',   'tableau'                     'replacetableau'
 'replace')

 REGEXP_MATCH('string', '')      FALSE                         TRUE

Unsupported syntax

RE2 prioritizes speed and security by excluding features that require complex backtracking. If your
current calculated fields use the following syntax, they will need to be modified to not use the syntax in
this table.

                                     Unsupported Syntax
 Feature                         Unsupported Syntax Example    Description

 Backreferences                  (abc)\1                       Referencing a previously
                                                               captured group within the same
                                                               regex.

 Lookahead                       (?=...) or (?!...)            Checking if a pattern exists (or
                                                               doesn't) ahead of the current
                                                               position without "consuming"
                                                               characters.

 Lookbehind                      (?<=...) or (?<!...)          Checking if a pattern exists (or
                                                               doesn't) behind the current
                                                               position.

 Possessive Quantifiers          .*+ or [0-9]++                Quantifiers that do not allow the
                                                               engine to "backtrack" if a match
                                                               fails.

Concierge: Analytics Q&A Enhanced to Use Single Path for Questions

When you ask a question using Concierge anywhere in Tableau Next, the analytics agent will now route
all questions through the semantic query path to provide a single, consistent decision engine. This
change enables higher accuracy and reliability for all Concierge responses.

The semantic query path interacts with the underlying semantic model dynamically, allowing for custom
breakdowns, entity comparisons, and deeper exploration. Concierge generates and runs a semantic
query against the underlying semantic model. It synthesizes the query output data to create a textual
answer and creates a visualization based on the semantic query.

 Salesforce Release Notes Analytics

 • Boosts reliability with predictable behavior across all question types.
    Reduces latency for faster responses.
