New Features for Tableau Next Visualizations and Dashboards

Compose visualizations and dashboards with world-class analysis tools. Explore data and surface insights
that you can act on by building visualizations on related data in your workspace to draw conclusions and
make business decisions. Take data visualization to the next level with dashboards, where you can add
interactivity, enhance data exploration, and provide a clear overview of the critical information that you
need in one place.

  Navigate Levels of Detail Faster with Dimension Hierarchies


    198

Salesforce Release Notes Analytics

  Explore data in Tableau Next efficiently with dimension hierarchies to move between high-level
  summaries and detailed breakdowns. Define hierarchies on related dimensions or date fields from a
  single data object or across multiple data objects in a semantic model. And include the hierarchy in
  visualizations or tables to roll up or drill down analysis more easily.
  Manually Resize Table Columns for Better Readability
  Optimize your table layout in Tableau Next by manually resizing columns. Expand columns with more
  content to reduce horizontal scrolling. Or narrow columns to eliminate excess whitespace and improve
  readability. For example, widen columns that contain product descriptions so you can scan details
  more easily.
  Perform Deeper Analysis with Finer Time Granularity
  Uncover greater precision in analyzing data trends using hour, minute, and second levels from
  DateTime fields in Tableau Next. Analyze near real-time activity by using these fields in visualizations
  and tables to filter, sort, and aggregate data for deeper insights. Time values also appear in tooltips
  and on axes, making it easy to review exact timestamps. Previously, you could analyze time-based data
  only at the year, quarter, month, and day levels.
  Forecast Trends in More Chart Types
  Apply forecasting to any mark type in Tableau Next visualizations to review trends in your data. Select a
  forecasting model that best fits your data. Then compare projections for multiple segments of the
  same metric in a single chart or across related charts within one visualization. For greater control,
  decide how null values are handled and how much recent data to exclude, and preview changes
  dynamically to fine-tune results. Previously, you could apply forecasting only to line charts.
  Brand Your Tableau Next Dashboards with the New Image Widget

  recognizable and relatable for your stakeholders.
  Reuse Widgets Across Tableau Next Dashboards and Workspaces

  Find relevant assets with the new search bar and add them to your dashboard.

Perform Deeper Analysis with Finer Time Granularity

Uncover greater precision in analyzing data trends using hour, minute, and second levels from DateTime
fields in Tableau Next. Analyze near real-time activity by using these fields in visualizations and tables to
filter, sort, and aggregate data for deeper insights. Time values also appear in tooltips and on axes,
making it easy to review exact timestamps. Previously, you could analyze time-based data only at the
year, quarter, month, and day levels.

Where: This change applies to Tableau Next in Enterprise, Performance, and Unlimited editions.

Why: For example, view cases created by departments over time. Then drill to the hour level to pinpoint
periods of increased case activity.

How: To drill down by time unit, open a date field’s context menu in a visualization or table. Select a time
unit from Date Part or Date Value.

Forecast Trends in More Chart Types

Apply forecasting to any mark type in Tableau Next visualizations to review trends in your data. Select a
forecasting model that best fits your data. Then compare projections for multiple segments of the same
metric in a single chart or across related charts within one visualization. For greater control, decide how
null values are handled and how much recent data to exclude, and preview changes dynamically to fine-
tune results. Previously, you could apply forecasting only to line charts.

Where: This change applies to Tableau Next in Enterprise, Performance, and Unlimited editions.

Why: For example, review projected sales in a stacked bar chart by product category for upcoming
quarters. For comparison, include another stacked bar chart showing historical sales by category to see
how each category is expected to change over time.

How: On a chart with a Date Value field on Columns, drag the field you want to forecast onto Forecast in
the Analytics pane. To set the forecast parameters, click Forecast.

Lightning Reports and Dashboards

Save time and reduce errors when adding tables to dashboards by retaining existing report settings.
Ensure policy and regulatory compliance with custom disclaimers on exported reports.

  Use Existing Report Settings When Adding Tables to Dashboards (Generally Available)
  Save time and reduce manual configuration of report settings, such as groupings, custom formulas,
  and bucketing when adding lightning tables to dashboards. This feature reduces the risk of errors and
  ensures that the tables in the dashboard retain the same configuration as the report. This feature is
  now generally available.
  Ensure Compliance with Custom Disclaimers on Exported Reports
  Ensure that your exported reports meet corporate policies and regulatory requirements by appending
  a custom disclaimer after the standard Salesforce disclaimer.
  Share Reports and Dashboards Folders Using Usernames
  Securely share report and dashboard folders using precise usernames. Search for users by their
  usernames, and reduce the risk of sharing sensitive information with the wrong users. Previously, only
  the name was shown.
  Embed Custom Lightning Web Components in Dashboards for Interactive Data Views (Beta)
  Add custom Lightning Web Components (LWC) directly into Lightning Dashboards to create
  interactive, real-time data views that go beyond standard dashboard capabilities. Filter, explore, and
  act on data immediately without leaving your dashboard. For example, a business analyst can use a
  custom LWC to display a waterfall chart or other visualizations that are not available in standard
  dashboards.

  Salesforce Help: Share a Lightning Report or Dashboard Folder

Embed Custom Lightning Web Components in Dashboards for Interactive
Data Views (Beta)

Add custom Lightning Web Components (LWC) directly into Lightning Dashboards to create interactive,
real-time data views that go beyond standard dashboard capabilities. Filter, explore, and act on data
immediately without leaving your dashboard. For example, a business analyst can use a custom LWC to
display a waterfall chart or other visualizations that are not available in standard dashboards.

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience in Enterprise, Professional, and Unlimited editions.

     Note Embed Custom Lightning Web Components in Lightning Dashboards is a pilot or beta service
     that is subject to the Beta Services Terms at Agreements - Salesforce.com or a written Unified Pilot
     Agreement if executed by Customer, and applicable terms in the Product Terms Directory. Use of
     this pilot or beta service is at the Customer’s sole discretion.

How: To turn on this feature, contact Salesforce Customer Support. Then, in the dashboard edit mode,
click +Widget and select Lightning Web Component. Configure the properties of the custom Lightning
web component, and add the component to the dashboard.

See Also
  Salesforce Help: Add Custom Lightning Web Components to Lightning Dashboards (Beta)

Data 360 Reports and Dashboards

Calculate deeper insights with more row-level formulas.

  Expand Reporting Capabilities with More Row-Level Formulas
  Save time on reporting and generate deeper insights by including up to five row-level formulas in your
  Data 360 reports. Calculate values directly in the report without adding formula fields on an object.
  For example, calculate both the commission rate and the time-to-close metric in a single report
  without adding a formula field on the object. Previously, reports supported only one row-level formula.






    214

Salesforce Release Notes Analytics

Expand Reporting Capabilities with More Row-Level Formulas

Save time on reporting and generate deeper insights by including up to five row-level formulas in your
Data 360 reports. Calculate values directly in the report without adding formula fields on an object. For
example, calculate both the commission rate and the time-to-close metric in a single report without
adding a formula field on the object. Previously, reports supported only one row-level formula.

Where: This change applies to Data 360 in Developer, Enterprise, Performance, and Unlimited editions.

See Also
  Salesforce Help: Evaluate Each Record in Reports with Row-Level Formulas

CRM Analytics

CRM Analytics enhancements include new and updated features for dashboards, lenses, analytics apps,
and data integration.

  Analytics Experience and Visualizations
  Download Data 360 object data from lenses and widgets to CSV or Excel files. Take action across many
  assets with bulk actions. Query data more effectively with the new Data 360 SQL variant (beta).
  Analytics Data Integration
  Write and schedule your custom CRM Analytics recipes to output your transformed data directly to
  Data 360 data lake objects. Securely access your Amazon Redshift data by using a virtual private
  connection. Take advantage of OAuth functionality in your Microsoft Azure SQL Database connection.

Analytics Experience and Visualizations

Download Data 360 object data from lenses and widgets to CSV or Excel files. Take action across many
assets with bulk actions. Query data more effectively with the new Data 360 SQL variant (beta).

  Analyze Data Offline with CSV and Excel Exports of Data 360 Objects
  Export data directly from lenses and widgets that use data from Data 360 objects, such as data lake
  objects, data model objects, and calculated insights. Save up to 50,000 rows as an Excel or CSV file to
  use offline features, such as applying advanced filters, integrating with external tools, and performing
  complex calculations.
  Download CRM Analytics Dashboard Images
  Share insights faster by directly downloading an image of your CRM Analytics dashboard from the
  dashboard view. Previously, you had to use the Share window to download dashboard images.
  Manage CRM Analytics Assets with New Bulk Actions
  Minimize the risk of human error associated with repetitive manual tasks and manage multiple CRM
  Analytics assets efficiently with new bulk actions. You can now add or remove Favorites, and hide or
  show assets. You can perform bulk actions on up to 50 assets at a time. Previously, bulk actions were
  limited to Change Owner and Add to Collection.
  Speed Up Queries and Improve Data Handling with Data 360 SQL (Beta)


    215

Salesforce Release Notes Analytics

  Enhance data handling, strengthen security, and speed up query responses by using Data 360 SQL.
  New compact form queries and custom SQL queries now run on Data 360 SQL by default. Existing
  custom SQL queries continue to use legacy SQL, and you can manually switch them to Data 360 SQL
  for improved performance.
  Repeat Groupings in Compare Tables with Repeat Row Values
  You can now configure a compare table to replicate group dimension values on every row with Repeat
  Row Values. Tables with group dimensions, such as name or product, automatically repeat the group
  value on every row. This enhancement helps improve readability of large datasets without constant
  scrolling back to the first occurrence.
  Gain Full Control over Number Widget Tooltips
  You can now suppress tooltip bubbles on number widgets when a custom message isn't provided. This
  change allows for a more streamlined visual presentation, displaying tooltips only when they contain
  relevant information.
  Explore Pivot Tables with Expand and Collapse
  You can now expand and collapse groups and sub-groups in pivot tables to help you focus on specific
  insights and customize your view of large datasets.
  Keep Widget Action Menus Visible
  Keep important widget actions, such as downloading and sharing, always in sight for chart, number,
  text, repeater, list, toggle, date, range, and table widgets. Quickly access widget actions without
  needing to hover over the widget.

Analyze Data Offline with CSV and Excel Exports of Data 360 Objects

Export data directly from lenses and widgets that use data from Data 360 objects, such as data lake
objects, data model objects, and calculated insights. Save up to 50,000 rows as an Excel or CSV file to
use offline features, such as applying advanced filters, integrating with external tools, and performing
complex calculations.

Where: This change applies to CRM Analytics in Lightning Experience and Salesforce Classic. CRM
Analytics is available in Developer Edition and for an extra cost in Enterprise, Performance, and Unlimited
editions.

Who: To download Data 360 data as an Excel and CSV file, you need the Download CRM Analytics Data
permission.

How: Select a widget that contains data from a Data 360 object. From the widget’s action, click
Download. You can download the data in Excel, Excel with Metadata, or CSV format.

The Excel with metadata file includes the filters applied, groupings applied on columns, and count of
records.

You can now configure a compare table to replicate group dimension values on every row with Repeat
Row Values. Tables with group dimensions, such as name or product, automatically repeat the group
value on every row. This enhancement helps improve readability of large datasets without constant
scrolling back to the first occurrence.

Where: This change applies to CRM Analytics in Lightning Experience and Salesforce Classic. CRM
Analytics is available in Developer Edition and for an extra cost in Enterprise, Performance, and Unlimited
editions.

How: Create or edit a compare table on your dashboard. Click the Formatting icon and expand the
Layout section. Click Repeat Row Values.

Write and schedule your custom CRM Analytics recipes to output your transformed data directly to Data
360 data lake objects. Securely access your Amazon Redshift data by using a virtual private connection.
Take advantage of OAuth functionality in your Microsoft Azure SQL Database connection.

  Use CRM Analytics Datasets in Data 360 (Generally Available)
  Take advantage of the latest Data 360 features while retaining the functionality of CRM Analytics
  recipes. Write and schedule your custom CRM Analytics recipes to output your transformed data
  directly to Data 360 data lake objects (DLO). Then you can use your CRM Analytics data to create
  calculated insights, semantic models, and Data 360 reports and dashboards. This feature, now
  generally available, includes a change since the last release: Users can now select a category on the
  DLO.
  Securely Connect Your Private Redshift Data to CRM Analytics
  Integrate data from your private Amazon Redshift data warehouse into CRM Analytics. Use a virtual
  private connection (VPC) to make sure that all data transfer happens over an internal network,
  bypassing the public internet for enhanced security and compliance.
  Use OAuth Security with Your Microsoft Azure SQL Database Connection
  Increase data security by connecting to Microsoft Azure SQL Database using OAuth 2.0 authentication.
  You can now provide Azure authentication values directly, eliminating the need for a separate external
  authentication provider setup.
  Upgrade to OAuth Security for Your Salesforce External Connections
  Increase data security by using OAuth 2.0 authentication with your Salesforce external input and
  output connectors. The SOAP login() API isn't supported after v64. To maintain data sync, you
  must upgrade all existing Salesforce external connections to use OAuth before the Summer ‘26
  release.
  Control Access to Data Based on a User’s Assigned Territories (Generally Available)
  Allow users to see data in dashboards and insights only for the territories they’re assigned to in
  Territory Management 2.0. Reference the territory hierarchy from your dataset security predicates.
  Previously, you could only reference user data. This feature is now generally available.

  Actions (Beta)
  Decrease processing time when writing to Data 360 by overwriting existing Data Lake Objects (DLO)

  Accelerate Data Updates in Using Unique IDs for External Objects
  Now you can specify an external object field as a unique ID to function as a primary key for that

  records. For example, a nightly sync for a two-billion-row sales transaction object now processes only
  the 500,000 new or changed records instead of the entire dataset.

Use CRM Analytics Datasets in Data 360 (Generally Available)

Take advantage of the latest Data 360 features while retaining the functionality of CRM Analytics recipes.
Write and schedule your custom CRM Analytics recipes to output your transformed data directly to Data
360 data lake objects (DLO). Then you can use your CRM Analytics data to create calculated insights,
semantic models, and Data 360 reports and dashboards. This feature, now generally available, includes a
change since the last release: Users can now select a category on the DLO.

Where: This change applies to CRM Analytics in Lightning Experience and Salesforce Classic. CRM
Analytics and Data 360 are available for an extra cost in Enterprise, Performance, and Unlimited editions.

Why: For example, prevent churn with a DLO built from your transformed CRM Analytics recipe that
calculates a Churn Risk Score for each customer. Calculate the score from factors like case escalations
and declining purchases, and add it to the unified profile. Then, create a high-risk customer segment in
Data 360 to start a Marketing Cloud retention journey.

How: From Setup, in the Quick Find box, enter and select Analytics, then select Settings. Select
Enable CRM Analytics recipe to write output dataset to Data Cloud and then save your changes.

In Data Manager, in the recipe editor, specify Data Cloud as the Write To value in your output node.

Salesforce Release Notes Analytics

CSI Score (Beta)

Translate complex customer signals into unified, trusted scores to reduce departmental data silos. Gain a
unified view of business health by turning perception, behavioral, and operational signals into nine
composite scores that form one definitive CSI score. View overall business performance without
reconciling conflicting departmental reports. These scores reveal drivers of customer health, surface
emerging risks, and help leaders align teams to make outcome-driven decisions.

  Monitor Business Health with the CSI Score App
  Get instant visibility into customer health with prebuilt dashboards that accelerate time-to-value by
  delivering immediate, actionable insights. The app visualizes your composite scores, all-up CSI score,
  and predictive top drivers. Use KPI relationships to uncover exactly how individual KPIs drive changes
  in composite scores. Executives can focus on specific priorities by using the My Metrics tab, or evaluate
  comprehensive performance from the All Metrics tab. Leaders get a unified executive view while
  retaining the ability to drill down into the metrics driving performance.
  Simplify Score Analysis with AI-Powered Insights
  Understand the factors driving CSI score trends by using Insight Summary. This AI-generated summary
  provides an immediate explanation of the top two composite scores that impacted the all-up CSI
  score during a period. Powered by Tableau Next's Metric Insight Summaries, these insights provide
  clarity on how specific dimensions influence CSI scores to build company-level decision confidence.
  Analyze Customer Signals with an Impartial Scoring Framework
  Transform raw customer signals into actionable intelligence by using a tiered scoring framework.
  Rather than relying on simple averages, the framework standardizes diverse KPIs onto a common
  scale. Governed weighting prevents high-volume data from overpowering critical signals to maintain
  statistically sound scores. Leaders get an impartial baseline to evaluate business health without
  functional bias.
  Accelerate Time-to-Value with Guided CSI Score Setup
  Verify your org’s readiness and install CSI Score assets by using a guided setup checklist. Install all CSI
  Score assets including the CSI Score semantic model, Tableau Next dashboards, and the Lightning
  app. The process automatically installs and trains the predictive models with synthetic data. The app
  installation includes rules to conditionally update score calculations and weights based on data model
  objects (DMOs) mapped in Data 360.
  Customize CSI Score to Your Business Strategy
  Every business defines customer success differently. Serve these unique business requirements by
  cloning or extending the CSI Score semantic model. Map extra data model objects (DMOs) to include
  proprietary signals in the semantic layer. Modify calculated fields, adjust metric weights, and add KPIs
  to tailor composite scores and the all-up CSI score.
  Identify Top Score Drivers with Predictive AI Models
  Use predictive models to identify the top drivers for each composite score and remove guesswork. The
  models calculate Global SHAP (Shapley Additive Explanations) values to reveal which KPIs have the
  highest statistical leverage across your accounts. While initially trained on synthetic data, admins can
  retrain the models with company-specific data. Show executives cause-and-effect connections within
  your unique customer base.

  Get More Accurate Draft Flows with AI (Generally Available)
  Agentforce breaks down your business requirements into specific tasks and gives generative AI-specific
  instructions on how to complete those tasks, making your record-triggered or schedule-triggered flows

  instructions and then generate the draft flow.

  Improve and modify existing record-triggered and schedule-triggered flows by using natural language
  without starting from scratch. Use conversational prompts in the Agentforce panel to add, modify, and
  delete elements in a flow. This feature doesn’t consume generative AI credits.

  collapse and expand branching elements with Flow Builder, including Wait, Decision, Loop, Path
  Experiment, and Async Actions, helping you focus on the key parts of your flow. To ensure a consistent
  workflow, Flow Builder remembers your specific expand and collapse preferences. This layout is saved
  automatically and locally in your browser, making it easier to return to your work without changing the
  view for other users.
  Navigate Large Flows Faster by Collapsing or Expanding All Elements
  Collapse or expand all multiple-path elements, such as Wait, Decision, Loop, Path Experiment, and
  Async Actions, on the Flow Builder canvas with one click. This feature simplifies your view so that you
  can reduce visual clutter and focus on the important parts of the flow. You can still expand or collapse
  individual elements as needed. Flow Builder remembers your current layout automatically, even if you
  leave the flow. This layout saves locally in your browser, so you can pick up where you left off without
  changing the view for other users.
  Set Up the Agentforce Panel Without Admin Configuration

  summarizing, or evolving a flow. This feature doesn’t consume generative AI credits.

Get More Accurate Draft Flows with AI (Generally Available)

Agentforce breaks down your business requirements into specific tasks and gives generative AI-specific
instructions on how to complete those tasks, making your record-triggered or schedule-triggered flows
more accurate. Enter your instructions and let AI do the work. You can also use and modify the sample
instructions and then generate the draft flow.

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience in Essentials, Pro Suite, Professional, Enterprise,
Performance, Unlimited, and Developer editions with Foundations or Agentforce 1 editions. Verify
Agentforce 1 editions feature availability with your account executive.

This feature doesn’t consume generative AI credits. To learn more, see Agentforce and Generative AI
Usage and Billing.

How: Provision and enable Data 360 in your org. Then, turn on Einstein generative AI in Setup.

Create a flow in Flow Builder, and in the Let AI Help You Build section, click Get Started. Enter your
instructions and then click Draft with AI.

Evolve Flows Iteratively with Agentforce

Improve and modify existing record-triggered and schedule-triggered flows by using natural language
without starting from scratch. Use conversational prompts in the Agentforce panel to add, modify, and
delete elements in a flow. This feature doesn’t consume generative AI credits.

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience in Essentials, Pro Suite, Professional, Enterprise,
Performance, Unlimited, and Developer editions with Foundations or Agentforce 1 editions. Verify
Agentforce 1 editions feature availability with your account executive.

Who: Users with the Manage Flow permission or equivalent flow designer permissions who can create
and edit flows.

How: Provision and enable Data 360 in your org. Turn on Einstein generative AI in Setup. Then, open any
existing record-triggered or schedule-triggered flow in Flow Builder. Opt in to migrate to Agentforce, then
use the Agentforce panel to describe the modifications you want to make. For example:

•• “Add a decision element to check if the opportunity stage is Closed Won”.
• “Remove the loop element that processes inactive accounts”.
   “Add a fault path to handle errors in the Create Records element”.

Decision Logic Labels Were Updated for Clarity

The labels for the Decision Logic section of the Decision element were changed to Define Manually
(Default) and Define with AI (Advanced). The new labels clarify that defining conditions manually is the
first choice when working with structured data. When you can't define conditions because you're
working with complex or unstructured data, use AI.

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience in Enterprise, Performance, and Unlimited editions
with the Einstein for Sales, Einstein for Service, or Einstein Platform add-on. Einstein generative AI is
available in Lightning Experience. To purchase the Einstein for Sales, Einstein for Service, or Einstein
Platform add-on, contact your Salesforce account executive.

Screen Flow Updates

Sort and edit records in the Data Table component at runtime. Customize screen flows with component-
level style overrides. Add colorful, a11y-compliant text to your screens with the new Message
component. Streamline document-based screen flows with the File Preview component. Visualize and
track progress with the Kanban Board component (beta).

  Organize Data Table Records with Column Sorting at Runtime
  Enable users to organize their view of records directly in the flow screen. By clicking column headers,
  users can sort records alphabetically or numerically at runtime. Previously, the Data Table component
  displayed records in a fixed order, requiring users to scan manually to find what they needed.
  Edit Records Directly in the Data Table at Runtime
  Configure the Data Table component of a screen flow to support record editing at runtime. Previously
  read-only, the Data Table component now lets users modify values for specific field types. Confirmed
  changes are stored in the editedRows output parameter, making it easy to update records in
  Salesforce.
  Tailor Screen Flows to Your Audience with Component-Level Styling Overrides
  Deliver a personalized screen flow experience to your customers. Customize a variety of style
  properties for your screen flows, like background color, border color, border weight, border radius, text
  color, buttons, and more. Any styling changes you set override your org or Experience Cloud site’s
  default theme.
  Add Visually Distinct and Accessible Messages to Screen Flows
  With the new Message screen component, you can add an eye-catching a11y-compliant message to a
  screen to show information, a success, an error, or a warning.



    251

Salesforce Release Notes Automation

  Visualize and Track Record Progress with Kanban Boards in Screen Flows (Beta)
  Use the new Kanban Board component to show records as cards in columns that represent workflow
  stages, without custom Lightning implementations. Your users gain instant visibility into record
  progress and record details without leaving the flow. The Kanban Board is read-only, so users can’t drag
  cards between stages at run time.
  Preview Files Natively in Screen Flows
  Eliminate friction in document-based processes by enabling your users to review file content directly
  within a screen flow. The new File Preview screen component removes the requirement to download
  files externally, ensuring more streamlined document review and approval workflows.
  Find and Select Flow Resources More Easily in Screen Flows
  Flow Builder extends the enhanced resource selection experience to screen elements. For example,
  improved grouping makes it easier for you to find the resources that you need, user-friendly labels are
  shown instead of API names, tooltips with descriptions are available so you know more about what
  resource you’re selecting, and the search experience allows for nested searches with breadcrumbs to
  keep track of where you are.
  Open Screen Flows in Lightning Experience with a URL (Generally Available)
  Launch screen flows in Lightning Experience and Lightning console apps with a new standardized URL
  format. Opening flows in Lightning has several benefits, such as faster performance, keeping your
  users in Lightning console apps, and providing a more consistent browser experience. You can also
  pass information into your flow through its URL. The new URL format also supports the Salesforce
  Cosmos theme, and flow local actions.

Open Screen Flows in Lightning Experience with a URL (Generally Available)

Launch screen flows in Lightning Experience and Lightning console apps with a new standardized URL
format. Opening flows in Lightning has several benefits, such as faster performance, keeping your users
in Lightning console apps, and providing a more consistent browser experience. You can also pass
information into your flow through its URL. The new URL format also supports the Salesforce Cosmos
theme, and flow local actions.

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience in Essentials, Professional, Enterprise, Unlimited,
and Developer editions.

How: To open a flow in Lightning Experience, append /lightning/flow/YourFlowNameHere to your
URL. To run a specific flow version, append /lightning/flow/YourFlowNameHere/versionId to
your URL. Flows that open in Lightning Experience have improved performance because most required
Lightning components are already loaded into the browser session. In Lightning console apps, your tabs
are preserved when a flow opens, and you can switch to other tabs while the flow is working. Using the
new URL format also ensures that your browser behaves consistently, with forward, back, and your
browser history working as expected.

To pass data into a flow through its URL, append ?flow__variableIdHere=value to the end of your URL.
For example, to pass a case number into a flow, /lightning/flow/
YourFlowNameHere?flow__variableIdHereID={!Case.CaseNumber} .

Use & to append multiple variables into a flow. For example, /lightning/flow/
YourFlowNameHere?flow__varUserFirst={!$User.FirstName}&flow__varUserLast={!$User.LastName}
passes both the user first name and last name into the flow.

See Also
  Salesforce Help: Choosing Between Lightning and Non-Lightning Flow URL Formats
  Salesforce Help: Customize a Flow URL to Control Finish Behavior
  Salesforce Help: Send Variable Values to a Flow Using the Flow's URL

Flow Marketing Cloud Updates

Send Marketing Cloud Engagement emails in segment-triggered, event-triggered, activation-triggered,
and broadcast flows. Trigger automation event-triggered flows when records related to an individual are
changed. Get more control over schedule-triggered flows with more granular scheduling options. Use
contact point selection rules to make sure your messages get to the right person. Send email messages
using activation data.

  Automate Marketing Cloud Engagement Emails from Flow Builder
  Send Marketing Cloud Engagement emails via segment-triggered, event-triggered, activation-triggered,
  or broadcast flows. The Send Marketing Cloud Engagement Email action efficiently targets Data 360
  audience segments using your existing Marketing Cloud Engagement content and settings without
  requiring segment activation or data replication.
  Ensure Recipients Don’t Get Duplicate Messages
  Use contact point selection rules to send messages to the right individual record and a single
  messaging contact point. This update improves message precision. The update also enables flows to
  retrieve contact points from source systems, so that a contact point can be selected even if identity
  resolution or the data graph has not been refreshed.
  Send Email Messages Using Activation Data
  In activation-triggered flows, to include data from the activation in the Send Email Message action, use
  the $ActivationData variable in the email.
  Run Segment-Triggered Flows at The Right Time with More Scheduling Options
  Run segment-triggered flows on customizable schedules for more control and precision. For example,
  run a flow every hour to ensure you're working with the latest data, or schedule flows to run only on
  weekdays to avoid weekend sends. New scheduling options include Hourly, Daily on Weekdays,
  Weekly on specific days, Monthly on specific days, and Yearly.
  Get More Targeted Segments in Segment-Triggered Flows
  Create segment-triggered flows with segments built on Individual data model object (DMO) and
  engagement records, not just a Unified Individual DMO. For example, create a segment of all contacts
  converted yesterday. This update enables more precise targeting and provides access to engagement-
  specific data like order details or registration information.
  Test Multiple Records in Segment-Triggered Flows in Debug
  Test up to 10 records simultaneously. Use the debug panel to instantly verify how different customers
  move through your flow. This update helps you quickly identify issues across diverse customer profiles
  before activation.
  Trigger Automation Event-Triggered Flows When CRM Records Change
  Now you can trigger an automation event-triggered flow when a prospect, lead, or contact record
  changes, or when a record related to a prospect, lead, or contact record changes. For example, send a
  personalized email to a contact when a case is closed, or trigger a follow-up flow that notifies a lead
  owner when an opportunity moves to a new stage. This update helps you engage customers
  immediately when key business events occur, with prospect, lead, or contact data available for
  personalization in your messages.
  Stay Informed About Path Experiment Outcomes



    263

Salesforce Release Notes Automation

  Users who activate flows now receive automatic in-app notifications when path experiments are
  completed. Notifications cover winner selection, fallback handling, and inconclusive outcomes. This
  change keeps flow creators informed without requiring additional setup. If the activating user is
  deactivated, no notification is sent.
  View Path Comparison Analytics in Path Experiment Element
  Monitor path experiment results without leaving the Flow Builder canvas. The new Analytics tab in the
  Path Experiment element panel shows total participants, metrics, and confidence levels for path
  comparison. Monitor experiment results at a glance with this embedded summary, which is consistent
  with analytics available in other flow elements. To see in-depth analytics, click View Analytics.
  Control Path Selection When Debugging Path Experiments
  Configure the Path Experiment element to randomize path assignment or manually select a winning
  path while debugging. Randomization is the default, but you can validate specific paths without
  relying on chance by using manual selection. With the manual selection configuration, you can test
  the exact path you want to validate.
  View Path Experiment History
  Understand what happened during your path experiments with the new History tab. View all changes
  since activation, including timestamps, who made changes, and whether actions were automated or
  manual. Track events like experiment start, winner selection, delayed group releases, and fallback
  handling.
  Trace Individual Paths Through Flows with View Flow Run for Individual
  Troubleshoot specific customer issues by viewing the exact execution path that an individual took
  through a flow run. This capability shows you which branching paths were followed, what elements
  were completed, and where the individual potentially encountered errors or delays. This detailed view
  helps administrators investigate specific customer complaints, verify personalization logic, and identify
  bottlenecks for specific contacts in your marketing automation flows.
  Personalize and Debug On-Demand Flows with Apex
  Personalize on-demand flows with Apex code and control processing priority when triggering flows via
  API. Select specific individuals and contact points to target messages. Debug flows with built-in
  debugging tools to test logic and identify issues before activation. Access help documentation from
  the start node to understand configuration options and best practices. These updates provide more
  flexibility for customizing flow behavior and faster troubleshooting during development.
  Remove Individuals from Flows Externally via API
  Remove individuals from flows when external systems trigger exits via API. For example, exit
  customers from flows when they complete an order or when they reach a specified status. This update
  provides more flexibility to coordinate flow exits with external systems.

Send Mass Notifications or Wait for Events with Asynchronous Broadcast Flows

You can now set broadcast flows to run asynchronously. By running the flow asynchronously, you can
send notifications to larger audiences or to add Wait elements to the flow. That means you can resume
the flow after a certain event triggers, like if a customer opens an email.

Where: This change applies to Data 360 in Enterprise, Performance, Unlimited, and Developer editions.
Broadcast flows are also available for Marketing Cloud Growth and Marketing Cloud Advanced editions
with Data 360.

How: To run a broadcast flow asynchronously, in the Start element, select Async as the run type. With
asynchronous broadcast flows you can add Wait elements to the flow. If an asynchronous broadcast flow
is referenced in another flow through a subflow element, the asynchronous broadcast flow starts in a
separate transaction while the parent flow continues.

See Also
  Salesforce Help: Create a Broadcast Flow

Use Decisions, Add Exit Rules, and More with Enhancements to Activation-Triggered
Flows

In activation-triggered flows, you can now use the Decision element, add exit and reentry conditions,
pause an active flow, and in the Transform element, map activation data up to 5 levels deep.


    273

Salesforce Release Notes Automation

Where: This change applies to Data 360 in Enterprise, Performance, Unlimited, and Developer editions.
Activation-triggered flows are also available for Marketing Cloud Growth and Marketing Cloud Advanced
editions with Data 360.

How: To add exit rules and set reentry conditions, edit the flow’s Start element. You can reference the
$ActivationData system variable to set exit rules based on the activation. To set reentry conditions, select
a value for the Can Rejoin Flow field. Always is the default value and means an individual can reenter a
flow before they exit. After completion means individuals can enter a flow only after they exit it. Never
means that an individual can’t enter the flow again.

To pause an active flow, click the Pause button in the button bar. The button changes to a Resume
button when paused. When a flow is paused, processing stops at each element and its people and data
are held until you resume the flow. After you resume the flow, everything that was held is processed at
one time and then the flow continues as usual.

See Also
  Salesforce Help: Create an Activation-Triggered Flow

Assign Flow Tests to Specific Flow Versions for More Control

Reuse tests from previous flow versions if the scenario still applies to a new version. Align flow tests
precisely with each flow version so updates don’t cause incorrect results from other flow versions.

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience in Professional, Enterprise, Performance, Unlimited,
and Developer editions.

Why: Previously, a flow test applied only to the latest flow version. You deleted previous tests that didn’t
apply to the new flow version. For example, you deleted the flow test for flow version 1 after creating the
flow test for flow version 2. Starting in Spring ’26, you associate the same test with multiple flow versions.
Decide which test scenario is for which flow version. When you save a new flow version, the system
automatically includes tests from the source flow version.

How: From Flow Builder, open a record-triggered flow and create a flow test. Complete the test details.

Convert Speech to Text in Flow with the Speech To Text Action

Use the Convert Speech to Text flow action to transcribe audio files and make the resulting text available
within a flow. This action converts supported audio files into a transcript that can be referenced by
downstream flow elements, such as record updates or decision logic, helping incorporate spoken
information into automated processes.

Where: The Convert Speech to Text action is available in Flow Builder and can be added to any flow and
any topic where actions are supported, including autolaunched flows, record-triggered flows, and event-
triggered flows.

How: In Flow Builder, add an Action element to your flow. In the Action field, search for Convert
Speech to Text, and select the Convert Speech to Text action, and provide the Content Document
ID.

Flow and Process Release Updates

Salesforce Flow has several release updates that are scheduled to be enforced in future releases.

  Enforcing No-Argument Constructor on Apex Classes Used for Invocable Action Parameters
  (Release Update)
  When this update is enabled, you get access to certain built-in Apex classes that are available to be
  used as invocable action parameters. Additionally, this update enforces the visibility of the no-
  argument constructor on any class. This update was scheduled to be enforced in Summer ’26. Starting
  in Spring ’26, Salesforce no longer enforces this update, but we recommend that you enable it. This
  release update was previously named Enforce Permission Requirements Defined on Built-In Apex
  Classes Used as Inputs.
  Sort Apex Batch Action Results by Request Order (Release Update)
  With this update enabled, Apex batch action results are shown in the order that the requests are
  received. Currently, error-prone requests are prioritized at the top of the result list, and successful
  requests are at the bottom.

Enforcing No-Argument Constructor on Apex Classes Used for Invocable Action
Parameters (Release Update)

When this update is enabled, you get access to certain built-in Apex classes that are available to be used
as invocable action parameters. Additionally, this update enforces the visibility of the no-argument
constructor on any class. This update was scheduled to be enforced in Summer ’26. Starting in Spring
’26, Salesforce no longer enforces this update, but we recommend that you enable it. This release
update was previously named Enforce Permission Requirements Defined on Built-In Apex Classes Used
as Inputs.

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience and Salesforce Classic (not available in all orgs) in
Enterprise, Performance, Unlimited, and Developer editions.

When: This update was scheduled to be enforced in Summer ’26. Starting Spring ’26, Salesforce no
longer enforces this update.

How: When you enable this update, built-in Apex classes that were unavailable become available for
Apex actions. Because of this change, the visibility of the no-argument constructor for the
 invocableVariable Apex class is also enforced. Public no-argument constructors in managed
packages are no longer visible unless the access code is in the same package. An Apex action that refers
to a non-visible no-argument constructor invocableVariable Apex class results in errors.

From Setup, in the Quick Find box, enter Release Updates, and then select Release Updates. To get
the Enforcing No-Argument Constructor on Apex Classes Used for Invocable Action Parameters release
update, follow the testing and activation steps.

Sort Apex Batch Action Results by Request Order (Release Update)

With this update enabled, Apex batch action results are shown in the order that the requests are
received. Currently, error-prone requests are prioritized at the top of the result list, and successful
requests are at the bottom.

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience and Salesforce Classic in Enterprise, Performance,
Unlimited, and Developer editions.

When: Salesforce enforces this update in Summer ’26. To get the major release upgrade date for your
instance, go to Trust Status, search for your instance, and click the maintenance tab.

Why: Currently, error-prone requests are prioritized at the top of the result list, and successful requests
are at the bottom. With this change, action results are shown in the order that the requests are received.

How: After this update is applied, Apex batch action results are shown in the order that the requests are
received. Then, from Setup, in the Quick Find box, enter Release Updates, and then select Release
Updates. To get the Sort Apex Batch Action Results by Request Order release update, follow the testing
and activation steps.

Add Approval Submissions to Record Pages Without Custom Buttons

Add a component for your users to submit records for approval without you creating a custom button.
The Request Approval component works in both Lightning App Builder and Experience Builder.
Configure built-in options for approver selection and submission comments.

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience in Enterprise, Performance, Unlimited, all Einstein 1,
and Developer editions.

Who: To customize record page layouts in Lightning App Builder, you must have the Manage Flow user
permission. To customize an Experience Cloud site, you need to be a member of the site and have the
Create and Set Up Experiences user permission. Or you need to be a member of the site and an
experience admin, publisher, or builder in that site.

How: Before you add the Request Approval component to a record page layout, consider what input you
want from the submitter. If you plan to require that the submitter select an approver, design a flow
approval process to assign one or more approval steps to the firstApprover input variable. To expose
optional submitter comments to approvers, use the submissionComments input variable in your flow
approval process.

After you add the Request Approval component to a page, configure it to reference the relevant active
autolaunched flow approval process.

The component shows an Approval Request Comments field by default. To prevent the submitter from
adding comments about a submission, select Hide submitter comments.

To require the submitter to select a first approver, select Require submitter to select an approver.

Other Changes to Flow Approval Processes

Learn about improvements to Flow Approval Processes.

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience in Enterprise, Performance, Unlimited, all Einstein 1,
and Developer editions.

Why: Flow approval process designers can now:

• Provide input values and setup options one time per Flow Builder session instead of for every flow
   approval process debug run. Flow Builder preserves debug data such as triggering record inputs,
   debug options, and input variable values when you switch between Edit mode and Debug mode.
   Refreshing your browser or closing Flow Builder clears all debug settings. To clear debug settings
• manually, click Reset Debug Settings. Test input and test output that you set for steps aren't affected.
   Reduce email volume from approval work item notifications for individuals up the role hierarchy by
   using the new Send approval work item emails only to queue members setting. This approval setting
   limits notifications for queue-assigned approval steps to only queue members and their delegates. The
• setting has no effect if role hierarchy isn’t enabled.
   Use the Step panel’s Configure Test Output tab, previously known as Debug Configuration, to set test
   output values. The Manually Set Output Values option is now labeled Use Test Output. The new
   terminology reinforces that you’re specifying test values to use instead of running actual steps. All
• functionality remains the same.
   Place the Orchestration Work Guide, renamed from Flow Orchestration Work Guide, on the record
• page of an approval step’s related record in Experience Builder.
   Use the updated options in the Decision Logic section of the Decision element. See Decision Logic
   Labels Were Updated for Clarity.

  builds the flow directly on the Flow Builder canvas. This new creation approach speeds up the setup

  Use natural language to generate AI-powered MuleSoft for Flow: Integration flows that connect your
  org to external systems and then modify existing flows that use Agentforce. Agentforce dynamically
  generates new or evolves existing flows from simple text prompts. The prompts update the logic,
  mappings, or configurations flows in the Flow Builder side panel.

Enhance Data Exchange with Newly Added Third-Party Connectors

Use these newly added third-party connectors in flows for no-code connectivity to external systems and
to facilitate data and information exchange between different systems.

Where: This change applies to Salesforce Classic and Lightning Experience in Professional (with API
access add-on), Performance, Enterprise, Unlimited editions with the MuleSoft for Flow: Integration add-
on license and Agentforce 1 editions. Verify Agentforce 1 edition feature availability with your account
executive.

Who: To manage MuleSoft for Flow: Integration connections, you need the Manage Integration
Connections permission. For full access to flow types and features in Flow Builder—including Einstein and
Agentforce for Flow—the Manage Flow permission is required. To create and edit External System
Change-Triggered flows in the Automation app regardless of sharing settings, you need Manage Flow, or
the Create or Edit Flows and View Flows and View All Non-Admin Flows permissions. To create and edit
these flows when they are owned by or shared with you, you need the Create or Edit Flows and View
Flows permissions. To use MuleSoft for Flow: Integration templates, you need the Create or Edit Flows or
View Flows permission. Non-admins also need the App Framework Manage Template permission to use
these templates.

Extract Data from Digital and Scanned Documents by Using
MuleSoft for Flow: IDP (Generally Available)

Use MuleSoft for Flow: IDP to transform unstructured and semistructured data into structured,
actionable output, enabling automation of document-based workflows. Organizations get lots of
unstructured and semistructured documents that have important business data. But getting and
processing this information by hand is time-consuming and can introduce mistakes. With MuleSoft for
Flow: IDP, you define what data to extract through custom configurations. You set confidence thresholds
for automatic processing, and route low-confidence results for human review to verify accuracy. Manage
your document processing configurations on the Document Processing tab in the Automation app.

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience and Salesforce Classic in Professional (with API
access add-on), Performance, Enterprise, and Unlimited editions. Edit or delete Document processing
configurations in the Automation app. This feature is available with the MuleSoft for Flow: IDP add-on
license.

How: Define the data fields and tables you want to extract from documents by creating a document
processing configuration in the Automation app. Build the human review workflow by creating an
orchestration that routes documents with low confidence scores to a screen flow for a user to manually
review and continue the process. To process uploaded documents in Salesforce, add an Extract Data
from Document action to a flow or an orchestration and select the Document ID and Document
Processing Configuration to reference.

   26.4 Release

   The B2C Commerce 26.4 release occurs between March 24 and April 23, 2026.

    Catch System Security Issues Early with Anomaly Detection
    Identify performance regressions and security anomalies (such as error spikes or failed logins) earlier
    by running an Anomaly Detection log. Previously, detecting issues required manual investigation. Now,
    the system analyzes log patterns and shows anomalies in real time.
    Capture Customer and Order Search Queries in Security Logs
    Capture information about user-initiated search queries from Business Manager or via APIs for
    customer and order data. The log lists the user name, search parameters, and timestamp.
    Find Products by Using the Product Name
    Search for items in your product list without having to remember product IDs. In addition to the



    308

Salesforce Release Notes Commerce

  product ID, you can now enter product names in the enhanced search bar in Business Manager.
  Search supports locale-specific names, so make sure that you have the correct locale selected in
  Business Manager.
  Monitor Product Readiness in the Product List View
  Quickly check that your products are storefront-ready by viewing their status in the product list. The
  new Readiness column tracks key attributes, such as image availability, inventory, and pricing, for each
  product across locales and consolidates them into a single visual indicator. The Readiness badge
  shows the number of completed attributes for each product. Hover over the badge to see which
  attributes are present or missing.
  View Price and Inventory Data in the Product List
  Monitor your product stock levels and pricing strategies without leaving the product list. Add the new
  Price, Per Unit Price, and Available to Sell (ATS) columns to get a comprehensive view of your product
  data across locales. These columns provide the best price and real-time inventory quantities (OCI or
  native). For products using perpetual inventory, the ATS column displays Perpetual. The column values
  are based on your selected locale in Business Manager.
  Price Attribute Search Returns More Precise Results
  Shoppers now get more accurate search results with price filtering. For example, the search process
  can filter for quantitative ranges, such as “dress under $100.” This feature works with existing keyword
  search capabilities.
  Prioritize Exact Matches in Search Results
  Deliver more relevant search results by weighting a customer’s search query term higher than the
  term’s defined synonyms. Previously, search queries treated all terms in a synonym group with equal
  weight, often causing products that contained the synonym term to outrank products that actually
  matched the customer’s search query. By boosting the search query term, customers find exactly what
  they asked for first while still discovering similar, interchangeable products lower in the results.
  Improve Japanese Product Discoverability with Enhanced Tokenization
  Deliver more predictable search results for Japanese storefronts with an improved word-breaking
  algorithm. The search engine now breaks down Japanese text into tokens, resulting in higher relevancy
  when customers search for products with complex phrases or compound words.
  Visually Enhance Your Business Manager with the New Cosmos UI
  The new Salesforce Cosmos Design includes interactive circular motifs, improved fonts and icons,
  inviting cues, and higher contrast colors. You can switch to the new UI or continue to use the earlier UI
  styles.
  Use the Enhanced Proxy Zone Framework
  To improve security and performance, all deprecated proxy V1 zones are now migrated to the V2 zone
  configuration. This update enhances reliability for ghost routing and traffic splitting. Manage all
  custom hostnames under the more efficient V2 framework. If your site still uses legacy zones, migrate
  them to proxy zones.
  Control Center Audit Logs Are Now in Log Center
  You can no longer access in-app audit logs from Control Center, and the Audit Logs button has been
  removed. Instead, use the advanced filtering and long-term storage capabilities of Log Center to track
  configuration changes and user activity. To view your audit data, go to Log Center and filter by the
  Control Center category.

Prioritize Exact Matches in Search Results

Deliver more relevant search results by weighting a customer’s search query term higher than the term’s
defined synonyms. Previously, search queries treated all terms in a synonym group with equal weight,
often causing products that contained the synonym term to outrank products that actually matched the
customer’s search query. By boosting the search query term, customers find exactly what they asked for
first while still discovering similar, interchangeable products lower in the results.

Where: This change applies to B2C Commerce.

How: To enable this feature, contact Salesforce Customer Support.

algorithm. The search engine now breaks down Japanese text into tokens, resulting in higher relevancy
when customers search for products with complex phrases or compound words.

26.3 Release

The B2C Commerce 26.3 release occurs between February 24 and March 26, 2026.

   Guide Shoppers to the Right Products by Prioritizing Question Sequences
   Refine how your agent interacts with a shopper by prioritizing the sequence of questions during the
   product discovery process. You can tailor the sequence for each product type to have the agent ask
   the most-relevant questions and capture the most business-critical product attributes first.
   Preserve Shopper Preferences Across Categories
   Make it easier for shoppers to discover products by preserving their preferences as they search across
   categories. When a shopper switches to a new category or a previous one, the agent retains their



    314

Salesforce Release Notes Commerce

  preferences and proactively prompts to reapply the category. Previously, shoppers needed to reselect
  filters manually every time they switched to a different category.
  Search Products for Price and Availability
  Find products in your catalog that are missing prices or out of stock by using the new Price and
  Inventory filters in Advanced Search. You can also search for products that have prices or are in stock.
  Keep Your Sales Flowing Seamlessly with Omnichannel Inventory Resilience
  Ensure order continuity by capturing orders using the last-known inventory levels if connectivity to
  Omnichannel Inventory is lost. After the connection is restored, the new Continuous Order Capture
  option pauses order exports to Salesforce Order Management and reconciles pending reservations.
  Replicate Only the Price Books That You Need
  Reduce system load and update pricing for specific sites faster by replicating individual price books.
  You can replicate up to 25 price books at a time.
  Simplify Testing with a Default Domain (Generally Available)
  Accelerate time to market by using a preconfigured, Salesforce-managed default hostname for testing
  in development, staging, and production environments. The default domain, which is provisioned
  when you create a realm, has embedded CDN capabilities, eliminating the need to manually configure

Accelerate time to market by using a preconfigured, Salesforce-managed default hostname for testing in
development, staging, and production environments. The default domain, which is provisioned when
you create a realm, has embedded CDN capabilities, eliminating the need to manually configure DNS
settings. To maintain security, development and staging instances require user credentials. Production
instances have a Block All firewall rule applied by default. Configure Allow rules to grant access.

     causes issues with Page Designer and Preview functions. To ensure these functions work as

     Agents in the Default zone.

Reuse Content Across Page Designer Pages with Content Asset Binding

Bind component attributes to content asset attributes to reuse content across multiple pages and update
it from a single location.

Where: This change applies to B2C Commerce.

How: In Business Manager, select Administration | Global Preferences | Feature Switches. Turn on
Enable Page Designer Data Binding. Then, in Page Designer, select a component and click Select
Content Asset in the right pane. Choose a content asset and bind its attributes to the component. When
you update the content asset, the changes appear automatically on every page that uses it.

 Salesforce Help: Binding Components to Content Assets (can be outdated or unavailable during

Control Content Eligibility with eCDN Cache Rules

Customize caching eligibility for your content beyond default file extensions by using eCDN cache rules.
Cache rules allow resources like HTML, JSON, and XML to become eligible for caching based on specific
request attributes. By defining rules for URI paths, cookies, and headers, you improve cache hit ratios
and enable advanced cache purging capabilities.

Where: This change applies to B2C Commerce.


 319

Salesforce Release Notes                                                                     Commerce

How: Define cache rules by using the CDN Zones API to match specific GET requests based on host
names, paths, or HTTP headers. Ensure your origin server sends appropriate Cache-Control headers,
such as public with a max-age greater than zero, as these rules make content eligible for caching but
don’t override origin headers.

See Also
   Salesforce Developers: eCDN Cache Rules

Refine a Product Search While Chatting with the Shopping Agent

Shoppers can discover the most suitable product with the help of the Shopping Agent. If a shopper
wants to see more options, a list with multiple filters becomes available to refine the search, without
losing the context of their conversation.

Where: This change applies to B2C Commerce.

When: This functionality is available March 24, 2026.

Who: This feature is available to customers with a B2C Commerce Cloud license and the Agentforce add-
on.

How: After the agent gives a shopper some product suggestions, the agent asks a follow-up question
and suggests responses. If there are other suggestions, shoppers can select See More to view a page
with those options. The shopper selects the most suitable, and the agent repeats the search using these
refinements. This functionality is available by default. No configuration is necessary.

Commerce Search

Know immediately when a product is at risk of being unsearchable. Allocate resources strategically for
larger, more complex product catalogs with an increased searchable and filterable field limit.

  Product Catalogs Include More Searchable and Filterable Fields
  Previously, the search index was limited to 25 searchable fields and 50 filterable fields. Now, you can
  have a total of 100 searchable and filterable fields, enabling you to allocate resources strategically for
  larger, more complex product catalogs.
  Accelerate Conversions with Predictive Product Suggestions
  Help buyers find relevant products faster by showing bestsellers and suggestions. Bestselling products
  appear before a buyer begins typing in the search bar. Suggested products appear when a buyer
  enters at least three characters. Previously, predictive product suggestions were available only in D2C
  stores. Now, they’re also available in B2B stores.

 Determine Product Visibility Dynamically by Using Qualification Rules
 To evaluate product and product category eligibility, your B2B Commerce store applies entitlement
 policies that you’ve configured. However, if you have thousands of products, preconfiguring
 entitlement policies can get challenging. To make it easier to manage large numbers of products and
 product categories across your stores, create qualification rules that dynamically evaluate eligibility
 based on account or category attributes. You can also set up a disqualification rule to exclude
 products and product categories from a buyer’s view. If you enable qualification rules, your store uses
 qualification rules instead of entitlement policies.

  Enforce Regional Cash Limits at Checkout
  Restrict the amount of cash accepted during a sale. Updated CMS settings help your stores comply
  with local regulations by blocking cash tenders that exceed your defined threshold. The Modern POS
  app prompts associates to collect the balances that exceed the threshold via other payment methods
  and prohibits manager overrides to ensure strict compliance.
  Improve Commission Accuracy with Advanced Attribution Settings
  Control multiassociate tagging policies for sales attribution with updated CMS settings. Your associates
  can now manually distribute sales credit in different percentages to any sales associate. These settings
  replace rigid equal-split defaults, giving you more control over tracking and reporting sales
  performance.
  Support Multitender Flows for In-Store Pay by Link
  The in-store pay by link workflow now supports multitender scenarios. The workflow also verifies that
  the entire order amount is paid before returning an approved status to store associates. The system
  now validates that the sum of all payments equals the full order total before finalizing the sale.
  Previously, the POS app incorrectly treated a partial payment as a completed transaction and
  immediately showed the confirmation page.

  Manage Mixed Ownership Stores with Franchise Management
  Link your stores to franchise groups for organized corporate and franchise store management. This
  setup helps you support mixed ownership models and manage both store types within the same retail
  environment.
  Prevent Store Closure Failures with Time Zone Checks
  Keep your store operations running smoothly by requiring time zone consistency between your POS
  devices and store location. If the device time zone doesn’t match your store’s time zone you can now
  block device logins. Previously, cross-time zone logins created business data mismatches that
  permanently blocked daily store closures and disrupted operations.
  Process Fulfillment Orders in Bulk with Wave Picking
  Process up to 10 orders in a single trip by grouping product quantities across multiple orders into one
  picklist. Instead of picking items order by order, you can pick everything at once, reduce store travel
  time, and help high-volume stores stay on schedule.
  Prioritize Orders and Reduce Late Fulfillments
  Get the visibility you need to handle pickup and shipping orders in the right order. The POS app now
  highlights time-sensitive orders in the fulfillment list. A green indicator shows that an order is on track,
  an orange indicator shows that it’s nearing the deadline, and a red indicator shows that the deadline
  has passed.
  Simplify Transactions with Calculation-Driven Rounding for All Currencies
  Process cash payments and international orders compliantly. Salesforce POS supports calculation-
  driven rounding for zero and two-decimal currencies recognized by the International Organization for
  Standardization 4217. Rounding rules apply at the final sales calculation step, ensuring precise
  transaction totals and consistent sales and tax reports.

    Prioritize Orders and Reduce Late Fulfillments

    Get the visibility you need to handle pickup and shipping orders in the right order. The POS app now
    highlights time-sensitive orders in the fulfillment list. A green indicator shows that an order is on track, an
    orange indicator shows that it’s nearing the deadline, and a red indicator shows that the deadline has
    passed.

    Where: This change applies to Salesforce Point of Sale.

    How: In CMS, go to Store Management | Store Settings | Store Fulfillment. Enter a value for the Pickup
    SLA Threshold field. For example, if the pickup deadline is 24 hours and the threshold is 80, the order is
    marked with an orange indicator after 19 hours and 12 minutes.

Simplify Transactions with Calculation-Driven Rounding for All Currencies

Process cash payments and international orders compliantly. Salesforce POS supports calculation-driven
rounding for zero and two-decimal currencies recognized by the International Organization for
Standardization 4217. Rounding rules apply at the final sales calculation step, ensuring precise
transaction totals and consistent sales and tax reports.

Where: This change applies to Salesforce Point of Sale.

How: In CMS, go to Store Management | Store Settings | System and set the Number of Decimals
Supported by Currency. Save your changes.

Setup with Agentforce (Beta)

Simplify administrative tasks by using the new AI-powered agent in Setup.

     Note Setup with Agentforce is a pilot or beta service that is subject to the Beta Services Terms at
     Agreements - Salesforce.com or a written Unified Pilot Agreement, if executed by Customer, and the
     Non-GA Credit Consumption term in the Product Terms Directory. Enabling this pilot or beta service
     consumes Data 360 credits and is at the Customer's sole discretion.

  Streamline Administrative Tasks with Setup with Agentforce (Beta)
  Salesforce’s new agent-driven Setup experience integrates Setup with an AI assistant to simplify
  administrative tasks. Chat with the agent to issue commands or ask questions by using natural
  language. The agent makes activities like creating objects and flows, managing user access, and
  troubleshooting formulas more intuitive and efficient, reducing navigation and clicks.
  Chat with the Setup Agent in More Languages (Beta)
  Setup with Agentforce now has beta support for Catalan, Danish, Dutch, Finnish, French, German,
  Italian, Japanese, Norwegian, Portuguese, Spanish, and Swedish. Previously, only English was
  supported.
  Open Setup Pages in a Dedicated Tab (Beta)
  In Salesforce orgs that have enabled Setup with Agentforce, Setup pages open in a single dedicated
  tab instead of overwriting the Setup Home page. Now you can context switch between Home, agent
  conversations, and Setup pages without losing work.
  Updated Permission Requirements for Setup with Agentforce (Beta)
  Previously, you were required to assign users the Execute Prompt Templates user permission to allow
  access to the Setup agent. Now, you can assign users either the Execute Prompt Templates or
  Customize Application user permission. Alternatively, in place of the Execute Prompt Templates
  permission, you can assign the Prompt Template User standard permission set. The Use Setup with
  Agentforce user permission remains required as before.
  Get Enhanced Conversation Recommendations in Setup with Agentforce (Beta)
  Use engagement insights to improve search recommendations and agentic conversations for selected


                        351

Salesforce Release Notes Customization

  users in Setup with Agentforce (Beta). When enabled, this feature uses Data 360 to collect and process
  page views, record changes, and other user run-time data for a more personalized Setup with
  Agentforce experience.
  Get Information About Key Org Health and Usage Metrics with Setup with Agentforce (Beta)
  The Org Health and Usage dashboard now has even more information about your org's health and
  performance metrics. Use this dashboard to track your org's Security Health Check score, get an
  overview of your Apex health, and review login errors.
  Quickly Create a Salesforce Mobile App and Pages in Setup with Agentforce (Pilot)
  Agentforce builds custom mobile apps and home pages tailored to your specific roles, data, and
  components. After analyzing your workflow, it proposes a structured plan and executes the build once
  you approve the design.
  Open Newly Created Flows in Flow Builder from Setup with Agentforce (Beta)
  Transition smoothly from conversational, AI-generated flow creation to fine-tuning the results. After
  you create a flow in Setup with Agentforce, use the new links to open it directly in Flow Builder for
  review and modification. The links remain available as long as the tab where Agentforce created the
  flow is open.
  Troubleshoot Access Using the Setup Audit Trail (Beta)
  Find out why a user lost or gained access with the Setup agent. The Setup agent now answers
  questions such as “Why can’t Erica Douglass manage users anymore? What changed?” by reviewing
  recent changes in the Setup Audit Trail. The agent looks at Setup Audit Trail updates related to
  permission sets, permissions set groups, profiles, roles, user access policies, organization-wide
  defaults, and user records when determining the reason.
  Build Data Models Faster with Data Model Management Enhancements (Beta)
  With data model management you can use a conversation-centric UI to create custom objects, fields,
  and relationships. There are a number of enhancements to data model management in Setup with
  Agentforce. When you work with objects and fields, you can now include Percent and Currency field
  types. This update includes a tabular format for fields and a summary explanation of the action output
  to improve data visibility. You can also independently update object and field labels and API names for
  more flexibility during the customization process. Finally, we added linking for existing objects and
  fields so you can view their details in Object Manager.
  Explore Setup with Agentforce Capabilities (Beta)
  Learn what tasks the Setup agent can help with right from the source. You can get an overall summary
  of the Setup agent’s capabilities or information about a specific area. For example, ask, “What can you
  do?” or “What can you do related to user access management?”
  Manage Queues with Setup with Agentforce (Beta)
  You can now create and manage queues through a conversation with the Setup agent, rather than
  navigating to multiple Setup pages. When making updates, you can modify queue details such as its
  name, support emails, supported objects, and routing configurations. For easier management, you
  can also ask the Setup agent for a list of all queues and public groups.
  Use Both API Names and Labels to Reference Features (Beta)
  You can now generate flow summaries and reference formulas, permission sets, and other features in
  Setup with Agentforce using either their API name or label. The generated flow summary references
  the precise API names of objects and fields that the flow interacts with. Using the API names allows


    352

Salesforce Release Notes Customization

  you to easily find what you’re looking for and to avoid ambiguity when multiple features and flows
  have similar labels.
  Reference Users with More Flexibility in Setup with Agentforce (Beta)
  When you chat with the Setup agent, you can now reference or locate users with their email,
  username, first name, last name, and role.
  Troubleshoot External Client App Access in Setup with Agentforce (Beta)
  To resolve access issues more efficiently, the Setup agent can help you determine whether a user has
  access to an external client app (ECA) through a permission set or profile. Ask the agent a question
  such as, “Can you check whether Kathy Cooper has access to external client application Example
  Integration?”

Streamline Administrative Tasks with Setup with Agentforce (Beta)

Salesforce’s new agent-driven Setup experience integrates Setup with an AI assistant to simplify
administrative tasks. Chat with the agent to issue commands or ask questions by using natural language.
The agent makes activities like creating objects and flows, managing user access, and troubleshooting
formulas more intuitive and efficient, reducing navigation and clicks.

Where: This feature is available in Lightning Experience in Enterprise, Performance, Unlimited, and
Developer editions with Foundations or Agentforce 1 editions.

     Note Setup with Agentforce is a pilot or beta service that is subject to the Beta Services Terms at
     Agreements - Salesforce.com or a written Unified Pilot Agreement, if executed by Customer, and the
     Non-GA Credit Consumption term in the Product Terms Directory. Enabling this pilot or beta service
     consumes Data 360 credits and is at the Customer's sole discretion.

When: This feature is available starting in early January 2026.

Who: To use Setup with Agentforce, users must have these permissions: Use Setup with Agentforce and
Execute Prompt Template. Users must also have access to the Data 360 default data space and the
required permissions for the task they want to perform.

Why: Setup with Agentforce is available from every page in Setup. You can chat with the agent in the
Agentforce panel while still viewing and navigating through Setup. And when necessary, the conversation
can transition into a full-sized agentic experience that opens new conversations in different console tabs
and includes a canvas to display rich content such as record details, list views, and metadata previews.
