Export and Import Translated Files with Ease

Reduce metadata translation file size and complexity with export filters. Now, you can filter metadata
translation files for export from the Translation Workbench when you select metadata components and
date ranges. To improve the import experience, when you import translated files that contain invalid
records, the valid records are imported.

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience and Salesforce Classic in all editions.

Who: To export metadata files from the Translation Workbench, admins and developers need the
Manage Translation and Create Documents permissions.

Why: Filtering provides granular control, helps create smaller, more efficient translation packages, and
you can create highly precise translation files. For example, you can limit the export to only records
modified since a specific date. Or, you can focus on recently changed items when you define a date
range based on the source’s last modified date.

When you import translated files that contain invalid records, the valid records are imported. All errors
are reported and the error report is a link to a .zip archive. Previously, only up to 50 errors were reported,
there was complete failure or success, and the error report was available as an email attachment.

How: To create files for your translators that contain your Salesforce org’s translatable metadata, from
Setup, in the Quick Find box, enter Export, and then select Export. If data translation is enabled, select
the Metadata translation type. Then filter by Salesforce Setup components or by modification date.

Enable ICU Locale Formats (Release Update)

With this update, the International Components for Unicode (ICU) locale formats replace Oracle’s Java
Development Kit (JDK) locale formats in Salesforce. Locales control the format for dates, times,
currencies, addresses, names, numeric values, and the start day of the week. ICU sets the international
standard for these formats. The ICU locale formats provide a consistent experience across the platform
and improve integration with ICU-compliant applications across the globe. This update was first made
available in Winter ’20. Orgs that haven’t already switched to ICU locale formats are encouraged to
manually update.

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience, Salesforce Classic, and all versions of the Salesforce
mobile app in all editions, except Database.com.

When: To get the major release upgrade date for your instance, go to Trust Status, search for your
instance, and then click the maintenance tab.

Who: You can enable this update for all orgs. To use the ICU locale formats in your customizations, all
Apex classes, Apex triggers, and Visualforce pages must use API version 45.0 or later.

How: To manually enable this update, from Setup, in the Quick Find box, enter Release Updates, and
then select Release Updates. To Enable ICU Locale Formats, follow the testing and activation steps.

The English (Canada) locale (en_CA) requires separate activation. From Setup, in the Quick Find box,
enter User Interface, and select User Interface. Then select Enable ICU formats for en_CA, and save
your changes.

To confirm whether your org is using ICU or JDK locale formats, from Setup, enter Company
Information in the Quick Find box. On the Company Information page, locate the Locale Formats field.

The enablement of this release update is not enforced in Spring '26. If your org is already using ICU
locale formats, those locale formats remain enabled. For any org still using JDK, we recommend that they
use the release update to manually enable ICU locale formats.

List Views

When you sort a list view, blank fields are sorted as the highest value in the list instead of the lowest
value. In list views rendered with Lightning Web Components (LWC), you receive an error notification
earlier in the edit process if you try to edit more than 200 records at a time.

  List View Edit Limits Are Communicated More Clearly
  List views rendered with Lightning Web Components (LWC) now prevent you from selecting or
  attempting to edit more than the supported maximum of 200 records at one time. Previously, if you
  selected more than 200 records, the edit icon still appeared and Salesforce didn’t restrict you from
  changing a field. However, when you attempted to apply your changes, an error notified you that your
  changes were unsaveable. To save you time and prevent the input of changes that can’t be saved, list
  views now enforce the 200-record limit earlier in the edit process.
  Use Updated Empty Value Placement in List View Sorting
  When you sort a list view, blank fields, or null values, now are treated as the highest value in the
  dataset. For example, let’s say you have a column with the data 5, 9, null, and 2. If you sort this column
  in ascending order, you see 2, 5, 9, null. Previously, Salesforce treated blank fields as the lowest value,
  so that in the example given, you saw the data as null, 2, 5, 9.

  Connect to Snowflake on Azure with Private Connect
  Private Connect establishes a direct and secure network path between your Data 360 tenant and
  private Snowflake or Databricks instances on Azure. This connection bypasses the public internet,
  making sure that you access your data lake without opening any non-private network paths.
  Ingest Helpjuice Knowledge Articles into Data 360

  can then access your Adobe content for more informed responses, better customer insights, and
  enhanced project visibility.

  Connector (Generally Available)
  Ingest unstructured documents from Microsoft SharePoint directly into Data 360 to power AI and
  search experiences. With the Microsoft SharePoint Unstructured (Documents) connector, you can
  transform your SharePoint repository into an AI-ready knowledge base. This feature is now generally
  available.
  Re-enable a Disabled Salesforce CRM Connector Data stream Field
  Resume data ingestion for a previously disabled field in a Salesforce CRM data stream. If a field
  becomes relevant again, you can re-enable it without creating a new data stream.
  Confirm Salesforce CRM Connection Changes for Enhanced Security
  Enhance security by confirming your intent when you reauthenticate or disconnect a Salesforce CRM
  org. This step confirms your agreement that the Data 360 org retrieves—or stops retrieving—data from
  your source org, enhancing security.

  Ingest Data Faster with Ready-to-Use Data Lake Objects
  Ingest data more efficiently by using standard data lake objects (DLOs) and mappings in Data 360.
  Previously, each DLO and mapping required manual configuration. Now, ready-to-use DLOs reduce
  setup time and ensure that data is immediately available for use. Standard DLOs include all available
  standard fields of CRM objects by default. These objects include a standard category that is locked, so
  you can’t edit it. In this release, Data 360 doesn't map all standard DLOs.

  code. If native batch data transforms don't meet your business requirements, use code extension to
  author, debug, and deploy your transform logic, then create batch data transforms using that
  deployed logic.

Create Batch Data Transforms by Using Custom Code with Code Extension
(Beta)

With code extension in Data 360, you can create batch data transforms using your custom Python code.
If native batch data transforms don't meet your business requirements, use code extension to author,
debug, and deploy your transform logic, then create batch data transforms using that deployed logic.

Why: Code extension gives you the flexibility to create batch data transforms using custom logic that the
native visual transform builder doesn't support. For example, you need windowed percentiles on
engagement data, such as email opens and site visits, and text similarity on lead notes to match your
ideal customer profile. With Code Extension, you can create batch data transforms that use Python
libraries, such as scikit-learn and difflib , in your custom transform logic to calculate windowed
percentiles and text similarity.

Where: This change applies to Data 360 Enterprise, Performance, Developer, and Unlimited editions.

     Note Code extension is a pilot or beta service that is subject to the Beta Services Terms at
     Agreements - Salesforce.com or a written Unified Beta Agreement if executed by Customer, and
     applicable terms in the Product Terms Directory. Use of this pilot or beta service is at the Customer's
     sole discretion.

When: This feature is available starting in February 2026.

How: In Data 360, on the Data Transforms tab, click New. Select Create From Custom Code, and click
Next. Enter a name and API name for your batch transform, select your deployed custom code from the
list, and then save.

See Also
  Salesforce Developer Help: Invoke Custom Code by Creating a Batch Data Transform (Beta)
  Salesforce Developer Help: Code Extension in Data 360 (Beta)

Build a Semantic Model

Create, manage, and query semantic models using Tableau Semantics.

  Standardize Business Performance with the Updated Metric Creation Flow
  Build a single source of truth by centralizing logic, sentiment, and trends in the Semantic Layer and
  applying them across data models. The updated flow ensures that every team across your organization
  measures success by using the same standards and definitions.
  Unify Data Views with Global Filters
  Create a focused, consistent view of your data by applying global filters to your semantic models. A
  global filter applies constraints at the model level to ensure that all reports and dashboards use the
  same baseline data and irrelevant records aren’t included. You can’t use a global filter with a published
  data source—in this case, apply filters directly in the Tableau data source.
  View Semantic Models with Restricted Fields or Data Objects
  Analysts can view semantic models that contain objects or fields they haven't been granted access to.
  Restricted data objects or fields are masked or hidden, letting analysts see and test the model as a
  whole. This unblocks their ability to use the portions of the semantic model they have access to in
  visualizations and metrics.
  Build and Navigate Complex Models With the Improved Semantic Builder Canvas
  Build and manage your data models more efficiently with a modern, flexible authoring canvas. Focus
  on the logic of your data modeling rather than manual screen adjustments. Existing layouts are
  preserved, so you can start working immediately.

Use Search in Data 360

Ground search on unstructured and structured data in Data 360 to use generative AI, improve analytics,
and use automation tools.

   Fine-Tune, Test, and Optimize Retrievers in Retriever Playground (Generally Available)
   Customize, test, and validate retriever responses in the Data 360 Einstein Studio Retriever Playground.
   A misconfigured retriever can lead to irrelevant output, erode user trust, and increase costs. You can
   verify response accuracy directly in the playground without making calls to an LLM or performing
   manual testing in local environments.
   Add Context to Chunks with Prepend Fields from Data Model Objects
   You can now use prepend fields to add additional metadata that provides context for chunks
   generated from UDMOs. For example, if your search index configuration includes unstructured data
   from webcrawler or sitemap connectors, metadata fields such as Labels, Title, or URL can provide
   additional context to each generated chunk. Prepending these fields improves accuracy of RAG
   responses in Agentforce. Previously, prepend field chunking was available only for search indexes
   created from DMOs.
   Combine Docling Parsing with LLM-Based Image Processing for Accuracy and Cost-Efficiency
   Enhance retrieval augmented generation (RAG) responses with information extracted from images,
   such as flowcharts or diagrams, by enabling LLM-based image processing. When you select the
   Docling parser, which brings together multiple open-source models to understand document layout
   and tables, optionally turn on LLM-based image processing for accurate responses with optimal costs.
   Customize Retrievers with Advanced Filter Conditions
   Include custom logic, define multiple dynamic filters, and use the Like operator to define filter
   conditions in Einstein Studio for Retrievers. Retriever filter conditions now support more data types,
   such as Boolean and Date values. Previously, filter conditions supported only one dynamic filter and
   were limited to text and number data types.






    392

Salesforce Release Notes Data 360

Fine-Tune, Test, and Optimize Retrievers in Retriever Playground (Generally
Available)

Customize, test, and validate retriever responses in the Data 360 Einstein Studio Retriever Playground. A
misconfigured retriever can lead to irrelevant output, erode user trust, and increase costs. You can verify
response accuracy directly in the playground without making calls to an LLM or performing manual
testing in local environments.

Where: This change applies to Data Cloud Developer, Enterprise, Performance, and Unlimited editions.
Not available: Government Cloud.

When: This feature is available starting in February 2026 in the AMER region and in March 2026 across
all regions.

Why: Consider a scenario where an agent answers field service questions on how to install double-door
refrigerators. Technicians report that the agent responses are incomplete and include only five steps of
an 11-step article. The admin tests the retriever in the playground and finds that the article that contains
the response is split between two chunks. The top chunk includes the keyword “double-door” and
appears in the response, but the second chunk ranks lower and is excluded. The admin increases the
result count in the retriever playground to include the second chunk and validates the fix before
deployment.

See Also
  Salesforce Help: Customize, Test, and Validate Retrievers with Retriever Playground

Add Context to Chunks with Prepend Fields from Data Model Objects

You can now use prepend fields to add additional metadata that provides context for chunks generated
from UDMOs. For example, if your search index configuration includes unstructured data from
webcrawler or sitemap connectors, metadata fields such as Labels, Title, or URL can provide additional
context to each generated chunk. Prepending these fields improves accuracy of RAG responses in
Agentforce. Previously, prepend field chunking was available only for search indexes created from DMOs.

Where: This change applies to Data Cloud Developer, Enterprise, Performance, and Unlimited editions.

When: This feature is available starting in February 2026.

How: In the Search Index Advanced Setup for vector search or hybrid search, select fields to prepend to
chunks.

See Also
  Salesforce Help: Chunking Strategies
  Salesforce Help: Create a Vector Search Index with Advanced Setup
  Salesforce Help: Create a Hybrid Search Index with Advanced Setup

Salesforce Release Notes Data 360

Combine Docling Parsing with LLM-Based Image Processing for Accuracy
and Cost-Efficiency

Enhance retrieval augmented generation (RAG) responses with information extracted from images, such
as flowcharts or diagrams, by enabling LLM-based image processing. When you select the Docling parser,
which brings together multiple open-source models to understand document layout and tables,
optionally turn on LLM-based image processing for accurate responses with optimal costs.

Where: This change applies to Data Cloud Developer, Enterprise, Performance, and Unlimited editions.
Now available in Government Cloud.

When: This feature is available starting in March 2026.

How: In Data 360, when you configure a search index, select the Docling Parser. Next, when you select
chunking strategies, turn on image processing to process images by using an LLM.

Why: Consider an airline maintenance division that manages operational processes through structured
RACI-style flowcharts within its governance manuals.These process maps define critical handoffs and
validations across functions such as operators, service representatives, modules, planning, and
operations. Each diagram includes directional arrows, decision nodes, and annotated swim lanes that
reflect step-by-step responsibilities from irregularity detection to workplan reprioritization and resource
redistribution.

Now, Docling parses the text, tables, and extracts the layout. The LLM interprets the flowchart as a
structured process and recognizes nodes, connectors, arrows, and step order. Instead of a flat list of
labels, the LLM reconstructs the sequential flow of actions across roles and departments. As a result,
answers to questions from the field related to responsibilities or the sequence of steps are more
accurate.

See Also
  Salesforce Help: Docling Parser
  Salesforce Help: Billing Considerations for Docling Parser

Customize Retrievers with Advanced Filter Conditions

Include custom logic, define multiple dynamic filters, and use the Like operator to define filter conditions
in Einstein Studio for Retrievers. Retriever filter conditions now support more data types, such as Boolean
and Date values. Previously, filter conditions supported only one dynamic filter and were limited to text
and number data types.

Where: This change applies to Data Cloud Developer, Enterprise, Performance, and Unlimited editions.

When: This feature is available starting in March 2026.

Why:Consider a scenario where your customers are asking questions about car mileage for different
makes and models in a digital portal. You can define a combination of standard and multiple dynamic

filter conditions, such as:

••   1. Make Equal To {!$Make}
•    2. Model Equal To {!$Model}
     3. ModelYear Greater Than 2000

You can then define a custom condition by using logic such as 1 AND (2 OR 3).

  Streamline the development lifecycle by using the Data Kit and Change Set framework to merge copy
  field enrichments from a development sandbox into a production environment. This capability
  reduces the risk associated with manual configuration and ensures consistency across environments.
  Data 360 Clean Rooms Are Now Generally Available
  Use Data 360 clean rooms to partner with other organizations and analyze your combined data while
  maintaining strict privacy. Compare and verify your clean room data mappings in a sandbox org before
  moving them to a production org. Delete unused mapped templates, and end clean room
  collaborations as needed.
  Activate Segments with Consistent Order of Attributes or Columns
  If an activation is run multiple times, the order of attributes or columns in the activated file is now
  consistent, when activating to file storage targets like Amazon S3, SFTP, GCS, or Azure. Consistent
  order of attributes or columns helps in easy consumption of the activation output by a downstream
  system.
  Trigger Data 360 Activations Directly from a Flow (Beta)
  Create an API activation in Data 360 and trigger it from Flow Builder by using an API call. API
  activation expands where and how you can initiate activations. You can trigger activations mid-flow,

  precisely when they’re most impactful, independent of how a flow is triggered. This gives you the
  flexibility to start activations based on any Salesforce event, independent of a segment publish

  Trigger flows using a batch data model object (DMO) activation and activate complete datasets,
  including profiles, engagement history, and large-scale product recommendations to destinations
  powered by activation-triggered flows. Moving beyond segment-based activations, batch DMO

  name that’s unique across the entire activation.

  points.

LWC API Version 66.0

Update the API version for your components to use new features and improvements. Versioning your
Lightning web components ensures that your existing components aren’t affected when Salesforce ships
new features, bug fixes, and performance improvements that change existing behavior. Versioning also
helps Salesforce deprecate legacy features.




    409

    Salesforce Release Notes        Development

    Where: This change applies to custom Lightning web components in Lightning Experience, Experience
    Builder sites, and all versions of the Salesforce mobile app.

    How: You can change a component’s API version in its .js-meta.xml file.

     <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
        <LightningComponentBundle xmlns="http://soap.sforce.com/2006/04/metadat
     a">
        <apiVersion>66.0</apiVersion>
        </LightningComponentBundle>


     Important We recommend that you upgrade your component API version one version at a time. For
     example, from 58.0, upgrade from 58.0 to 59.0, fix any errors or warnings you encounter, and then
     repeat until you get to the latest API version.

When a component’s LWC API version is set to 59.0 or later, it uses that value for its LWC framework
version. Components that specify LWC API version 58.0 and earlier continue to work based on LWC
framework behavior in Summer ’23 (API 58.0). When you set a component to use an earlier API version,
you don’t get new features, bug fixes, and enhancements that are available only with later LWC API
versions.

  Use Complex Template Expressions in Your Lightning Web Components (Beta)
  Add sophisticated presentation logic to your Lightning web component template files, and remove
  extra code from your component implementation. A component that renders a user interface can now
  use complex JavaScript expressions directly in its HTML template file. Use complex template
  expressions anywhere you use basic properties.

Use Complex Template Expressions in Your Lightning Web Components (Beta)

Add sophisticated presentation logic to your Lightning web component template files, and remove extra
code from your component implementation. A component that renders a user interface can now use
complex JavaScript expressions directly in its HTML template file. Use complex template expressions
anywhere you use basic properties.

     Note Complex template expressions is a pilot or beta service that is subject to the Beta Services
     Terms at Agreements - Salesforce.com or a written Unified Pilot Agreement if executed by Customer,
     and applicable terms in the Product Terms Directory. Use of this pilot or beta service is at the
     Customer's sole discretion.

Where: This change applies to Lightning web components in Lightning Experience, Experience Builder
sites, and all versions of the mobile app in all editions.

Why: One superpower of Lightning Web Components is the templating system, which uses the virtual
DOM to render components intelligently and efficiently. Complex template expressions extends this
capability to include a comprehensive subset of JavaScript expressions, enabling more dynamic and


        410

Salesforce Release Notes Development

expressive templates while maintaining your components' performance characteristics and security
model.

How: Complex template expressions can be used anywhere basic properties could previously be used.
You must set the apiVersion of your component to 66.0 or later to enable complex template
expressions for that component.

For documentation and examples, see Template Expressions the Lightning Web Components Developer
Guide.

Display Consistent Empty State Illustrations With Theme Support (Beta)

Use the new lightning-empty-state component to add meaningful visuals and content to your
components that show empty states. This component displays the latest Salesforce Lightning Design
System (SLDS) empty state illustration and correctly sizes it for the container, simplifying your UI
development. The SVG illustrations automatically adjust to the user's selected theme, and can adapt to
dark mode in SLDS 2 themes, for a consistent look and feel across your app. The new lightning-
illustration component displays the same set of illustrations without text.

Where: This feature applies to Lightning Experience. The component must run in a Salesforce org to
display the illustrations.

     Note The lightning-empty-state and lightning-illustration components are a pilot or
     beta service that is subject to the Beta Services Terms at Agreements - Salesforce.com or a written
     Unified Pilot Agreement if executed by Customer, and applicable terms in the Product Terms
     Directory. Use of this pilot or beta service is at the Customer's sole discretion.

Why: Use the lightning-empty-state component wherever you expect a container to display data,
such as records or tasks, but there’s no data to populate it. There can be several reasons why there’s no
data, and now you can find just the right illustration to provide context and lighten the mood. The
 lightning-empty-state component also provides a title, description, and call-to-action buttons so
you can provide more clarity or lead users to the next step of their journey. You can also depict an empty
state without an illustration, title, or call-to-action button. Only the description is required.

How: Include the <lightning-empty-state> tag in your Lightning web component and pass the
illustration name and title by using attributes. Pass the description and cta (call-to-action) by using slots.
See the illustration names and usage information in the Lightning Component Reference . See the SLDS
2 site for images of the illustrations and extensive information about the Empty State design.

This example shows an empty cart illustration along with a Browse Products call-to-action button with
the brand variant.

  <!-- myEmptyState.html -->
  <!-- With illustration and action -->




    411

Salesforce Release Notes    Development


 <lightning-empty-state
  illustration-name="cart:noitems"
  title="It's looking a little empty in here">
  <p slot="description">Head to the product catalog to add something to your c
 art.</p>
  <lightning-button
   variant="brand"
   label="Browse Products"
   slot="cta"
   onclick={handleCtaClick}>
  </lightning-button>
 </lightning-empty-state>

The button handler in the component's JavaScript file carries out the action.

 import { LightningElement } from "lwc";

 export default class MyEmptyState extends LightningElement {
  handleCtaClick(event) {
   // go to the Products tab
  }
 }

The same myEmptyState example component can run in both SLDS 1 and SLDS 2 themes. The
lightning-empty-state component automatically detects the SLDS version of the theme and
presents the correct version of the illustration.

illustration.

Check For Errors From the Disconnected DOM Node Rehydration Fix

To improve framework consistency, Lightning web components now rehydrate only when they're actively
connected to the DOM. For example, rehydration skips detached nodes to prevent lifecycle methods like
 renderedCallback from firing multiple times. Previously, certain edge cases allowed disconnected
DOM nodes to be rehydrated, which could trigger reactive state updates or function invocations on
detached components.

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience, Experience Builder sites, and all versions of the
mobile app in all editions. This change also applies to Lightning web components in Open Source.

How: This change is enabled automatically. If your implementation created a dependency on the
previous rehydration behavior, review your logic for breakages.

before continuing. Fatal errors are also collected in the Error Console for later inspection.

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience.

Why: The Error Console keeps non-fatal errors from interrupting your work, while making it easier to

Salesforce Release Notes        Development

LWS Trusted Mode Enablement Is Discontinued

In Spring ’26, we’re no longer enabling Lightning Web Security (LWS) Trusted Mode. Salesforce briefly
released LWS Trusted Mode in Winter ’26. We re-evaluated LWS Trusted Mode and decided to make it
available only as a beta service in the same Winter ’26 release. This feature gives customers great
responsibility for the security of scripts allowed to run in their org. We want to make sure that the
customers that enable LWS Trusted Mode have a strong security posture both as a company and built
into their processes.

Where: This feature applies to Lightning web components (LWC) in Lightning Experience, and LWC
components in Aura-based Experience Cloud sites. It doesn’t apply to LWR sites or to Aura components
in Lightning Experience or in Aura sites.

Why: Salesforce provides a secure by default environment. Although we recognize the functional
advantages and third-party compatibility that LWS Trusted Mode offers, we’re limiting its availability.
Salesforce can work directly with customers to help make sure that they understand the recommended
security checks and balances before use.

See Also
   Security for Lightning Components: Lightning Web Security

API Distortion Changes in Lightning Web Security

Lightning Web Security (LWS) includes new security protections with more distortions for web APIs.
ESLint rules matching the distortions are also available.

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience, LWR-based Experience Cloud sites, and Lightning
web components in Aura sites when LWS is enabled.

How: These APIs have new distortions documented in the LWS Distortion Viewer (can be outdated or
unavailable during release preview). Corresponding ESLint rules are in the ESLint package.

•   Promise.try
•   WebAssembly.Instance.prototype.exports getter
•   WebAssembly.instantiate
•   WebAssembly.instantiateStreaming

See Also
   Security for Lightning Components: Look Up Distortion Details in LWS Distortion Viewer

Lightning Design System

The Salesforce Lightning Design System (SLDS) includes the resources to create user interfaces consistent
with Salesforce Lightning principles, design language, and best practices.

     Salesforce Lightning Design System Component Blueprints Updates
     Get more out of SLDS component blueprints and utilities with these enhancements and bug fixes.
     Use Dark Mode in More Editions (Beta)
     You can now enable dark mode for Salesforce Lightning Design System 2 (SLDS 2) themes in Free
     Suite, Pro Suite, Professional, Enterprise, and Developer edition orgs. Previously, dark mode was
     available only for Salesforce Starter Suite orgs. Dark mode shows light-colored text and visual elements
     on a dark background, which lays the foundation for richer theming opportunities and more
     customization of Lightning base components. With dark mode enabled, your users can select an
     appearance that reduces eye strain in low-light conditions and enhances readability.

Salesforce Lightning Design System Component Blueprints Updates

Get more out of SLDS component blueprints and utilities with these enhancements and bug fixes.

Where: These changes apply to Salesforce Lightning Design System (SLDS) and Lightning Experience.

How: Improve your user interface (UI) with these recent updates to SLDS component designs.

Deploy Apex Components Faster by Running Only Relevant Tests (Beta)

To reduce Apex component deployment time, use the new RunRelevantTests test level to run only
the tests relevant to your code changes. This feature automatically determines which tests to run based
on an analysis of the deployment payload and the payload dependencies. For fine-grained control, you
can annotate test classes so that they either run regardless of the deployment payload, or run when
specified components are new or modified. This targeted approach boosts the speed and reliability of
your deployment while maintaining code quality and coverage requirements.

Where: The RunRelevantTests test level is available in all API versions. The
 @IsTest(critical=true) and @IsTest(testFor='...') annotations are available in API version
66.0 and later. The feature is available in Lightning Experience and Salesforce Classic in Enterprise,
Performance, Unlimited, and Developer editions.



    427

    Salesforce Release Notes    Development


     Note The RunRelevantTests test level and the associated @IsTest() annotations are pilot or
     beta services that are subject to the Beta Services Terms at Agreements — Salesforce.com or a
     written Unified Pilot Agreement if executed by Customer, and applicable terms in the Product Terms
     Directory. Use of these pilot or beta services are at the Customer’s sole discretion.

    Why: The new RunRelevantTests test level addresses the limitations of the existing
    RunLocalTests and RunSpecifiedTests test levels.      RunLocalTests , the default test level for
    Apex production deployments, runs all Apex tests in the org except the ones that originate from installed
    managed and unlocked packages. In orgs with extensive test suites,  RunLocalTests can result in long
    deployment times even for small changes. In contrast, RunRelevantTests runs only Apex tests
    relevant to modified components in the deployment payload, so the number of tests that run scales
    proportionally to the deployment size. RunRelevantTests also addresses a drawback of the
    RunSpecifiedTests test level. With     RunSpecifiedTests , you must manually determine which
    tests are applicable to the changes, which often requires custom DevOps tooling. In contrast, the
    RunRelevantTests test level engine analyzes the deployment payload and automatically runs a
    subset of tests based on that analysis.

    How: To specify the RunRelevantTests test level when you deploy Apex components, use one of
    these methods.

• To deploy by using a file-based call, set the testLevel field on the DeployOptions object to
   RunRelevantTests . Then pass DeployOptions as an argument to the deploy() method.
• To deploy by using the deployRequest REST resource, define a deployOptions object in the
   POST request body and set its testLevel field to RunRelevantTests .
• To deploy by using the Salesforce CLI, use the sf project deploy start command and set the
   --test-level flag to RunRelevantTests .

    If a test class must always run regardless of the classes or triggers in the deployment payload, annotate
    the test class with @IsTest(critical=true) .

    If a test class must always run whenever specified classes or triggers are new or changed in the
    deployment payload, annotate the test class with @IsTest(testFor='ApexClass:ClassName,
    ApexTrigger:TriggerName') .

    See Also
     Metadata API Developer Guide: Run Relevant Apex Tests in a Deployment (Beta)
     Metadata API Developer Guide: deploy()
     Apex Developer Guide: IsTest Annotation
     Salesforce CLI Command Reference: project Commands

    Use Apex Cursors for Expanded SOQL Query Result Support (Generally
    Available)

    Use Apex cursors and pagination cursors to work with large SOQL query result sets in manageable parts.


     428

Salesforce Release Notes                                                                          Development

This feature, now generally available, includes enhancements since the beta release. Standard cursors,
when combined with queueable Apex, address the limitations of batch Apex. Pagination cursors are
designed for UI elements, such as multipage record lists. Both Apex cursor types can traverse forwards
and backwards through result sets and can handle high-volume, high-resource processing.

Where: This feature is available in API version 66.0 and later. The feature is available in Lightning
Experience and Salesforce Classic in Enterprise, Performance, Unlimited, and Developer editions.

Why: Apex standard cursors offer an efficient alternative to batch Apex for processing large result sets. If
you use an Apex batch job, you must set the batch size to the smallest value that stays within platform
limits. The batch size is the same across the entire result set, so processing that result set can require an
increased number of transactions. In contrast, using an Apex cursor with a chain of queueable jobs gives
you flexibility in how many records are processed with each transaction. This approach provides better
utilization of the asynchronous Apex limit. Calling        Cursor.fetch() still counts against the SOQL query
limit, and the rows fetched count against the SOQL query row limit.

How: This feature, now generally available, includes these enhancements.

•  A PaginationCursor class to implement pagination in a UI. Calling the
    PaginationCursor.fetchPage() and PaginationCursor.fetchDeleted() methods count
•  against the SOQL query limit, and the rows fetched count against the SOQL query row limit.
•  Debug log events to track cursor operations.
   Updated cursor governance limits. The maximum cumulative number of new cursor rows per 24-hour
•  period is 100 million.
   These new methods to track usage against new governor limits.
    -  Limits.getApexCursors() and its upper bound Limits.getLimitApexCursors() method
    -  Limits.getApexPaginationCursors() and its upper bound
       Limits.getLimitApexPaginationCursors() method
    -  Limits.getApexPaginationCursorRows() and its upper bound
       Limits.getLimitApexPaginationCursorRows() method
•  Cursor and pagination cursor support in AuraEnabled serialization and deserialization. You can
   serialize a cursor in an @AuraEnabled response and deserialize a cursor as an input parameter in an
   @AuraEnabled method.

See Also
   Apex Developer Guide: Apex Cursors
   Apex Reference Guide: Cursor Class
   Apex Reference Guide: PaginationCursor Class
   Salesforce Developer Limits and Allocations Quick Reference: Apex Governor Limits

 y=flow&namespacePrefix=ourManagedPackage

Specify the Number of Async Jobs to Delete

Use the new method overload for   purgeOldAsyncJobs() to specify the number of oldest, completed
async jobs in your org to purge. Providing an upper bound for the number of records to delete enables
incremental progress when large volumes of records are to be deleted.

Where: This feature is available in API version 66.0 and later. This feature is available in Lightning
Experience and Salesforce Classic in Enterprise, Performance, Unlimited, and Developer editions.

How: Specify the number of completed async jobs to delete, starting from the oldest jobs that finished
before the specified date. This example shows how to delete up to 1000 job records for jobs that
finished before today’s date.

 Integer maximumNumberOfJobsToDelete = 1000;
 Integer count = System.purgeOldAsyncJobs(
   Date.today(),
   maximumNumberOfJobsToDelete
 );
 System.debug('Deleted ' + count + ' old jobs.');

See Also
  Apex Reference Guide: purgeOldAsyncJobs(dt, numOfJobs)

  Expose Custom SOQL in REST API Calls Using Named Query API (General Availability)
  Use Named Query API to define and expose custom SOQL queries, or Named Query APIs, as scalable
  actions for REST API clients. Named Query APIs can retrieve data quickly and more efficiently than

  Update Instanced URLs in API Traffic (Release Update)
  To prevent disruption when Salesforce ends support for API traffic that uses an incorrect instanced
  URL, make sure that API traffic to your org uses the org’s My Domain login URL. First available in
  Summer ’25, this release update was scheduled to be enforced in Spring ’26, but we postponed the
  enforcement to Winter ’27.
  EventBusSubscriber Object’s Position and Tip Fields Are Being Deprecated
  The EventBusSubscriber object’s Position and Tip fields are being deprecated. They are being replaced
  with the new fields LastProcessed and LastPublished. The field type is changing from int to string in
  order to handle large replay IDs. We recommend updating your code to use LastProcessed and
  LastPublished to avoid issues when the replay ID exceeds the maximum integer size.
  Sending Session IDs in Outbound Messages Is Being Removed
  To align with modern security best practices, you can no longer send session IDs in outbound
  messages starting February 23, 2026. Instead, use OAuth to authenticate. When this change goes into
  effect, the new outbound message form won't include the option to send a session ID, the
  IncludeSessionId flag in the API will be ignored and set to FALSE, and the <sessionID></sessionID>
  element of an outbound message payload won't include a session ID.
  Metadata Deployments and Retrievals Have New Limits
  To maintain predictable performance, we're now applying limits to the volume of metadata deployed
  and retrieved for four specific metadata types: AIAuthoringBundle, AnalyticsDashboard,
  AnalyticsWorkspace, and AnalyticsVisualization. These limits restrict the number of metadata
  components allowed within a single package zip file, and the total number of deployments or


    433

Salesforce Release Notes Development

  retrievals permitted within a 24-hour period.
  Data 360 SOQL Query Results Are Limited to 12-MB at a Time
  To prevent large queries from crashing the app server, Data 360 limits Salesforce Object Query
  Language (SOQL) results to 12-MB. SOQL returns the results up to the size limit with a query more link
  to paginate through the rest of the results. If a single query result exceeds the size limit, SOQL rejects
  the query and you can’t retrieve the results.
  SOAP API login() Call in SOAP API Versions 31.0 Through 64.0 Is Being Retired (Release Update)
  In Summer ‘27, the SOAP API login() call in SOAP API versions 31.0 through 64.0 will no longer be
  supported and no longer be available.

To prevent large queries from crashing the app server, Data 360 limits Salesforce Object Query Language
(SOQL) results to 12-MB. SOQL returns the results up to the size limit with a query more link to paginate
through the rest of the results. If a single query result exceeds the size limit, SOQL rejects the query and
you can’t retrieve the results.

Where: This change applies to Developer, Enterprise, Performance, and Unlimited editions.

SOAP API login() Call in SOAP API Versions 31.0 Through 64.0 Is Being
Retired (Release Update)

In Summer ‘27, the SOAP API login() call in SOAP API versions 31.0 through 64.0 will no longer be
supported and no longer be available.

Where: This change affects these SOAP API versions:

31.0, 32.0, 33.0, 34.0, 35.0, 36.0, 37.0, 38.0, 39.0, 40.0, 41.0, 42.0, 43.0, 44.0, 45.0, 46.0, 47.0, 48.0,
49.0, 50.0, 51.0, 52.0, 53.0, 54.0, 55.0, 56.0, 57.0, 58.0, 59.0, 60.0, 61.0, 62.0, 63.0, 64.0

This change applies to Salesforce Classic and Lightning Experience in all API-enabled Professional,
Enterprise, Performance, Unlimited, and Developer editions.

When: You can continue to use login() in SOAP API versions 31.0 through 64.0 until Summer ’27 is
released. At that time, login() in these SOAP API versions will be retired and unavailable. When login() in
these SOAP API versions is retired, applications using login() in these SOAP API versions will experience
disruption. The requests will fail with an error message indicating that the login() endpoint has been
deactivated.

How: Before Summer ’27 is released, customers and partners must modify or upgrade their applications
to use external client apps for authentication. See SOAP API login() Retirement.

Test the retirement’s impact on your org by enabling the test run in release updates. The test run disables
the SOAP API login() call in your org.

Packaging

Packaging facilitates the development and distribution of business apps. Use second-generation
managed packages to create apps to sell and distribute on AppExchange. Use unlocked packages to
develop internal business apps.

  Manage Package Upgrades with Customized Push Upgrades
  Customized push upgrades enable partners and customers to manage the push upgrade lifecycle.
  With this feature, partners can grant select customers the ability to block push upgrades. Customized
  push upgrades are especially useful for highly regulated environments where strict compliance and
  validation protocols require control of upgrade timing and version oversight. This feature provides the
  granular control necessary to ensure compliance and system stability during version transitions.
  Recommend a Package Version to Your Subscribers
  You can now encourage your subscribers to upgrade to a specific version of a package by setting a
  recommended version. When you set a package version as the recommended version, your
  subscribers see an Upgrade to Recommended Version option on the Installed Packages page in their
  org. Only released package versions can be the recommended version.
  Troubleshoot Subscriber Issues Faster by Enabling Debug Logs
  You can now self-serve enabling a subscriber’s access to managed Apex debug log entries by using the
  License Management App (LMA). Use debug logs to troubleshoot issues that are specific to the
  subscriber’s interaction with the managed package. Previously, a subscriber’s access to debug logs
  showing ENTERING_MANAGED_PKG could only be granted by opening a Salesforce Partner Support
  case.

Manage Package Upgrades with Customized Push Upgrades

Customized push upgrades enable partners and customers to manage the push upgrade lifecycle. With
this feature, partners can grant select customers the ability to block push upgrades. Customized push
upgrades are especially useful for highly regulated environments where strict compliance and validation
protocols require control of upgrade timing and version oversight. This feature provides the granular
control necessary to ensure compliance and system stability during version transitions.

Where: This change applies to second- and first-generation managed packages.

Who: To manage customized push upgrades, users need the permissions to perform packaging push
upgrades.

Why: In highly regulated industries like healthcare or finance, an unannounced automated upgrade can
disrupt validated workflows or trigger compliance audits. Customized push upgrades allow you to test
new package versions in a sandbox environment before scheduling the production push at a time that
minimizes operational risk.

  Second-Generation Managed Packaging Developer Guide: Enable a Package Subscriber to Restrict

Recommend a Package Version to Your Subscribers

You can now encourage your subscribers to upgrade to a specific version of a package by setting a
recommended version. When you set a package version as the recommended version, your subscribers
see an Upgrade to Recommended Version option on the Installed Packages page in their org. Only
released package versions can be the recommended version.

Where: This change applies to second-generation managed packaging.

How: Promote a package version to the released state. Run the sf package update CLI command
and specify the version in the --recommended-version-id flag. If a subscriber has a package version
installed in their org that’s lower than the version you set for the --recommended-version-id flag,
the subscriber sees the Upgrade to Recommended Version option on the Installed Packages page.

Troubleshoot Subscriber Issues Faster by Enabling Debug Logs

You can now self-serve enabling a subscriber’s access to managed Apex debug log entries by using the
License Management App (LMA). Use debug logs to troubleshoot issues that are specific to the
subscriber’s interaction with the managed package. Previously, a subscriber’s access to debug logs
showing ENTERING_MANAGED_PKG could only be granted by opening a Salesforce Partner Support
case.

Where: This change applies to first- and second-generation (2GP) managed packages.

How: In the LMA, find the subscriber’s org, then enable debug logs for the package namespace.

0 Important You enable debug logs for all managed packages in the namespace, rather than for
     individual managed packages. When you enable debug logs for a namespace, logs from Apex code
     execution in that namespace become visible in the subscriber org.Because multiple packages can
     share a namespace in 2GP, enabling debug logs for 2GP means enabling logs for all managed
     packages in the namespace.

The New Data Mask and Seed (Beta)

Secure your sandbox data by using the new Salesforce Data Mask and Seed (beta). Admins and dev
teams can define Data Mask policies and use them to mask sensitive sandbox data, such as proprietary,
restricted, government-regulated, and personally identifiable information (PII).

  Mask Sensitive Data by Using Data Mask and Seed (Beta)
  The new Data Mask and Seed (beta) is a native Salesforce app and not a managed package. As a native
  app, users don’t hassle with managed package installation. Instead, the Salesforce platform
  automatically applies necessary app updates.
  Work with the Data Mask and Seed’s (Beta) Redesigned User Interface
  Configure data masking and seeding tasks more easily with a redesigned, intuitive interface. The
  updated experience provides well-organized displays and clear messaging to simplify navigation and
  the configuration process for admins and developers.
  Proactively Detect Personally Identifiable Information with Data Mask and Seed (Beta)
  The new Data Mask and Seed (beta) automatically identifies object fields in masking policies that
  contain personally identifiable information (PII). During policy configuration, the feature provides a
  suggested “Mask With” option for these object fields. Suggesting “Mask With” options reduces the
  manual effort required to secure sensitive data in your sandbox environments. You can always modify
  the suggested “Mask With” option for an object field.
  Maintain Field Value Distribution with Data Mask and Seed (Beta)
  The new Data Mask and Seed (beta) analyzes the existing distribution of field values across your
  sandbox object records during a masking job. This process makes sure that the masked data reflects
  the original frequency and proportion of values for each field type. Your developers can work with
  realistic datasets that mirror the statistical profile of your production environment while keeping
  sensitive information secure.



    442

Salesforce Release Notes Development

  Get Precise Detail from Informative Masking Job Error Messages
  Effectively troubleshoot masking jobs with error messages that provide precise details, including
  problematic record IDs and offending fields. Masking job error messages also include a link to
  documentation explaining common errors. By identifying specific records and fields that cause issues,
  you can immediately address data integrity problems in your sandbox and get it ready for use.
  Run Masking Jobs with Flexible Execution
  You now have more control over when to mask your data. With the new Data Mask and Seed (beta),
  you can manually run masking jobs or schedule them to run later. This flexibility helps you align data
  preparation with your team’s development cycles and maintenance windows.
  Automate Data Masking with Run on Refresh
  Protect your sandbox data by using the new Data Mask and Seed (beta) feature Run on Refresh. By
  automating the masking process, you prevent exposing sensitive production data in a newly created or
  a refreshed sandbox. You also eliminate the task of remembering to initiate manual masking.

Why: This feature provides you with the ability to preserve the integrity of your data distributions. For
example, you can maintain a specific percentage split of city values across thousands of contact records.
By mimicking the original data’s characteristics, you provide your users a more accurate environment for
testing and development without exposing actual field values.

Consider a scenario where the object Contact includes the City field. The distribution of City field values
across all 3,700 object records is as follows: 20% have the value Tokyo, 30% have the value Athens, and
50% have the value Abu Dhabi. Data Mask and Seed maintains the sandbox’s existing 20:30:50
distribution of City field values when masking that field.

How: During the beta period, the new Data Mask and Seed doesn’t automatically bypass workflows,

triggers, or validation rules. Therefore, before running a masking job, manually turn off any necessary
Salesforce automations and then re-enable them after job completion. The new Data Mask and Seed
(beta) is available as a native, Salesforce app that requires no installation. In the App Launcher, search for
and select Data Mask and Seed (Beta).

     Note When the new Data Mask and Seed becomes Generally Available, it will provide the ability to
     filter object records. With record filtering, users can define a desired subset of object records to
     mask.

Build Enterprise-Ready Agents with Agentforce DX and Agent Script (Generally Available)

Use pro-code tools, such as VS Code and Salesforce CLI, to build hybrid reasoning Salesforce agents.
These new types of agents have both the predictability that your business demands and the creativity
that large language models (LLMs) make possible.

Where: These new features are available in Salesforce CLI version 2.123.1 and Agentforce VS Code
Extension version 1.7.0.

What: Agentforce DX helps pro-code developers build these agents by minimizing context switching,
enabling professional DevOps, and simplifying collaboration between low-code and pro-code
developers.

On December 10, 2025, we released these beta features:

•  Author agents by using Agent Script, the language for building Salesforce hybrid reasoning agents.
   Agent Script combines the flexibility of natural language for code generation with the reliability of
•  programmatic expressions for handling business rules.
   Easily edit Agent Script files in the VS Code editor with the new Agent Script VS Code extension, which
   provides standard code editing features: syntax highlighting, visual syntax cues (such as red squiggles
•  for errors), internal validation, and outline support.
   Preview an agent conversation from its Agent Script file with the updated Agentforce DX VS Code
   Extension. With preview, you get behind-the-scenes details of how your agent is working. The preview
   supports two modes: simulated (which uses mocked actions) and live mode (which uses real Apex
•  classes, flows, and other resources).
   Generate, validate, preview, and publish an authoring bundle with these new CLI commands. An
   authoring bundle is a new metadata type ( AiAuthoringBundle ) that represents an agent that uses
   Agent Script as its blueprint.
    - agent generate authoring-bundle : Generate an authoring bundle from an existing agent
      spec YAML file.
    -    agent validate authoring-bundle : Validate an authoring bundle to make sure that its Agent
      Script file compiles successfully and you can use it to publish an agent.
    -   agent publish authoring-bundle : Publish an authoring bundle to your org, which results in a
      new agent or a new version of an existing agent.
    - agent preview : Interact with an agent to preview how it responds to your statements, questions,
      and commands (utterances).

On February 18, 2026, we released the Generally Available product, and we added or changed these
features:

•  Agentforce Vibes Rules for Agent Script: Agentforce Vibes now includes a global rule for coding
•  Agent Script files.
   Improved Agent Preview: Previewing an agent now works the same regardless of how you started the
   conversation (using an Agent Script file or a published agent.) Previously you were required to
•  configure extra security using a connected app to preview a published agent.
   Programmatic Agent Preview: Preview an agent programmatically, without starting an interactive


      451

    Salesforce Release Notes        Development

   session, with these four new CLI commands. This feature is useful when you want an agent to test your
   agent.
    - agent preview start : Start a programmatic agent preview session.
    - agent preview send : Send a message to an existing agent preview session.
    - agent preview sessions : List all known programmatic agent preview sessions.
• - agent preview end : End an existing programmatic agent preview session and get trace location.
   Enhanced Session Tracer: Get oodles of useful session trace information with the enhanced Agent
• Tracer panel in VS Code.
   Simpler Authoring Bundle Generation: You're no longer required to generate an agent spec YAML file
   when generating an authoring bundle. This feature makes it even easier to get started with Agent
   Script agents.

    Agentforce DX is the pro-code equivalent of the newly released Agentforce Builder UI that runs in your
    org.

     nfo Agent" --target-org my-org

    Improve Deploy Performance by Running Only Relevant Apex Tests

Run only relevant Apex tests when you deploy metadata to your org. Use the new RunRelevantTests
value of the --test-level flag of the project deploy start|validate commands. You can also
use the same flag with the project delete source command.

    Salesforce automatically identifies the relevant tests based on an analysis of the deployment payload and
    the payload dependencies.

This example deploys source files in the force-app package directory to the org with the alias my-



                                454

    Salesforce Release Notes        Development

    scratch and runs only relevant Apex tests:

     sf project deploy start --source-dir force-app --test-level RunRelevantTests
     --target-org my-scratch


    Run Apex and Flow Tests with a Single CLI Command (Beta)


         Note This feature is a beta service that is subject to the Beta Services Terms at Agreements -
         Salesforce.com or a written Unified Pilot Agreement if executed by Customer, and applicable terms
         in the Product Terms Directory. Use of this pilot or beta service is at the Customer's sole discretion.

    Ensure interoperability between Apex classes and flows by running their tests in a single and unified way
    with these new CLI commands:

    •   logic run test : Run tests for Apex and Flows in an org.
    •   logic get test : Get the results of an async test run, or if it timed out.

Many flags of these new commands mimic the flags for the existing apex run|get test and flow
run|get test commands, such as --tests , --test-level , --code-coverage , --class-
names , and --output-dir . But the new logic run test command expands the --tests flag so
that you can specify both Apex and flow tests and adds a --test-category flag to narrow the type of
tests you want to run.

    By default, the logic run test command runs asynchronously and returns a test run ID. Then use the
       logic get test command to retrieve the results.

    This example runs all local Apex and flow tests in the org with the alias my-scratch asynchronously:

       sf logic run test --test-level RunLocalTests --test-category Apex --test-categ
       ory Flow --target-org my-scratch

    The command returns a test run ID that you pass to the logic get test command to get the test
    results:

       sf logic get test --test-run-id <test-run-id>


Retrieve Package Metadata for a Specified Package Version

You can retrieve package metadata for only second-generation managed package versions or unlocked
packages.

This example shows how to retrieve package metadata for a converted subscriber package version ID
(starts with 04t) into my-directory in your Salesforce DX project directory:


         455

Salesforce Release Notes    Development


sf package version retrieve --package 04tXXX --output-dir my-directory --targe
t-dev-hub devhub@example.com


Customize the Timeout When Attempting to Log Into an Org

If you try to authorize an org with the org login web CLI command, and it runs into an issue, the CLI
command now times out after 2 minutes, rather than hanging indefinitely. Customize the number of
milliseconds that the command waits to time out with the new SF_WEB_OAUTH_SERVER_TIMEOUT
environment variable. The default value is 120000 (2 minutes).

This example sets the timeout to 3 minutes:

export SF_WEB_OAUTH_SERVER_TIMEOUT=180000


Customize the Apex Test Polling Interval

Specify the number of seconds to poll the org to check for the test status when you run apex test
run with the new --poll-interval flag. Previously the poll interval was hard-coded to 1 second. This
example shows how to set the poll interval to 5 seconds:

 sf apex run test --class-names MyClassTest --result-format human --poll-interv
 al 5 --target-org my-org

AppExchange Partners

AppExchange partners must follow new security requirements for Connected App (CA) and External
Client App (ECA) solutions to better protect integrations.

  Secure Your Connected App and External Client App Solutions
  All AppExchange Partners must follow new security requirements for Connected App (CA) and
  External Client App (ECA) solutions to ensure the highest level of trust and security for Customer Data.
  These requirements apply to any Connected App or External Client App that is included or used in
  connection with a Partner Application, provided or created by the Partner, and in use by more than
  two customer production orgs. These updates include mandatory Proof Key for Code Exchange (PKCE)
  and Refresh Token Rotation (RTR) enablement to prevent authorization code interception and token
  theft. Implementing these standards ensures these CAs or ECAs meet the latest Salesforce security
  protocols and safeguard Customer Data. Failure to comply may result in the Partner Application’s
  AppExchange de-listing and/or Salesforce’s temporary or permanent suspension of the Partner
  Application’s interoperation with Salesforce’s services.

Secure Your Connected App and External Client App Solutions

All AppExchange Partners must follow new security requirements for Connected App (CA) and External
Client App (ECA) solutions to ensure the highest level of trust and security for Customer Data. These
requirements apply to any Connected App or External Client App that is included or used in connection
with a Partner Application, provided or created by the Partner, and in use by more than two customer
production orgs. These updates include mandatory Proof Key for Code Exchange (PKCE) and Refresh
Token Rotation (RTR) enablement to prevent authorization code interception and token theft.
Implementing these standards ensures these CAs or ECAs meet the latest Salesforce security protocols
and safeguard Customer Data. Failure to comply may result in the Partner Application’s AppExchange de-
listing and/or Salesforce’s temporary or permanent suspension of the Partner Application’s


    460

Salesforce Release Notes        Development

interoperation with Salesforce’s services.

Where: Any Connected App or External Client App that is included or used in connection with a Partner
Application, provided or created by the Partner, and in use by more than two customer production orgs.

When: Mandatory security requirements must be implemented for any CAs/ECAs by May 11, 2026.

Why: Detailed security configurations like RTR and PKCE provide critical defense layers against threat
actors.

How: For any Partner Applications with CAs or ECAs that are included or used in connection with a
Partner Application, provided or created by the Partner, and in use by more than two customer
production orgs, update your CA or ECA definitions to enable PKCE and Refresh Token Rotation within
your app configurations and implement relevant changes in the client code.

        This component now supports manual image upload (developer preview).
        Note Manual image upload is available as a developer preview. This feature isn’t generally

    •    This attribute is new.
          manual-image-upload —If present, an image is inserted in the rich text editor but not
         uploaded. To upload images when using this attribute, call uploadPendingImages() .

• This method is new.
   uploadPendingImages() —Uploads images that you insert in the rich text editor. Returns a
   promise that resolves with an array of results, one per image:
 - When an image upload successfully, the results include the imageId , file , success:true ,
   downloadUrl , and contentVersionId .
 - When the image upload fails, the results include the imageId , file , success: false , and
   error .
   If there are no pending images, this method returns an empty array.

    •    These custom events are new.
          imageupload —The event fired when an image upload succeeds. The event detail properties
         include:
       -  imageId —The image's tracking ID, which uses pending-img- followed by the timestamp that
         represents when the image was inserted, and a unique identifier.
       -  file —The uploaded file, which includes the file name, size, and type.
       -  success —Specifies   true when an image upload is successful.
       -  downloadUrl —The permanent URL for the uploaded image.
       -  contentVersionId —The ContentVersion ID for the image. The ContentVersion ID is prefixed
         with 068 .
    •     imageuploaderror —The event fired when an image insert or upload fails. The event detail
         properties include:
       -  error —The upload error message, which can be returned when an upload fails. When the
         image upload fails, the image continues to be available at the temporary URL until a successful


                               464

    Salesforce Release Notes        Development

        upload.
      - file —The rejected file, which includes the file name, size, and type.
      - imageId —The image's tracking ID, which uses pending-img- followed by the timestamp that
        represents when the image was inserted, and a unique identifier. The ID is returned when an
        upload fails.
      - maxSize —The maximum file size in bytes, which is 1 MB or 1,048,576 bytes. Files exceeding
        this limit are not inserted into the rich text editor.
      - reason —The cause of the image upload error. Possible reasons are SIZE_EXCEEDED and
        UPLOAD_FAILED .

            lwr —Determines whether the component is compatible with Lightning Web Runtime (LWR)

ConnectApi (Connect in Apex): New and Changed Classes and Enums

Create custom experiences in Salesforce using Connect in Apex.

Many Connect REST API resource actions are exposed as static methods on Apex classes in the
ConnectApi namespace. These methods use other  ConnectApi classes to input and return
information. The ConnectApi namespace is referred to as Connect in Apex.

 ConnectApi Rate Limit Changes
 To avoid potentially restrictive per user, per namespace, per hour ConnectApi rate limits, we’re
 migrating orgs to the per org, per 24-hour Salesforce Platform API rate limit. Orgs created in Summer
 ’24 and later are already using the Salesforce Platform API rate limit. For migrated and new orgs, only
 method calls that require Chatter are subject to the per user, per namespace, per hour rate limit.
 New Connect in Apex Classes
 These classes are new.
 Changed Connect in Apex Input Classes
 These input classes have changes.
 Changed Connect in Apex Output Classes
 These output classes have changes.
 Changed Connect in Apex Enums
 These enums have changes.

 Connect REST API Developer Guide

ConnectApi Rate Limit Changes

To avoid potentially restrictive per user, per namespace, per hour ConnectApi rate limits, we’re migrating
orgs to the per org, per 24-hour Salesforce Platform API rate limit. Orgs created in Summer ’24 and later
are already using the Salesforce Platform API rate limit. For migrated and new orgs, only method calls
that require Chatter are subject to the per user, per namespace, per hour rate limit.

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience, Salesforce Classic, and all versions of the Salesforce
mobile app in all editions in all API versions.

When: Org migrations to the Salesforce Platform API rate limit continue on a rolling basis. Migrations
occur in the background without notification.

Get the current user’s User record
 Get the currently logged-in user’s User record data, such as the user’s ID or name. You can
 request any fields that are available on the User record.

 This example queries the ID and name of the current user.

  {

    currentUser{
           Id
           Name {
            value
           }
    }
   }
  }

        objectApiName: String!

        layoutConfigs: [LayoutConfig!]
        layoutType: LayoutType
        formFactor: FormFactor
        mode: LayoutMode
        first: Int
        after: String
  ): LayoutConnection
 }

Create, update, or delete record data with mutations (generally available)
      GraphQL mutations, which is now generally available, includes some changes since the beta
    • release.
      The RecordUpdatePayload type includes a Record field that defines the fields that you want
      the response to return. For example, use this mutation query to update a contact record and
      specify the ID and name fields that you want the response to return.

    mutation ContactUpdateExample{
    uiapi {
     ContactUpdate(input: {
      Contact: {
         FirstName: "Sam"
         LastName: "Smith"
      }
      Id: "003RM000008AAAAAA4"
     }) {
      Record {
         Id
         FirstName {
             value
         }
         LastName {
             value
         }
      }
     }
    }
    }

    This example is the response.

    {
     "data": {

 "uiapi": {
   "ContactUpdate": {
    "Record": {
        "Id": "003RM000008AAAAAA4",
        "FirstName": {
          "value": "Sam"
        },
        "LastName": {
          "value": "Smith"
        }
    }
   }
 }
 },
 "errors": []
}

  Previously, the RecordUpdatePayload included a success field that returned true or
   false .

 Make Site Pages More Discoverable by AI
 To make public site pages more discoverable by AI-powered search engines and enhance the precision
 of generated answers, enable generative engine optimization (GEO) in Experience Builder. When you
 enable GEO, AI bots can request content snapshots of your site’s pages to generate answers more
 effectively.
 Use Dynamic Redirect Rules in Aura Sites
 Redirect users from your Aura site to another URL without any coding. Configure dynamic redirect
 rules that use a pattern to identify a URL from your site and redirect it. Previously, dynamic redirect
 rules were available only for LWR sites.
 Return Users to Their Previous Page After Session Timeout
 In all LWR sites, authenticated users are now returned to the page they were viewing before their
 session ended. Previously, the session timeout notification redirected users to the login page, and
 upon logging back in, they were returned to the Home page.

Salesforce Release Notes Experience Cloud

Site Performance

Reduce the risk of downtime for custom domains that are served by a third party. For Visualforce sites,
leave an empty value in the Site Favorite icon field and show your site visitors a cleaner browser tab. In
2026, Salesforce begins to migrate enhanced and custom domains that use the Salesforce Content
Delivery Network to the Cloudflare CDN.

  Simplify Custom Domain Management with a Stable Target Host Name
  If a third party serves your custom domain and your org uses Salesforce Edge Network, reduce your
  effort and the risk of downtime during Salesforce maintenance. Work with your third-party provider to
  update the domain’s target host name to your org’s My Domain login URL, which continues to work
  when your Salesforce instance changes. The current target host name works until your instance name
  or Hyperforce cell changes. We recommend that you update the target host name before your next
  org migration.
  Visualforce Sites Display Only the Specified Favicon
  Visualforce sites now support an empty value in the Site Favorite Icon field. The small icon appears in
  browser tabs, bookmarks, and search results for your site. Previously, when no icon was specified,
  users could see the Salesforce logo.
  Salesforce Migrates Enhanced and Custom Domains Serving Digital Experiences to Cloudflare CDN
  Beginning in 2026, Salesforce is migrating all enhanced and custom domains serving Digital
  Experiences that use the Salesforce Content Delivery Network (CDN) from Akamai to Cloudflare.
  Starting with the Spring ’26 release, all enhanced and custom domains that use the Salesforce CDN
  service are created using the Cloudflare CDN as the default service provider. You can manually migrate
  custom domains to the Cloudflare CDN ahead of the Salesforce-initiated migration.
  Finish Updating Your Legacy Force.com Site URLs
  To ensure continued access to your sites, update references to your old site URLs that end in
  force.com. Redirections from those site URLs stop working in this release. Look for references to those
  URLs in Salesforce, such as in knowledge articles, and outside Salesforce, such as integrations and links
  in your marketing materials.

Simplify Custom Domain Management with a Stable Target Host Name

If a third party serves your custom domain and your org uses Salesforce Edge Network, reduce your effort
and the risk of downtime during Salesforce maintenance. Work with your third-party provider to update
the domain’s target host name to your org’s My Domain login URL, which continues to work when your
Salesforce instance changes. The current target host name works until your instance name or Hyperforce
cell changes. We recommend that you update the target host name before your next org migration.

Where: This change applies to Salesforce Sites and Aura, LWR, and Visualforce sites accessed through
Lightning Experience and Salesforce Classic in Enterprise, Performance, and Unlimited editions. This
change applies only to custom domains with the domain configuration “Use a third-party service or CDN
to serve the domain.”

Why: Custom domains serve your Digital Experiences or Salesforce Sites on a domain that you own, such


    502

Salesforce Release Notes Experience Cloud

as https://www.example.com. When a third-party service or content delivery network (CDN) serves
your custom domain, the target host name routes your domain traffic to your Salesforce org. If that host
name changes, your custom domain stops working until your third party updates the domain
configuration to match.

Until you update your target host name to your My Domain URL, that host name contains your Salesforce
instance or Hyperforce cell, which can change during an org migration. My Domain login URLs continue
to work when those values change.

How: To get the target host name for your custom domain, in Setup, find and select Domains. Then click
the name of your domain.

    Salesforce Migrates Enhanced and Custom Domains Serving Digital
    Experiences to Cloudflare CDN

    Beginning in 2026, Salesforce is migrating all enhanced and custom domains serving Digital Experiences
    that use the Salesforce Content Delivery Network (CDN) from Akamai to Cloudflare. Starting with the
    Spring ’26 release, all enhanced and custom domains that use the Salesforce CDN service are created
    using the Cloudflare CDN as the default service provider. You can manually migrate custom domains to
    the Cloudflare CDN ahead of the Salesforce-initiated migration.

    Where: This change applies to Aura and LWR using the CDN accessed through Lightning Experience in
    Enterprise, Performance, Unlimited, and Developer editions.

    When: The migration occurs from January through June 2026.

    How: To manually migrate your custom domain, from Setup, enter Domains in the Quick Find box and
    select Domains. From the list of domains, select the domain to edit. Select Use the Cloudflare® CDN to
    serve this domain. After the domain has migrated, you receive a notification. Click Activate to begin
    using the migrated domain.
