Set Up Agentforce Lead Nurturing Faster with Guided Configuration

When you’re ready to create a Lead Nurturing agent, the new guided setup experience in Salesforce Go
saves you time and simplifies the process by automating several steps.

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience in Enterprise, Performance, and Unlimited editions
with the Agentforce SDR add-on. Setup for agents is available on the desktop site.

Why: The guided setup process reduces the number of steps and lets you configure and test your agent
all in one place. Setup takes care of tasks like creating a user record for the agent, assigning it
permissions, and configuring Einstein Activity Capture.

How: From Salesforce Go, click Agentforce for Sales and follow the instructions.




Scale Up Lead Nurturing Activity with Automatic Limit Management

Agentforce now manages the Lead Nurturing prospect outreach queue automatically so that agents can
nurture large numbers of prospects simultaneously while respecting email send and LLM request limits.

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience in Enterprise, Performance, and Unlimited editions
with Sales Cloud and the Agentforce Lead Nurturing add-on. Setup for agents is available on the desktop
site.

Why: Previously there was a maximum number of prospects assignments per day. Now, users can keep
adding prospects while Agentforce manages the queue automatically. The queue gives highest priority to
reply emails, then intro emails and nudges.

Build Pipeline Faster by Assigning Prospects to Agentforce Lead Nurturing in Bulk

Users can now assign up to 200 prospects at once to a Lead Nurturing agent from list views. Agentforce
adds assignments that exceed email send or LLM limits to a managed queue that’s visible in the Agent



    930

Salesforce Release Notes Sales

Command Center. Previously, you could only assign records one at a time or by using assignment rules in
the agent configuration. Adding more than 30 prospects at a time sometimes caused an error. The
managed queue eliminates these errors.

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience in Enterprise, Performance, and Unlimited editions
with Sales Cloud and the Agentforce Lead Nurturing add-on. Setup for agents is available on the desktop
site.

Why: Users can assign up to 200 prospects at once from list views. Agents that use a Gmail account can
have a maximum of 25200 prospects assigned. Agents that use an Outlook account can have a
maximum of 137200 prospects assigned.

Control and Customize Agent Behavior Faster with Modular Topics and Actions

You can now directly view and modify each step of the Lead Nurturing agent workflow, eliminating the
need for complex prompt engineering. In Agentforce Builder, the agent's logic appears as discrete,
configurable topics and actions that are easy to navigate and edit.

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience in Enterprise, Performance, and Unlimited editions
with Sales Cloud and the Agentforce Lead Nurturing add-on. Setup for agents is available on the desktop
site.

Why: For example, you could easily update the Return Calendar Link action to use a custom link for
booking meetings.



How: In Agent Builder, find the Return Calendar Link action and insert your custom link. The agent will
immediately begin using it for all meeting requests.

Connect with Prospects More Effectively by Letting Lead Nurturing Agents Use Sellers’
Email Addresses

Make Lead Nurturing agent emails feel more authentic and increase prospect engagement by letting the
agent send emails on behalf of the prospect record owner. Send as Seller combines the scale and
efficiency of a Lead Nurturing agent with the trusted identity of a human sales rep. The agent uses the
seller’s email address to send outreach and listen for prospect replies.

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience in Enterprise, Performance, and Unlimited editions
with Sales Cloud and the Agentforce Lead Nurturing add-on. Setup for agents is available on the desktop
site.

When: This feature is available beginning February 13, 2026.

How: In Lead Nurturing Setup, turn on Send as Seller in the agent’s Email settings. If you have already
activated a Lead Nurturing agent, create a new agent to turn on Send as Seller. You can create an agent



    931

Salesforce Release Notes Sales

with the new configuration and then deactivate the old agent. When Send as Seller is on, the agent uses
the prospect owner’s email address, signature, and business hours.

When sending as the seller, the agent can send up to 1000 emails per day per record owner. The agent
adds an AI disclosure to the beginning of each generated email. If Require Manual Approval is on in the
agent email settings, generated emails don’t include the default AI disclosure. The default AI disclosure
can be modified in Agentforce Studio, but should be done according to your local regulations. For more
information, see the Salesforce Ethical Use Policy.



    On the Lead Nurturing Monitoring page, a new Sent From column shows the email address used for
    each prospect outreach.




Confirm the Voice, Tone, and Personalization of Agent Emails Before They are Sent

Sellers can now review, edit, and approve agent-generated emails before they are sent. Sales teams can
add an agent to their top-of-funnel outreach workflow without ceding control over email content.
Prospect owners can review intro, nudge, and reply emails, edit them, and either approve or cancel
individual emails.

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience in Enterprise, Performance, and Unlimited editions
with Sales Cloud and the Agentforce Lead Nurturing add-on. Setup for agents is available on the desktop
site.

When: This feature is available beginning February 13, 2026.

How: In Lead Nurturing Setup, turn on Require Manual Approval in the agent’s Email settings. If you have
already activated a Lead Nurturing agent, create a new agent to enable Require Manual Approval. You
can create a new agent with the new configuration and then deactivate the old agent.



When Require Manual Approval is on, the prospect record owner and their manager see pending agent
emails in the Activity Timeline and have up to 14 days to approve each email. The record owner or
manager can edit the email before approving it. If Send as Seller is also turned on for the agent, only the
record owner can approve emails sent on their behalf.

If both Send as Seller and Require Manual Approval are on in the agent setup, the agent omits the
automatic AI disclosure at the beginning of each email because there is now a sales rep in the loop.
When Send as Seller is on, only the prospect record owner or their manager can edit or approve the
emails being sent on their behalf.



    Sales reps can also see the full list of emails awaiting their approval in the Lead Nurturing Control Center.

Understand Why You Win or Lose with Opportunity Closing Recaps

Unlock scalable sales intelligence and trend analysis by replacing unstructured, manual notes with
generative AI for closing recaps. Generated recaps automatically capture the specific drivers behind deal
outcomes, such as pricing, competitors, or product gaps.

Where: This change applies to Einstein Conversation Insights in Agentforce 1 Sales Edition and
Agentforce for Sales add-on license.

Who: This change applies to customers who turn on Einstein Conversation Insights for the first time
starting in Spring ‘26. The Deal Recap feature applies to all opportunities, and data is viewable to users
with the Deal Recap Standard User permission set and who also have access to the specific opportunity.

® Note Deal Recap is currently not supported for existing Einstein Conversation Insights customers
     whose data is scheduled for migration to the Salesforce Platform in Summer ‘26. See Einstein
     Conversation Insights Data Is Moving to the Salesforce Platform.

Why: Deal recap provides a deeper understanding of your pipeline health by transforming unstructured
opportunity data, conversation insights, and so on, into actionable data. By automatically compiling
conversation and activity details into structured deal recaps, sales reps save time while capturing specific
drivers behind deal outcomes. With this structured approach, managers gain instant clarity on individual
deals, and sales leaders can identify and act on trends across the entire organization.

How: From Setup, select Salesforce Go. Then search for the Einstein Conversation Insights feature. Scroll
down to find Unlock Advanced Functionality with Generative AI and turn on Opportunity Closing Recap.

Einstein Conversation Insights Data Is Now Native to the Salesforce Platform

Einstein Conversation Insights (ECI) data for new customers is now stored natively on the Salesforce
Platform. For existing ECI customers, data migration to the Salesforce Platform is scheduled to begin in
Summer ’26.

Where: This change applies to Einstein Conversation Insights in Lightning Experience. Einstein
Conversation Insights is available in Enterprise, Performance, Unlimited, and Agentforce 1 Sales editions.

When: Starting in January 2026, standard Salesforce objects for ECI are turned on by default for all new
customers. Data stored in these records count toward your organization’s data storage capacity.

     Note Analytics for Conversation Insights is scheduled for retirement in Summer ’26. See Analytics
     Dashboard for Einstein Conversation Insights Upcoming Retirement (Summer ’26).

Who: This change applies immediately to customers who turn on Einstein Conversation Insights for the
first time starting in Spring ’26.

Why: With ECI data stored in Salesforce objects, you can now:

• Reference conversation data directly in your CRM automations with tools like Flow, Apex, and Prompt
• Builder to create alerts, update records, and trigger actions based on specific conversation insights.
   Query and report on conversation data by using standard Salesforce tools. Run models, draw new
   inferences, and extract valuable intelligence to guide your sales organization.

Control Access to Layers and Folders in Salesforce Maps

Folder permissions are centralized to make sure access control is consistent. Salesforce Maps
automatically hides layers within restricted folders from search results, Recents lists, and Plot on Load.
Also, new capacity limits are in place to optimize performance and to make sure that users only interact
with authorized data.

Who: The following permission sets now include access: Advanced, CommunityLogins,
CommunityNamedUser, LiveAdmin, MapsAdmin, MapsUser, SFMaps, TerritoryPlanning, and
TerritoryPlanningForSalesPlanning.

Why: To optimize performance and prevent timeouts, Salesforce Maps now limits folder saves to 2,500
rows and layer search results to 200 rows. Non-admins now view folders only for their subordinates
within the role hierarchy.

How: Admins control Corporate folders by default, while Personal folders remain private. The role
hierarchy determines User folder access. With permission logic now centralized, developers should verify
access before creating or cloning layers.

Allocate Financial Targets to Accounts in Territory Planning

Distribute top-down financial targets directly to accounts within Territory Planning. You can split targets
evenly, weight them based on criteria like annual revenue, or distribute by defined segments. To ensure
realistic planning, the allocation logic respects existing bottom-up targets set by the field. This alignment
simplifies the transition from territory design to quota planning.

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience and Salesforce Classic in Professional, Enterprise,
Performance, Unlimited, and Developer editions with Web Services API enabled.

How: Configure a goal within an alignment connected to a segment data source to enable allocation
options. Use an allocation formula to distribute targets using even, weighted, or bucketed methods,
while automatically subtracting any existing bottom-up targets from the total. You can also import
overrides or publish targets to use them in downstream quota planning.

Enjoy Improved Performance in Territory Planning

Create territories for your sales teams with confidence, efficiency, and trust. Territory Planning provides
enhanced security, reliable scalability, and better performance for some resource-intensive functionality.

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience and Salesforce Classic in Professional, Enterprise,
Performance, Unlimited, and Developer editions with Web Services API enabled.



                                                                957

Salesforce Release Notes Sales

How: When you optimize a territory plan, the job now runs on Hyperforce, the Salesforce public cloud
infrastructure with integrated standards for compliance, security, agility, and scalability.

And, when you publish territories to Salesforce Field Service, the job that generates KML files runs more
efficiently. However, in some limited geographies, viewing these published territories in Field Service can
cause a slight degradation of shapes.

See Also
  Knowledge Article:Introducing Hyperforce - General Information & FAQ
  Salesforce Help:Publish Alignments to Field Service

Create Alignment-Based Quota Plans

Streamline the planning process by creating quota plans directly from existing territory alignments.
Planners can now view account-level details and metadata within the quota planning interface to inform
target setting. Because the plans share data, updates to territory models flow into the quota plan,
ensuring assignments and targets remain synchronized.

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience and Salesforce Classic in Professional, Enterprise,
Unlimited, and Developer editions with Sales Planning in English only and with Web Services API
enabled.

Why: Planning traditionally relies on assumptions that shift rapidly as deals close or account rosters
change, which can force teams back into planning cycles. By linking quota plans to territory alignments,
Sales Operations can maintain control over data updates while validating plans against the latest
hierarchy and assignment structures. This integration provides visibility into account-specific metadata,
such as historical revenue, helping to balance quotas fairly even when territory structures are complex or
shifting.

How: Select a territory alignment when creating a new quota plan to import the area hierarchy and
account data. The hierarchy remains read-only within the quota plan to preserve the territory structure,
but you can view account details and allocate targets based on the imported areas. If the source territory
changes, such as a deleted area, the system flags the mismatch and prompts you to accept changes to
keep the plans aligned.

Sales Planning Version 1 is Scheduled for Retirement

Sales Planning version 1 is scheduled for retirement in Summer ’26.

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience and Salesforce Classic in Professional, Enterprise,
Unlimited, and Developer editions with Sales Planning in English only and with Web Services API
enabled.

See Also
  Knowledge Article:Sales Planning version 1 Retirement

Adopt Authorized Email Domains (Release Update)

If you previously worked with Salesforce Customer Support to disable email change verifications, set up
authorized email domains instead. Salesforce is retiring the existing exemption process for disabling this
feature, and authorized email domains provide the same benefit. This update is available starting in
Spring ’26.

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience, Salesforce Classic, and the Salesforce mobile app in
all editions.

When: Salesforce enforces this update in Winter ’27. To get the major release upgrade date for your
instance, go to Trust Status, search for your My Domain name or instance, and click the maintenance tab.

Why: The process to disable email change verification relied on a manual change by Salesforce Customer
Support, which created operational inefficiencies and potential risks. With authorized email domains,
you simplify the onboarding process for new users by using domain-level email verification. Email
verification is bypassed for users with email addresses on a domain that you trust.

     Note These changes relate to the verification of email addresses stored in Salesforce and the ability
     to send email from Salesforce. There’s no change to the requirements for account verification for
     access to Salesforce.

How: To review this update, from Setup, in the Quick Find box, enter Release Updates, and then
select Release Updates. For Adopt Authorized Email Domains, follow the testing and activation steps.

See Also
  Salesforce Help:Authorize a Domain for Return Email Verification
  Knowledge Article:Disable 'Email Change Verification'

Send Email for Users with an Unverified Email Domain

Enable users whose email domains you can't verify—such as users with public email addresses,
consultants, and site users—to send email from Salesforce. With your substitute email address, the user's
display name remains unchanged, but the From address uses email@UniqueId.sfcustomeremail.com,
where UniqueIdis your org ID or site ID. This option also applies to system-generated emails and emails
sent via shared email accounts with an unverified domain.

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience and Salesforce Classic in all editions except
Salesforce Free Suite and Database.com. This change has no impact on trial orgs.

When: This feature is available when Salesforce requires email domain verification shortly after your org
gets Spring ’26, patch 11. See Mandatory Sending-Email Domain Verification Timeline.

Why: Users with public email addresses, consultants, and site users often have domains that you can't
add to your verified list. When you enable this feature, those users can send email from Salesforce while
preserving their display names.

How: From Setup, in the Quick Find box, enter Deliverability, and then select Deliverability. Select
Use a substitute email address for unverified domains, and then save your changes.

Einstein Activity Capture

Accurately monitor event and email syncing with detailed insights and reports on failure. Extend the
scope of your Account, Contact, Opportunity, and Lead reports by integrating detailed email insights in
your reports.

  Migrate Microsoft 365 Authentication in Einstein Activity Capture to Microsoft Graph
  Transition your Einstein Activity Capture’s Microsoft 365 authentication from Exchange Web Services
  (EWS) to Microsoft Graph, which is more modern, secure, and scalable. Microsoft is retiring EWS in
  October 2026, so switch to Microsoft Graph to avoid service disruption. Proactive notifications and a
  single-click tool make the migration process smooth.
  Include Email Insights in Custom Report Types
  Extend the scope of your Account, Contact, Opportunity, and Lead reports by integrating detailed
  email insights such as message type and content in your reports. Insights like these provide a more
  holistic view of your sales activities and help you stay on top of important customer communications.
  Monitor Accurate Event and Email Sync with Detailed Metrics and Failure Reports
  Get clear insights into event and email sync status with accurate metrics. For example, identify and
  resolve setup issues more effectively and improve user trust with sync failure reports. Starting Spring
  ’26, daily event sync time reports exclude no-operations events, which are non-meaningful changes
  that don’t update the event. By excluding events, such as onboarding and backfill events, the reports
  provide accurate sync metrics that reflect only meaningful changes. Salesforce admins can accurately
  assess whether significant events process within published performance times.
  Make Captured Emails Available as Activity Data by Updating Einstein Activity Capture
  Use an option in Setup to update Einstein Activity Capture and migrate previously captured email to
  Salesforce activity data. With this update and migration, all new email data and previously captured
  email data are synced, stored, and available as activity data. This update and migration makes email
  data available to platform tools and operations. After you start the update and migration process, it
  runs and is completed automatically.
  Set Unique Thresholds for Automatic Contact Creation from Emails and Events
  Automatic contact creation from email and calendar events is now available with Sync Email as


    962

Salesforce Release Notes Sales

  Salesforce Activity. We’ve added separate thresholds for emails and events to improve this setting,
  giving you control over contact creation based on the context of user interaction. For example, set a
  higher threshold for emails (three or four interactions) and a lower threshold for events (one meeting)
  to prioritize capturing contacts who are actively building relationships with sales reps. Like before, the
  new contact record is associated with an existing relevant account record.
  Enhance Contact Records Automatically with Sync Email as Salesforce Activity
  Automatic Contact Enhancement is now available if Sync Email as Salesforce Activity is turned on.
  Automatic Contact Enhancements uses generative AI to scan users’ email activity for important buyer
  details. Salesforce automatically updates contact records with information such as seniority level,
  department group, and other buyer attributes. This feature saves sales reps time on manual data entry
  and helps maintain content-rich profiles for more accurate buyer relationship maps.
  Automatically Relate New Contacts to Past Email and Event Records with Sync Email as Salesforce
  Activity
  Sales reps now see important relationship information directly on their records instead of only in the
  activities timeline. When a contact or lead is created, Salesforce automatically associates it with
  relevant email and event activity from the past 30 days. Manually and automatically creating a new
  contact or lead triggers this matching process.
  Event Data Is Now Stored on the Salesforce Platform
  Event data synced through Einstein Activity Capture is now stored on the platform. This update is
  automatic and requires no action on your part. Meeting invitees included in past events who don’t
  have a contact, lead, or user record no longer appear in Meeting Digest. However, invitees without
  records included in upcoming events appear in Meeting Digest. Also, users outside of an Einstein
  Activity Capture configuration no longer see event data on the activity timeline. If you move these
  users into a configuration, data from the previous 180 days populates their timeline.
  Synced Calendar Overlay Is Retiring
  If Show Synced and Captured Events is turned on, Einstein Activity Capture users access a view-only
  copy of events from Microsoft or Google on their Calendar. Some customers mistook the view-only
  events as duplicate calendar entries, so we’re retiring this feature.
  Prepare for Activity 360 Reporting, Activity Metrics, and Activities Analytics Dashboard Retirement
  Before these tools retire, we recommend turning on Sync Email as Salesforce Activity for Einstein
  Activity Capture and configuring reports to explore data captured from email.

Migrate Microsoft 365 Authentication in Einstein Activity Capture to Microsoft Graph

Transition your Einstein Activity Capture’s Microsoft 365 authentication from Exchange Web Services
(EWS) to Microsoft Graph, which is more modern, secure, and scalable. Microsoft is retiring EWS in
October 2026, so switch to Microsoft Graph to avoid service disruption. Proactive notifications and a
single-click tool make the migration process smooth.

Where: This feature is available in Lightning Experience in Starter, Professional, Enterprise, Unlimited,
Einstein 1 Sales, and Agentforce 1 Sales editions. It’s also available with the Einstein for Sales, Sales
Engagement, and Revenue Intelligence add-ons.

When: This feature is available starting in February 2026.


    963

Salesforce Release Notes Sales

Why: This migration is essential to align with Microsoft’s evolving security standards and to avoid
potential disruptions as EWS reaches its end of life in October 2026. By transitioning to Microsoft Graph,
Salesforce makes sure that your organization remains compliant and competitive, with improved support
for modern features and enhanced user-level authentication.

How: Before and during migration, make sure that your Azure admin has granted Microsoft Graph
consent. Then, use the single-click migration tool to complete the migration and select the correct
authentication method.

Salesforce Release Notes Sales

Make Captured Emails Available as Activity Data by Updating Einstein Activity Capture

Use an option in Setup to update Einstein Activity Capture and migrate previously captured email to
Salesforce activity data. With this update and migration, all new email data and previously captured
email data are synced, stored, and available as activity data. This update and migration makes email data
available to platform tools and operations. After you start the update and migration process, it runs and
is completed automatically.

Where: This feature is available in Lightning Experience in Starter, Professional, Enterprise, Unlimited,
Einstein 1 Sales, and Agentforce 1 Sales editions. It’s also available with the Einstein for Sales, Sales
Engagement, and Revenue Intelligence add-ons.

When: This tool rolls out as a staggered release beginning late December 2025 in sandboxes and early
2026 in production.

Who: This is available if Einstein Activity Capture is set up without Sync Email as Salesforce Activity. If
you’ve set up Sync Email as Salesforce Activity, you don’t need to update or migrate.

Why: Updating Einstein Activity Capture turns on Sync Email as Salesforce Activity for all newly captured
email and migrates previously captured email to activity data. Email synced as activity data is stored in
EmailMessage and Task object records, making it available to platform reports, automation, and APIs. It
also offers more granular privacy and sharing settings for captured email data. Previously, captured email
data wasn’t stored in standard objects or available to platform tools and required unique reports to
access and analyze the data. Sync Email as Salesforce Activity was introduced as a default setting for
Einstein Activity Capture in Summer ’25.

Set Unique Thresholds for Automatic Contact Creation from Emails and Events

Automatic contact creation from email and calendar events is now available with Sync Email as
Salesforce Activity. We’ve added separate thresholds for emails and events to improve this setting, giving
you control over contact creation based on the context of user interaction. For example, set a higher



    966

Salesforce Release Notes Sales

threshold for emails (three or four interactions) and a lower threshold for events (one meeting) to
prioritize capturing contacts who are actively building relationships with sales reps. Like before, the new
contact record is associated with an existing relevant account record.

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience in Starter, Professional, Enterprise, Unlimited,
Einstein 1 Sales, and Agentforce 1 Sales editions. The feature is also available with the Einstein for Sales,
Sales Engagement, and Revenue Intelligence add-ons.

When: This feature is available in production starting early March 2026.

Who: This feature is available in Einstein Activity Capture when Sync Email as Salesforce Activity is turned
on.

How: From Setup, enter Contact Creation Automation in the Quick Find box. Turn on Automatic
Contact Creation, if you needed, and set separate thresholds for events and emails. The threshold
maximum value is 10 and the minimum value is 1.

If you set up Einstein Activity Capture before Spring ‘26 and migrate to Sync Email as Salesforce Activity,
the existing value in Automatic Contact Creation is used for the new email and event threshold values. If
you set up Einstein Activity Capture in Spring ‘26 or later, the default threshold for both emails and
events is 3.

Event Data Is Now Stored on the Salesforce Platform

Event data synced through Einstein Activity Capture is now stored on the platform. This update is
automatic and requires no action on your part. Meeting invitees included in past events who don’t have a
contact, lead, or user record no longer appear in Meeting Digest. However, invitees without records
included in upcoming events appear in Meeting Digest. Also, users outside of an Einstein Activity Capture
configuration no longer see event data on the activity timeline. If you move these users into a
configuration, data from the previous 180 days populates their timeline.

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience in Starter, Professional, Enterprise, Unlimited,
Einstein 1 Sales, and Agentforce 1 Sales editions. The feature is also available with the Einstein for Sales,
Sales Engagement, and Revenue Intelligence add-ons.

When: This change occurs in all orgs by March 21, 2026.

See Also
  Salesforce Help:Meeting Preparation and Follow-Up with Meeting Digest
  Salesforce Help:Create a Configuration for Einstein Activity Capture

Synced Calendar Overlay Is Retiring

If Show Synced and Captured Events is turned on, Einstein Activity Capture users access a view-only copy
of events from Microsoft or Google on their Calendar. Some customers mistook the view-only events as
duplicate calendar entries, so we’re retiring this feature.

Where: This feature is available in Lightning Experience in Starter, Professional, Enterprise, Unlimited,
Einstein 1 Sales, and Agentforce 1 Sales editions. It’s also available with the Einstein for Sales, Sales
Engagement, and Revenue Intelligence add-ons.

When: The view-only calendar overlay and the Synced and Captured Events setting in Einstein Activity
Capture is retiring. They’re no longer available unless previously turned on. If you turn it off, you can’t re-
enable it.

Prepare for Activity 360 Reporting, Activity Metrics, and Activities Analytics Dashboard
Retirement

Before these tools retire, we recommend turning on Sync Email as Salesforce Activity for Einstein Activity
Capture and configuring reports to explore data captured from email.

Where: Activity 360 Reporting, Activity Metrics, and Activities Analytics Dashboard are available in
Lightning Experience in Starter, Professional, Enterprise, Unlimited, Einstein 1 Sales, and Agentforce 1
Sales editions. They’re also available with the Einstein for Sales, Sales Engagement, and Revenue
Intelligence add-ons.

Why: Starting in Summer ’25, Einstein Activity Capture can sync and store email data as Task and
EmailMessage object records. With this new data structure you can explore and use email activity data
with standard reports, SOQL, automation workflows, and APIs. Activity 360 Reporting, Activity Metrics,
and Activities Analytics Dashboard aren’t available unless previously turned on. Additionally, data from
these reporting tools that appears in other features, including Prospecting Center, Pipeline Inspection,
and Einstein Conversation Insights, aren’t available unless previously configured. This change affects
other features that use Einstein Activity Capture data, including Prospecting Center, Pipeline Inspection,
and Einstein Conversation Insights. Objects related to Activity 360 Reporting data are also scheduled to
retire: UnifiedEmail, UnifiedEmailParticipant, UnifiedMeeting, UnifiedMeetingParticipant, UnifiedTask,
and UnifiedTaskParticipant.

How: To turn on Sync Email as Salesforce Activity, update Einstein Activity Capture and migrate
previously captured email. Use the Update & Migrate option available in Setup. Sync Email as Salesforce
Activity is enabled by default if you turned on Einstein Activity Capture in Summer ’25 or later.

Microsoft announced the retirement of Exchange Web Services (EWS) starting October 1, 2026.
Lightning Sync configurations that use EWS won’t capture or sync data from Microsoft after EWS is
retired.

  Prepare Lightning Sync for Microsoft Exchange Web Services (EWS) Retirement
  Microsoft announced the retirement of Exchange Web Services (EWS) starting October 1, 2026.
  Lightning Sync configurations that use EWS won’t capture or sync data from Microsoft after EWS is
  retired. To prepare, review the Microsoft guidelines on migrating to Microsoft Graph, the
  recommended API for accessing Microsoft services. Or, plan to move from Lightning Sync to Einstein
  Activity Capture. Contact Salesforce Customer Support to evaluate your options for more information
  on the Salesforce connection to Microsoft Graph API (beta).

Prepare Lightning Sync for Microsoft Exchange Web Services (EWS) Retirement

Microsoft announced the retirement of Exchange Web Services (EWS) starting October 1, 2026.

Transition your Inbox’s Microsoft 365 authentication method from Exchange Web Services (EWS) to

Other Changes in Sales

Review and anticipate other changes that can impact your sales team.

  Update Tasks and Events in Lightning Web Components with the User Interface API
  Bring activities into your custom Lightning Web Components (LWC) by leveraging the User Interface
  API’s support for Task and Event objects. Now, instead of manually coding layouts, security settings,
  and other metadata from scratch, quickly build a custom LWC that automatically syncs with your
  existing configurations.
  Salesforce to Salesforce Is Being Retired (Release Update)
  Salesforce to Salesforce is being retired in Spring ’27. Salesforce has more powerful and integrated
  solutions that align with modern business needs. To prevent disruption when Salesforce ends support
  for the Salesforce to Salesforce product, make sure that you migrate your integrations to one of these
  recommended solutions: Partner Cloud, Data Cloud One, MuleSoft Anypoint, or MuleSoft for Flow.
  New Sales Dialer Licenses Are No Longer Available
  New Sales Dialer licenses aren’t available for customers to purchase. We are planning to retire features
  and functionality for the product in the future.
  Include Records from any Account on Account Plan Objectives
  Support sales account plans across account hierarchies by associating records from different accounts
  to an Account Plan Objective. Previously, you were limited to associating records linked directly to the


    977

Salesforce Release Notes Sales

  account plan's primary account. Now, to build more comprehensive account plans, search for and add
  relevant records from any account. We delivered this feature due to your idea on IdeaExchange.
  Sales Pages Optimized for Salesforce Lightning Design System 2
  To align with the new Salesforce Lightning Design System 2 (SLDS 2) Salesforce Cosmos theme, we
  implemented style updates across several Sales pages. Get an enhanced user experience, particularly
  when you use SLDS 2 or dark mode. They’re also visible when you use an SLDS 1 theme.
  Sales Engagement Data Is Now Native to The Salesforce Platform
  Sales Engagement metrics for new customers are stored natively on the Salesforce Platform. For
  existing customers, data migration is scheduled to begin in June. With this change, the Sales
  Engagement Performance dashboard will be deprecated in October. Metrics are shown in a custom
  report instead.

Update Tasks and Events in Lightning Web Components with the User
Interface API

Bring activities into your custom Lightning Web Components (LWC) by leveraging the User Interface
API’s support for Task and Event objects. Now, instead of manually coding layouts, security settings, and
other metadata from scratch, quickly build a custom LWC that automatically syncs with your existing
configurations.

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience in Enterprise, Performance, Unlimited, and
Developer editions and in Professional Edition with API access enabled.

Why: We delivered this feature due to your idea on IdeaExchange. With User Interface API support for
Task and Event objects, you can now include activities in custom LWCs. Although the Task and Event
objects also have some support within screen flows, these objects aren’t yet available for Dynamic Forms,
list views, or standard flows. And, the IsRecurringSet and IsReminderSet fields on the Task object
aren’t supported in the User Interface API.

When: This feature was rolled out to customer sandboxes in February 2026. The rollout to production
begins on April 13, 2026 and is expected to be completed by mid-May, 2026.

See Also
  Idea Exchange: Support Task and Event Objects in UI API with LWC

A Warning Was Added for Potential Custom Domain Disruption

If your custom domain can experience disruption when you move to Salesforce Edge Network, you see a
warning on the My Domain Setup page.

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience and Salesforce Classic in Enterprise, Performance,
and Unlimited editions.

Why: A custom domain serves your site content on a domain that you own, such as
https://www.example.com. When a third-party service or content delivery network (CDN) hosts a
custom domain, the target host name for that domain changes when your org moves to Salesforce Edge
Network. Until your third-party service or CDN updates that value, your custom domain stops working.

To reduce the risk of outages during the move to Salesforce Edge Network, we added a warning on the
My Domain page when you edit the Routing and Policies section. If your org isn’t on Salesforce Edge
Network and a third party serves at least one of the custom domains in the org, you see this warning.

Identity and Access Management

Connected app creation is disabled by default for all Salesforce orgs. The Salesforce-managed app for the
X (formerly Twitter) auth provider is being retired. Create a Canvas app with an external client app.
Migrate SAML-enabled connected apps to external client apps.

  Creation of New Connected Apps Is Disabled by Default
  The ability to create new connected apps is disabled by default for all Salesforce orgs. This change
  improves security by removing the risks associated with connected apps. This update does not affect
  any existing connected apps, which will continue to function normally. Also, packaged, existing
  connected apps that are deployed in a new org aren't affected. We recommend using external client
  apps for all new integrations and migrating existing connected apps to external client apps.
  Configure Canvas Plugin for External Client App
  You can now create a Canvas app using the external client app framework, which is a more secure and
  modern replacement for connected apps. Existing connected apps with Canvas integrations continue
  to function normally, including those that are packaged and deployed. We recommend using external
  client apps for all new Canvas integrations.



                      990

Salesforce Release Notes Security, Identity, and Privacy

  Track Attempts to Use Uninstalled Connected Apps
  You can now track denied attempts to use connected apps that aren't installed in your org (uninstalled
  apps for short). By tracking these denied attempts, you can identify both legitimate and suspicious
  attempts to use uninstalled apps. You can decide whether to allow usage of the app or to block it
  entirely.
  New and Updated Security Alerts for OAuth Flows
  To discourage users from connecting unfamiliar third-party apps to Salesforce, we added security
  alerts for OAuth flows. These security alerts appear when a user connects a device to Salesforce via the
  OAuth 2.0 device flow. We also updated the security alert on the page where users authorize access to
  their data via OAuth 2.0 flows.
  Device Activation Is Required for Single Sign-On
  As part of ongoing measures to uplift security, we’re enforcing a new device activation requirement for
  users who log in via single sign-on (SSO). We’ll require device activation if the SSO provider doesn’t use
  authentication methods that meet Salesforce security standards. We’re enforcing this requirement in
  phases based on the type of identity provider.
  API-Only Users Are Blocked from Bridging into UI Sessions
  To improve security, users with the API Only User permission can no longer bridge into UI sessions by
  using the frontdoor URL generated by the /services/oauth2/singleaccess endpoint, also known
  as UI Bridge API. This change can break integrations that unintentionally grant UI access to API-only
  users.
  Set Up Passwordless Login with Passkeys (Beta)
  Give users a fast, easy, and phishing-resistant alternative to passwords. You can now enable
  passwordless login with passkeys. With this feature, users can log in with a built-in authenticator (such
  as Touch ID or Face ID) or a security key (such as a YubiKey or mobile device). Look forward to fewer
  password resets, fewer login issues, and happier users.
  Migrate SAML-Enabled Connected Apps to External Client Apps
  Bring the improved usability and security of the external client apps framework to your SAML single
  sign-on (SSO) configurations. With a few clicks, you can now transform SAML-enabled connected apps
  into external client apps. After migration, you get an identical external app with all of your SAML
  configurations, while your old connected app remains in read-only mode.
  Migrate to a Multiple-Configuration SAML Framework (Release Update)
  If you see this release update, your Salesforce instance is using our original single-configuration SAML
  framework, which supports single sign-on (SSO) with only one identity provider. We’re giving you a
  final reminder that with Summer ’26, we’re no longer supporting the single-configuration SAML
  framework. To make sure that your SSO configurations don’t break, migrate to our newer multiple-
  configuration SAML framework, which supports SSO with multiple identity providers instead of just
  one. If you don’t migrate, your SAML SSO configurations will stop working when this release update is
  enforced in Summer ’26.
  Salesforce-Managed X (Formerly Twitter) Authentication Provider Retirement (Release Update)
  The Salesforce-managed app for the X (formerly Twitter) authentication provider is being retired. This
  update breaks any single sign-on (SSO) configurations that use the Salesforce-managed X app. To
  avoid disruptions, create a custom X app and update your SSO configurations.
  New LinkedIn Authentication Providers Use LinkedIn API v2


    991

Salesforce Release Notes Security, Identity, and Privacy

  To stay up to date with the latest LinkedIn API version, new LinkedIn authentication providers now use
  LinkedIn API v2. Configurations that you created before Spring ’26 still use LinkedIn API v1. Also, new
  and existing authentication providers that use the Salesforce-managed LinkedIn app still use LinkedIn
  API v1.
  Triple DES for SAML Single Sign-On Stops Working in Summer ’26
  In Summer ’26, SAML single sign-on (SSO) configurations that use the Triple Data Encryption Standard

  Create an External Client App in a Scratch Org

  be created on scratch orgs. At that time, the only way to get an external client app on a scratch org was
  to package it and associate it with an existing external client app on a Dev Hub org.
  Verification Method Order Is Changed
  Salesforce now uses this order of precedence for identity verification methods: built-in authenticators,
  security keys, Salesforce Authenticator, and third-party authenticator apps. Previously, this was the
  order of precedence: the Salesforce Authenticator mobile app, built-in authenticators, security keys,
  and third-party authenticator apps. This change affects verification method registration, multi-factor
  authentication (MFA), and device activation. As part of this change, we changed the "Show all
  verification method registration options instead of starting with Salesforce Authenticator" setting to
  "Show all verification method registration options instead of starting with built-in authenticators." The

  update will break all connected app integrations that use this flow. For better security, update your
  integrations to use the OAuth 2.0 web-server flow or the OAuth 2.0 client credentials flow instead.
  Check Authentication Method Strength with the SAML Assertion Validator
  We made it easy to check for strong authentication methods in SAML responses from your single sign-
  on (SSO) identity provider. You can now use the SAML Assertion Validator to check the strength of
  Authentication Method Reference (AMR) and Authentication Context Class Reference (ACR) values.

  include any information about their strength.
  Heading Was Added to Salesforce Login Pages
  For a more intuitive login experience, we added a clear “Salesforce login” heading to several login
  pages.
  Improved Support for IPv6 and Private IPs
  We significantly increased the IPv6 address limit for trusted IP ranges and profile IP ranges, and we
  now exclude private IPs from 10.0.0.0 to 10.255.255.255 when calculating the total. If your

Creation of New Connected Apps Is Disabled by Default

The ability to create new connected apps is disabled by default for all Salesforce orgs. This change
improves security by removing the risks associated with connected apps. This update does not affect any
existing connected apps, which will continue to function normally. Also, packaged, existing connected
apps that are deployed in a new org aren't affected. We recommend using external client apps for all
new integrations and migrating existing connected apps to external client apps.

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience, Salesforce Classic, and all versions of the mobile
app in Essentials, Professional, Enterprise, Performance, Unlimited, and Developer editions.

Why: This change addresses an ongoing security threat that takes advantage of connected apps. This
change encourages the adoption of external client apps, which are a more secure, modern replacement
for connected apps.

How: With Spring '26, the ability to create connected apps is disabled. The Allow creation of connected
apps preference in External Client App Settings is also removed. To enable creation of new connected
apps, contact Salesforce Customer Support.

Track Attempts to Use Uninstalled Connected Apps

You can now track denied attempts to use connected apps that aren't installed in your org (uninstalled
apps for short). By tracking these denied attempts, you can identify both legitimate and suspicious
attempts to use uninstalled apps. You can decide whether to allow usage of the app or to block it
entirely.

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience and Salesforce Classic (not available in all orgs) in all
editions.

Why: To prevent unauthorized access to your data, Salesforce automatically denies attempts to use
uninstalled connected apps unless a user has the Approve Uninstalled Connected Apps user permission.
This user permission is intended only for highly trusted users, like admins. As a result, non-admin users
can be blocked from using uninstalled apps that have legitimate use cases. Now that you can track
denied attempts, you can easily see when a user is stuck in this situation. To allow these users to access
legitimate apps from trusted developers, install these apps.

By tracking denied attempts, you can also see if a threat actor is trying to use connected apps to get
access to your org. To tighten security, block suspicious apps. Blocking a connected app ends all sessions
and prevents further usage, even for users with the Approve Uninstalled Connected Apps user
permission.

How: On the Connected Apps OAuth Usage page in Setup, review the Denied Attempts Due to Usage
Restriction column. You can also review the date and time of the most recent denied attempt.

   Device Activation Is Required for Single Sign-On

   As part of ongoing measures to uplift security, we’re enforcing a new device activation requirement for
   users who log in via single sign-on (SSO). We’ll require device activation if the SSO provider doesn’t use
   authentication methods that meet Salesforce security standards. We’re enforcing this requirement in
   phases based on the type of identity provider.

   Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience, Salesforce Classic, and all versions of the Salesforce
   mobile app in all editions.

   When: Starting on January 20, 2026, Salesforce will begin a staggered rollout of the first phase. The first
   phase includes all SSO configurations that use predefined authentication provider types. A predefined
   authentication provider is an OpenID Connect (OIDC) provider that doesn't use a custom authentication
   provider plug-in. To see if your provider type is predefined, go to the Auth. Providers page in Setup and
   check the Provider Type column. These provider types are predefined.

fingerprint or face scans, and physical security keys. To determine whether to require device activation,
Salesforce checks the Authentication Method Reference (AMR) claim in the ID token.

•    Active production and sandbox orgs: Enforced only for orgs with oversized IP ranges. IP ranges are
     oversized if the total number of IP addresses across all ranges exceeds 16,777,216. This limit applies
     separately to the org-wide trusted IP ranges set in your Network Access settings and to login IP ranges
•    for a specific profile.
     Non-revenue orgs: Enforced for all orgs, regardless of IP ranges.

For more information, including a list of acceptable AMR values and an overview of future phases, see
Changes to Device Activation for Single Sign-On (SSO) Logins.

API-Only Users Are Blocked from Bridging into UI Sessions

To improve security, users with the API Only User permission can no longer bridge into UI sessions by
using the frontdoor URL generated by the /services/oauth2/singleaccess endpoint, also known as
UI Bridge API. This change can break integrations that unintentionally grant UI access to API-only users.

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience and Salesforce Classic (not available in all orgs) in all
editions.

How: If you call the /services/oauth2/singleaccess endpoint with an access token that was issued
to an API-only user, the call fails with a Bad_OAuth_Token error.

To allow these users to bridge into UI sessions via frontdoor URLs, remove the API Only User permission.

Set Up Passwordless Login with Passkeys (Beta)

Give users a fast, easy, and phishing-resistant alternative to passwords. You can now enable passwordless
login with passkeys. With this feature, users can log in with a built-in authenticator (such as Touch ID or
Face ID) or a security key (such as a YubiKey or mobile device). Look forward to fewer password resets,
fewer login issues, and happier users.

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience and Salesforce Classic (not available in all orgs) in all
editions.

     Note Passwordless login with passkeys is a pilot or beta service that is subject to the Beta Services
     Terms at Agreements - Salesforce.com or a written Unified Pilot Agreement if executed by Customer,
     and applicable terms in the Product Terms Directory. Use of this pilot or beta service is at the
     Customer's sole discretion.

Who: This feature is available only for internal users, such as employees, who log in to your Salesforce
org. It isn't available for Experience Cloud site users.

Why: Passkeys are phishing-resistant, making them more secure than password-based authentication.
They're also more convenient for users. Because passkeys inherently use multiple factors for
authentication, they satisfy the Salesforce multi-factor authentication (MFA) requirement. So, if users log
in with a passkey, they aren't prompted to provide a second factor for authentication, saving time and
effort with each login.

Passkeys are based on the Fast IDentity Online (FIDO) authentication standard. For more information on
the benefits of passkeys, see the FIDO documentation.

How: You can enable passwordless login with passkeys on the Identity Verification page in Setup.
Passwordless login with passkeys is available only for users with a registered built-in authenticator or
security key, and only for saved usernames. To log in, users click on their saved username and then use
their built-in authenticator or security key.

See Also
  Salesforce Help: Passwordless Login with Passkeys (Beta)
  Salesforce Help: Enable Passwordless Login with Passkeys (Beta)

Migrate to a Multiple-Configuration SAML Framework (Release Update)

If you see this release update, your Salesforce instance is using our original single-configuration SAML
framework, which supports single sign-on (SSO) with only one identity provider. We’re giving you a final
reminder that with Summer ’26, we’re no longer supporting the single-configuration SAML framework. To
make sure that your SSO configurations don’t break, migrate to our newer multiple-configuration SAML
framework, which supports SSO with multiple identity providers instead of just one. If you don’t migrate,
your SAML SSO configurations will stop working when this release update is enforced in Summer ’26.

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience and Salesforce Classic (not available in all orgs) in
Enterprise, Unlimited, and Developer editions.

     Note This release update is available only if you’re using the single-configuration SAML framework. If
     you don’t see this release update, you’re already using the multiple-configuration framework, and
     this release update doesn’t apply to your instance.

When: This update is enforced for production instances in Summer ’26 and was enforced for sandboxes
in Summer ’24. To get the major release upgrade date for your instance, go to Trust Status, search for
your instance, and click the maintenance tab.

This update was first made available in Spring ’24. It was scheduled to be enforced for all instances in
Summer ’24, but we enforced it only for sandboxes in Summer ’24. We postponed the enforcement date
for production instances to Spring ’26 and then postponed it again to Summer ’26.

Why: We’re removing support for the single-configuration SAML SSO framework that you currently use.
With this change, all SAML SSO configurations must use our newer multiple-configuration framework.
With the multiple-configuration SAML framework, you can integrate your org or Experience Cloud site
with multiple external identity providers.

How: If you don’t migrate to the multiple-configuration SAML framework, your SAML SSO configuration
will break when this update is enforced.

When you follow the steps to migrate, your current SAML SSO configuration is preserved, but with some
key changes:

• Your Salesforce login URL changes. Make sure you have a plan to communicate this change to your
   users.

The Salesforce-managed app for the X (formerly Twitter) authentication provider is being retired. This

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience and Salesforce Classic (not available in all orgs) in

When: Salesforce enforces this update in Summer ’26. To get the major release upgrade date for your

managed X app, you can leave the consumer key and secret blank when you set up the authentication

Triple DES for SAML Single Sign-On Stops Working in Summer ’26

In Summer ’26, SAML single sign-on (SSO) configurations that use the Triple Data Encryption Standard
(Triple DES) algorithm will stop working. This change applies to all SSO configurations that use the Triple
DES algorithm, whether you use Salesforce as an identity provider or as a service provider. To improve
security, use the Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) algorithms, AES 128 or AES 256, instead.

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience and Salesforce Classic (not available in all orgs) in all
editions.

When: Triple DES will stop working in Summer ’26. There’s no change to Triple DES support in Spring ’26,
but we recommend that you update your SAML configurations as soon as possible.

Why: The Triple DES algorithm uses a cryptographic key that’s too short to be secure. The AES 128 and
AES 256 algorithms use longer keys that make these algorithms harder to attack. For more information
about encryption algorithm security from the National Institute of Standards and Technology, go to
https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/131/a/r3/ipd.

How: Before Summer ’26, update your configurations to use the AES 128 or AES 256 algorithm. The
steps to update your configuration are different depending on whether you use Salesforce as an identity
provider or as a service provider.

• If you use Salesforce as an identity provider, check your connected app SAML configuration. First, go to
   your connected app Web App Settings and check the Block Encryption Algorithm setting. If Block
   Encryption Algorithm is set to Triple DES, update your configuration to use a more secure algorithm.
   On the service provider, update your settings to decrypt the new algorithm.





    1001

    ¥ Web App Settings


    Subject Type Federation ID



• If you use Salesforce as a service provider, check with your identity provider to see what encryption
   algorithm they use. If they use the Triple DES algorithm, work with your identity provider to use a more
   secure algorithm and to generate a new decryption certificate. In Salesforce, update the Assertion
   Decryption Certificate in your SAML Single Sign-On Settings.

Retirement of OAuth 2.0 Username-Password Flow for Connected Apps
(Release Update)

In Winter ’27, we'll stop supporting the OAuth 2.0 username-password flow for connected apps. This
update will break all connected app integrations that use this flow. For better security, update your
integrations to use the OAuth 2.0 web-server flow or the OAuth 2.0 client credentials flow instead.

Where: This change applies to Lighting Experience and Salesforce Classic in all editions. If you don't see
this release update, you already have the username-password flow blocked, and this change doesn't
affect you.

When: Salesforce enforces this update in Winter ’27. To get the major release upgrade date for your
instance, go to Trust Status, search for your instance, and click the maintenance tab.

This release update is currently English-only. Translations are scheduled to be available in late March
2026.

Why: This update improves security and better protects your Salesforce data. The username-password
flow directly passes the user’s credentials in HTTP requests, which presents security risks.

How: All connected app integrations that use the username-password flow will no longer work. As an
app developer, update your integrations to use a more secure flow. For end user login and authorization,
use the OAuth 2.0 web-server flow with the Proof Key for Code Exchange (PKCE) extension. For server-to-
server integrations, use the OAuth 2.0 client credentials flow. For apps that you didn't develop, contact
the app developer.

Release Updates. For Retirement of OAuth 2.0 Username-Password Flow for Connected Apps, follow the
testing and activation steps.

Improved Support for IPv6 and Private IPs

We significantly increased the IPv6 address limit for trusted IP ranges and profile IP ranges, and we now
exclude private IPs from 10.0.0.0 to 10.255.255.255 when calculating the total. If your IPv6



         1005

Salesforce Release Notes Security, Identity, and Privacy

ranges are now under the new limit of 2^99 (2 to the power of 99), users can log in from allowlisted IPs
without completing device activation. We apply this limit separately from the IPv4 limit, which is still
16,777,216.

Where: This change applies to Lighting Experience and Salesforce Classic in all editions.

Why: The previous IP address limit of 16,777,216, which was a blanket limit for IPv4 and IPv6 ranges,
was too restrictive for IPv6. The previous limit also made it difficult to allowlist private IP addresses.

How: For logins that don’t use multi-factor authentication (MFA) or a strong single sign-on (SSO)
authentication method, IP address limits affect device activation.

• For org-wide trusted IP ranges: if your org exceeds the limit, Salesforce issues a device activation
• challenge even if the user’s IP address is in range.
   For profile login IP ranges: if the specific profile exceeds the limit, Salesforce challenges users for
   device activation even if the user’s IP address is in range. Salesforce also challenges users if your org
   ranges exceed the limit, even if the profile ranges don’t. If users are outside of the profile range,
   Salesforce blocks the login entirely.

This behavior hasn't changed, but with a higher IPv6 limit and more room for private IPs, you can have
more control over device activation.

   Extend Your Custom Apps with the Ability to Update and Delete Named Credentials from Apex
   You can now update or delete a named credential, an external credential, or an external auth identity
   provider from Apex. ISVs and partners that build managed package apps can use these new Apex
   methods for automated setup and more flexible management of external system integrations. If a
   customer uses a managed package that programmatically updates the endpoint URL for a named
   credential or any URL fields on its related external credential or auth identity provider, the Enabled for
   Callouts field on the named credential is turned off until an admin manually reviews and enables it.
   Enhanced Security for Named Credentials in Managed Packages
   By default, as of this announcement, named credentials added to a managed package are now
   developer controlled and can’t be updated. Therefore, subscribers (customers) can’t edit the named
   credentials after package installation. This change prevents malicious automation from silently
   changing the endpoint URL.

Salesforce Release Notes Security, Identity, and Privacy

Extend Your Custom Apps with the Ability to Update and Delete Named
Credentials from Apex

You can now update or delete a named credential, an external credential, or an external auth identity
provider from Apex. ISVs and partners that build managed package apps can use these new Apex
methods for automated setup and more flexible management of external system integrations. If a
customer uses a managed package that programmatically updates the endpoint URL for a named
credential or any URL fields on its related external credential or auth identity provider, the Enabled for
Callouts field on the named credential is turned off until an admin manually reviews and enables it.

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience in Enterprise, Performance, Unlimited, and
Developer editions in API version 66.0 and later.

Why: ISVs and partners often need to manage multiple target endpoints for different customers, making
packaged credentials difficult to manage. Previously, developers could only programmatically create
named credentials, which required manual intervention for any subsequent updates or removals.

How: Developers use these new Apex methods to update and delete credentials via a UI in their
managed packages: deleteExternalAuthIdentityProvider ,
 updateExternalAuthIdentityProvider , deleteExternalCredential ,
 updateExternalCredential , deleteNamedCredential , and updateNamedCredential . If the
named credential Enabled for Callouts field is turned off, the customer admin must review any endpoint
changes to the named credential or its related external credential or external auth identity provider and
manually enable the field.

See Also
  Apex Developer Guide: NamedCredentials Methods
  Named Credentials Developer Guide: Update or Delete an OAuth Named Credential

Enhanced Security for Named Credentials in Managed Packages

By default, as of this announcement, named credentials added to a managed package are now
developer controlled and can’t be updated. Therefore, subscribers (customers) can’t edit the named
credentials after package installation. This change prevents malicious automation from silently changing
the endpoint URL.

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience in Enterprise, Performance, Unlimited, and
Developer editions in API version 66.0 and later.

When: Salesforce is making this change on a rolling basis starting in February 2026.

How: ISVs can explicitly enable editing of specific credentials by subscribers. If a managed package
programmatically updates a credential endpoint URL (via Apex or Metadata API), Salesforce
automatically disables callouts for that credential. The customer admin must review any endpoint
changes to the named credential and manually enable callouts.

Privacy Center

Explore Privacy Requests as a new way to fulfill Right to Be Forgotten (RTBF) requests from your
customers. Additionally, you can now ignore object processing errors and bypass automations at the
object or policy level.

  Delete Records in Your Org and Data 360 with Privacy Requests
  When fulfilling Right to Be Forgotten (RTBF) requests from your customers, you can now delete records
  across your Salesforce org and Data 360 with a single, integrated solution. Use Privacy Requests to find
  and selectively delete records for a data subject. Easily search for records using flexible criteria, see
  record details and relationships, and make informed decisions about data deletion.
  Ignore Errors While Processing Records
  Configure your Privacy Center policies to ignore object processing errors. When errors are ignored, the
  job session continues to the next object on the policy instead of stopping completely. This option is
  useful if validations or business logic produce errors that you know are safe to ignore. Keep in mind
  that ignoring object processing errors can cause accidental data loss or modification.
  Bypass Automations While Processing Records
  There’s a new way to bypass automations while processing records in Privacy Center. Instead of
  modifying individual triggers or validation rules, you can select a bypass setting at the object or policy
  level. This approach bypasses all triggers and validations for the selected objects on a policy, or for the
  entire policy.

Shield Platform Encryption

Reduce friction in the encryption process with Database Encryption, now generally available in all
regions. Bring Your Own Key for Data 360 opens more root key management options.

  Encrypt Your Entire Database (GA Release)
  Database Encryption is generally available worldwide. It began its deployment in Winter '26. Due to
  the pace of the controlled release, some regions lagged in enabling the new feature. Database
  Encryption allows you to sort, filter and reference encrypted data without functional or performance
  tradeoffs. You can still apply Field Level Encryption to individual fields if required.
  Bring Your Own Key to Data 360
  Platform Encryption for Data 360 customers can now make use of the Bring Your Own Key (BYOK)
  feature of Shield Platform Encryption. When you supply your own root key, you get the benefits built
  into Salesforce Shield Platform Encryption, plus the extra assurance that comes from exclusively
  managing your own key material. For Data 360, BYOK supports root keys only. Data 360 then manages
  all DEK creation and wrapping using the root key. To be compatible with Salesforce BYOK, use a
  PKCS#8 encrypted, Base64 encoded 4096 RSA key pair with appropriate headers and footers.
  Encrypt Newly Supported Fields with Shield Platform Encryption
  You can now encrypt the Comments field on these objects: Business Operations Process Participant,
  Compliance Control Participant, Compliance Policy Participant, Validation Procedure Participant,
  Financial Account Participant, and Regulation Participant. On the Case object, you can encrypt the
  Rich Text Area for Case Description field. On the Provider Activity Goal Limit object, you can encrypt
  the Source System Identifier field.

pace of the controlled release, some regions lagged in enabling the new feature. Database Encryption
allows you to sort, filter and reference encrypted data without functional or performance tradeoffs. You

Other Security Changes

Quickly see the impact of each violation in the Trusted URL and Browser Policy Violations list.

  Distinguish Between Blocked and Reported CSP Violations
  See at a glance whether a recent violation blocked a resource request or redirection with the new
  Impact field on the Trusted URL and Browser Policy Violations list. Violations with an impact of
  Reported block that resource request only when you enable a stricter CSP policy, such as when you
  enable Adopt Updated CSP Directives in Session Settings. Previously, you used the DISPOSITION field
  of the CSP Violation Event Type object to determine whether a violation was enforced or reported.
  Salesforce Sites Display the Specified Favicon Only
  Salesforce Sites now support an empty value in the Site Favorite Icon field.

Distinguish Between Blocked and Reported CSP Violations

See at a glance whether a recent violation blocked a resource request or redirection with the new Impact
field on the Trusted URL and Browser Policy Violations list. Violations with an impact of Reported block
that resource request only when you enable a stricter CSP policy, such as when you enable Adopt
Updated CSP Directives in Session Settings. Previously, you used the DISPOSITION field of the CSP
Violation Event Type object to determine whether a violation was enforced or reported.

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience and Salesforce Classic in Enterprise, Performance,
Unlimited, and Developer editions.

How: In Setup, find and select Trusted URL and Browser Policy Violations. The impact of blocked
redirections and malformed URLs is always Blocked.

Salesforce Voice with Telephony Providers

Explore the latest Salesforce Voice with Telephony Providers (formerly Service Cloud Voice)
enhancements that empower reps and supervisors to more efficiently and effectively resolve customer
issues over the phone.

     Note Service Cloud Voice is now Salesforce Voice with Telephony Providers. While we’re tidying up
     our content to update the name everywhere, you will see the previous name until we replace it,
     including in the app itself.

  Track Your Telephony Models with New Salesforce Voice Names
  As Service Cloud Voice becomes Salesforce Voice to take advantage of the latest AI innovations and

        1032

Salesforce Release Notes Service

  capabilities, we are also renaming its underlying telephony models. We group these models as
  Salesforce Voice with Telephony Providers to distinguish them from our native Salesforce Voice. We
  have updated the name on the landing page, but updates to the UI and documentation are in
  progress. You still see the previous names in the app and documentation until we fully replace them.
  There's no setup required, and the updated names appear automatically as they roll out.
  Get the Latest Amazon Connect Contact Center Version 20.1
  Update your contact center to version 20.1 to unlock the latest Service Cloud Voice features. This
  version automatically refreshes JSON Web Tokens (JWTs) every five minutes to ensure uninterrupted
  transcriptions during long calls and provides optimized resource management during stack updates.
  You also gain improved security updates and advanced health diagnostics for your contact center
  environment. To test the updates before they go live in production, deploy them to your sandbox first.
  Scale Your VoiceCall Object with More Custom Fields
  For greater flexibility, the maximum number of custom fields for the standard VoiceCall object is
  increased to 300. This update improves data capacity and avoids the architectural complexity of
  creating custom objects or polling other standard objects to store voice-related data.
  Manage Contact Center Groups and Queues in Bulk
  Save time and reduce manual data entry when managing your contact center. Admins can now use
  the Bulk API to create contact center groups and queues in bulk. This enhancement improves admin
  efficiency, supports large contact centers, and enables more comprehensive data management.
  Add Flexibility to Unified Routing Transfers by Routing Calls to a Flow
  Simplify the decision process for your reps by configuring voice call transfers with Omni-Channel
  Flows. This Omni-Channel Unified Routing enhancement unlocks more dynamic routing capabilities,
  allowing you to use complex business logic and skill-based criteria within a flow to determine the next
  transfer target.
  Route Voicemails and Desk Phone Calls with Unified Routing
  Unified Routing now supports voicemails and desk phone calls. This feature reduces wait times,
  improves rep productivity, and provides an efficient Omni-Channel experience. You can use this
  feature only if your telephony provider supports it.
  Minimize Abandoned Calls with Queued Callbacks for Omni-Channel Unified Routing
  Respect customers’ time, save telephony minutes, and keep callers from abandoning their calls by
  giving them the option to request a callback without losing their place in a queue. When a rep accepts
  a contact request in Omni-Channel, an outbound call to the customer starts automatically. The initial
  inbound call, contact request, and outbound call are all linked for easy rep reference. This feature is
  available for contact centers using Omni-Channel Unified Routing.
  Use Voicemail Drop for Outbound Calls (Beta)
  When an outbound call reaches voicemail, you can disconnect the call to automatically leave your
  default pre-recorded message. While the system plays the message, you can move on to your next task
  immediately, increasing your productivity. You can record multiple messages and select one as your
  default.
  Link Voice Calls to Their Source Records Automatically
  When you initiate an outbound call by using Click-to-Dial from a custom object, or a contact role on a
  Case or Opportunity, the resulting VoiceCall record now automatically establishes a lookup
  relationship to the source record. This change removes the need for manual linking and reduces the


    1033

Salesforce Release Notes Service

   need for customization with Flows or Apex triggers. Previously, this automatic linking was available
   only for Account, Case, Contact, Lead, Opportunity, CollectionPlan, and ContactRequest records.
   Get Actionable Error Messages for Failed Outbound Calls
   When an outbound call fails to connect, reps now have descriptive and actionable error messages
   directly in the Omni-Channel widget, which helps them to take immediate corrective action. This
   feature improves rep productivity and helps increase successful call connection rates.
   Get the Latest Enhancements for Your Amazon Connect Contact Center
   Update your contact center to version 20.0 to unlock the latest Service Cloud Voice features. This
   version introduces a Lambda layer for running service health checks, and contact flows and subflows
   for voicemail drop. To test the updates before they go live in production, deploy them to your sandbox
   first.
   Update Your United States AWS Billing Address for Accurate Emergency Calling Fees
   As of March 1, 2025, AWS charges emergency calling fees for Amazon Connect based on the
   subaccount billing address. By default, Salesforce uses its own address for Service Cloud Voice with
   Amazon Connect customers with companies in the United States. To ensure correct charges and
   compliance with local regulations, update your AWS account to reflect your company’s address
   instead.
   Open CTI Is Scheduled for Retirement
   Open CTI is in maintenance mode and is scheduled for retirement on February 28, 2028. Effective
   immediately, Open CTI is deprecated and unavailable for newly created Agentforce Service orgs. We
   recommend transitioning your telephony integration to Service Cloud Voice to take advantage of the
   latest telephony innovations and native AI capabilities.

Track Your Telephony Models with New Salesforce Voice Names

As Service Cloud Voice becomes Salesforce Voice to take advantage of the latest AI innovations and
capabilities, we are also renaming its underlying telephony models. We group these models as Salesforce
Voice with Telephony Providers to distinguish them from our native Salesforce Voice. We have updated
the name on the landing page, but updates to the UI and documentation are in progress. You still see
the previous names in the app and documentation until we fully replace them. There's no setup
required, and the updated names appear automatically as they roll out.

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience in Enterprise, Unlimited, and Performance editions.

Salesforce Voice with Telephony Providers (formerly Service Cloud Voice) is available in Agentforce Sales
(formerly Sales Cloud), Agentforce Service (formerly Service Cloud), and Government Cloud with the
Service Cloud Voice add-on license. It’s also available in Agentforce for Industries built from Sales or
Service. View supported editions.

How: The updated telephony model names are:

•• Service Cloud Voice with Amazon Connect is now Salesforce Voice with Amazon Connect.
• Service Cloud Voice with Partner Telephony is now Salesforce Voice with Partner Telephony.
   Service Cloud Voice with Partner Telephony from Amazon Connect is now Salesforce Voice with
   Partner Telephony from Amazon Connect.

Update Your United States AWS Billing Address for Accurate Emergency Calling Fees

customers with companies in the United States. To ensure correct charges and compliance with local
