Email

Enhancements include new and updated features for Service Email.

  Email Across Languages with Real-Time Translations
  Let service reps translate Service Email conversations, expanding customer support across languages.
  A rep can translate an end user’s email into the rep’s language, as well as translate their response into
  the end user’s language before sending. Previously, a Service Email rep had to speak the same
  language as an end user in order to assist.
  Agent Session Continuity is Improved for Case-Related Email Threads
  An Agentforce Agent session now remains associated with a case and all of its related emails over a
  three-day period. This preserves crucial information and context variables, such as the variables set by
  previous actions. Previously, a new session was opened for every inbound email, causing AI to lose
  conversation history and requiring repeated reinterpretation of earlier interactions.
  Inbound Limit for Service Agent Emails is Extended
  Inbound emails handled by the Service agent count against your Agentforce for Service on Email daily
  transaction limit, which is 5,000 by default. You can ask Salesforce Customer Support to raise this
  limit. Previously, this checked against the org's single email limit, which is shared with Apex and flow
  emails.
  Email Composer is Modernized with New Button Colors
  As part of a TinyMCE upgrade, the email composer button icons changed from grey to blue. This
  brings the composer up to our Salesforce Lightning Design System standards.
  Access Email Context with Agentforce Service Agent Variables
  Use new context variables to pass information from the Service Email Connection directly to your
  agent. You can reference specific variables in topics and actions for more precise control over your
  implementation. Admins can now avoid relying on plain text instructions to obtain context.

Email Across Languages with Real-Time Translations

Let service reps translate Service Email conversations, expanding customer support across languages. A
rep can translate an end user’s email into the rep’s language, as well as translate their response into the
end user’s language before sending. Previously, a Service Email rep had to speak the same language as an
end user in order to assist.

Where: This change applies to Service Email. View required editions.

How: Go to the Real-Time Translations node in Setup, and turn on Translate Service Email. Optionally,
upload a custom terminology file to assist with translation of your business terminology.

A Service rep can translate an end-user’s email in the case feed by clicking the dropdown to the right of
the email and selecting Translate Email Body.

Access Email Context with Agentforce Service Agent Variables

Use new context variables to pass information from the Service Email Connection directly to your agent.
You can reference specific variables in topics and actions for more precise control over your
implementation. Admins can now avoid relying on plain text instructions to obtain context.

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience in Enterprise, Performance, Unlimited, and
Developer Editions with Foundations or Agentforce 1 Editions.

Why: Direct variable referencing replaces the previous method that used plain text instructions to
retrieve context passed by the Service Email Connection. Transitioning to these variables makes sure that
your topics and actions consistently access the correct Case ID, end-user email, and Contact ID.

How: New Agentforce Service Agents include these variables by default. You have to manually add them
to existing agents by deactivating the agent and using the Context tab in the Agentforce Builder. Create
variables for emailCaseId, endUserEmail, and endUserContactId, ensure Allow value to be set by API is
true.

Messaging

Explore the latest enhancements that empower reps and supervisors to more efficiently and effectively


    1043

Salesforce Release Notes Service

resolve customer issues over Messaging channels.

  Create Dynamic WhatsApp Messaging Content
  Go beyond simple data collection. Transform your WhatsApp Flows into dynamic, data-driven
  experiences to drive higher customer engagement and conversion rates. Based on input data and user
  responses, adapt the message content and screens. For example, offer personalized interest rates
  based on the user’s credit history or dynamically render the next screen in a WhatsApp Flow based on
  a user’s response in the previous screen.
  End Conversations from the Messaging Session List View
  You asked, we listened. We brought back the End Conversation menu option in the Messaging Session
  list view of a Messaging User record for Enhanced Messaging. When you select End Conversation, the
  messaging session is ended, and any future messaging sessions that are initiated by the end user
  aren’t stitched back to it in a cohesive conversation history.
  Prevent Reps from Disconnecting Conversation History
  To preserve conversation history in Enhanced Messaging, we removed the End Conversation menu
  option from the list view for messaging sessions. Selecting this option prevented future messaging
  sessions for an end user from being stitched to existing messaging conversation history, which worked
  against the asynchronous promise of Enhanced Messaging. This menu option is still available in
  messaging sessions for Enhanced Chat.
  Manage Messaging Costs with Salesforce Message Credits
  Optimize your messaging budget by switching to the new Salesforce Message Credits for WhatsApp
  and SMS. It tracks your WhatsApp and SMS consumption in real time through a single pool of credits
  that's applicable across Service and Marketing. You move away from bundled add-ons and pay for
  exactly what you use, with all messaging data integrated directly into your Salesforce Digital Wallet.
  Avoid Surprises with New License Checks in Messaging
  During messaging channel setup, we now let you know if you’re missing or running low on brand
  licenses, campaign licenses, or SMS lease licenses, or SMS or WhatsApp message credits. We also
  show the number of licenses or requests remaining. These messages are visible on the Regulatory
  Compliance and Messaging Settings pages in Setup.
  Replace your Messaging Permission Set License
  We’re replacing the Messaging User permission set license with a new one named Messaging
  Unlimited. To avoid interrupting feature access, if you upgrade your Messaging licensing model from
  Digital Engagement to Agentforce Contact Center Digital, assign the new permission set license to your
  Messaging users. If you’re still using Digital Engagement, no action is needed.
  Accept Clearer Terms and Conditions in Enhanced Chat
  Read and accept a modernized Terms and Conditions page for Enhanced Chat channels. When you
  create your first Enhanced Chat channel, you’re prompted to accept terms and conditions only once
  per Salesforce org. Get the information you need quicker with shorter, simplified text and links.
  Let Service Reps Edit Chat and Messaging Responses with AI
  With Write with AI for Enhanced Chat and Messaging, service reps can instantly refine, expand, or
  shorten their messages to match your brand's tone, decreasing response time while improving the
  quality and consistency of customer interactions.
  Save Money by Hiding the Real-Time Translations Preview Bar



    1044

Salesforce Release Notes Service

  Reduce calls to Agentforce Speech Foundation, each of which can consume flex credits if your free
  limit is reached, by hiding the Real-Time Translations preview bar. When the bar is hidden, a service
  rep won’t see a translation preview as they type, but their message will be translated when sent to the
  end user, calling Agentforce Speech Foundation just once.
  Protect Service Reps’ Privacy in Business-Initiated Outbound Messaging
  Replace your Service reps’ first and last name with your Company Name in the disclaimer that’s sent to

  Educate Service Reps About Chat Exit Behavior
  Enable confirmation modals to provide Service reps with more information about what happens when

  Streamline the Management of WhatsApp Templates
  Build and manage Utility and Marketing WhatsApp templates directly in Salesforce. You can now
  create, edit, submit for approval, publish, and delete these template types in Messaging Component
  Builder. By managing WhatsApp templates directly in Salesforce, you save time and minimize
  synchronization issues with your WhatsApp Business account (WABA). Previously, you created the
  WhatsApp templates and managed them in your WhatsApp Business account, and then import them
  into Salesforce.
  Take Ownership of your Data Residency on Unified WhatsApp
  Define the specific country or region where your WhatsApp data is stored at rest on Meta's side. By
  giving you control over data residency for each individual phone number, we help you meet your
  internal compliance and regulatory requirements.
  Review De-Duplication Activity for Unified WhatsApp
  New logic ensures that you contact the most recently added individual in a Unified WhatsApp channel,
  and new error codes explain why other duplicate individuals weren’t contacted. Previously, there
  wasn’t logic to choose an Individual, and there weren’t error codes to explain why we made the choice.
  Legacy Chat Is Being Retired
  Legacy Chat is scheduled for retirement on February 14, 2026. You can continue to use Legacy Chat
  until that date, but we recommend transitioning to Enhanced Chat for modernized customer
  communication. Enhanced Chat offers many of the Legacy Chat features that you love, plus
  asynchronous conversations that can be picked back up at any time.
  Bring Your Own Channel

  Support for Migration of SMS Channel Metadata from Sandbox to Production and Vice Versa
  You can now migrate SMS channels metadata from a sandbox org to a production org using metadata
  APIs and the tools that you're comfortable with.
  Manage Activation and Deactivation of Enhanced Messaging Channels in Bulk
  You can now activate and deactivate enhanced SMS messaging channels in both sandbox and
  production environments, either in bulk using a CSV file or individually at the record level.
  Convert Approved SMS Codes to SMS Channels in Service Cloud
  You can now convert your approved SMS codes to SMS channels in bulk or individually from Setup.

and assign the new Messaging Unlimited permission set license. You can assign it individually from the

    Review De-Duplication Activity for Unified WhatsApp

    New logic ensures that you contact the most recently added individual in a Unified WhatsApp channel,
    and new error codes explain why other duplicate individuals weren’t contacted. Previously, there wasn’t
    logic to choose an Individual, and there weren’t error codes to explain why we made the choice.

    Where: This change applies to Unified WhatsApp in Enterprise and Unlimited editions for Marketing
    Cloud Engagement Growth and Advanced Editions.

    Why: If a Unified Individual has multiple associated individuals, each with the same phone number, we
    only contact one Individual. We chose the latest Individual that was created with that phone number.

    We introduced three new error codes to help explain why an individual wasn’t contacted.

    •  SF-3025 - The message wasn't sent because the recipient's phone number wasn't a valid E.164
    •  number. Correct the phone number and try again.
       SF-3045 - The message wasn't sent because the recipient's phone number is associated with a
    •  different individual ID.
       SF-3035 - The message wasn't sent because a contact record wasn't found.

    How: To view the Individuals associated with a Unified Individual, and to see error messages explaining
    which Individuals were or weren’t contacted, create a Data Cloud Data Explorer view. For a Data Lake
    Object view, add the Error Code and Not Sent Reason columns. For a Data Model Object view, add the
    Messaging Error Code and Error Message columns.

Bring Your Own Channel

Improve the experience for reps and messaging end users by exploring the latest enhancements and
updates for Bring Your Own Channel for Messaging and Bring Your Own Channel for Contact Center as a
Service (CCaaS).

  Improve Security in Bring Your Own Channel by Migrating to an External Client App
  External client apps (ECAs) are the next generation of connected apps, designed to improve security
  and address packaging and distribution issues. While existing connected apps for Bring Your Own
  Channel integrations will continue to work, you won’t be able to create new connected apps without
  first requesting the ability from Salesforce Support starting with Spring ’26. This step is part of a
  Salesforce plan to eventually replace connected apps with ECAs. Consider migrating to an external
  client app for Bring Your Own Channel.
  Maintain Service for Your Bring Your Own Channel Integration by Migrating Settings Fields
  To improve the scalability of Bring Your Own Channel messaging services, we implemented changes to
  event-driven settings fields in the ConversationChannelDefinition and CustomMsgChannel objects.
  New fields are available in Winter ’26 (API version 65.0), and old fields are removed in Spring ’26 (API
  version 66.0). These are breaking changes.
  Increase Rep Efficiency by Ending or Inactivating Messaging Sessions from Your Partner System
  Use the End or Inactivate a Messaging Session API to quickly end or suspend a messaging session,
  regardless of whether the action is initiated by a messaging end user or your partner system. Reps
  receive a status notification when a session is ended or inactivated. This allows them to start After
  Conversation Work (ACW) if enabled and move on to the next session faster.

Maintain Service for Your Bring Your Own Channel Integration by Migrating Settings Fields

To improve the scalability of Bring Your Own Channel messaging services, we implemented changes to
event-driven settings fields in the ConversationChannelDefinition and CustomMsgChannel objects. New
fields are available in Winter ’26 (API version 65.0), and old fields are removed in Spring ’26 (API version
66.0). These are breaking changes.

Where: This change applies to Bring Your Own Channel for Messaging and Bring Your Own Channel for
CCaaS. View required editions.

Who: These changes impact partners who create messaging provider integrations for Bring Your Own
Channel for Messaging or Bring Your Own Channel for CCaaS and customers who have self-implemented
Bring Your Own Channel for Messaging. These changes also impact customers using partner-provided
managed packages with removed fields. Customers must update their managed package to one that
contains supported fields by Spring ’26.

How: Learn more about the removed event-driven settings fields and assess whether your
implementation requires updates to migrate to their replacements. Make required changes by Spring
’26, when the fields will be removed.

•  For ConversationChannelDefinition, deprecated fields are IsInboundReceiptsEnabled,
   IsRoutingWorkResultEnabled, and IsTypingIndicatorDisabled.
    --  Use EventCapabilitiesIsInboundAcknwOptionExposed instead of IsInboundReceiptsEnabled.
        Use EventCapabilitiesIsRoutingWorkResultSupported instead of IsRoutingWorkResultEnabled.
•   - Use EventCapabilitiesIsTypingIndicatorOptionHidden instead of IsTypingIndicatorDisabled.
   For CustomMsgChannel, deprecated fields are HasInboundReceipts and HasTypingIndicator.
    --  Use EventCapabilitiesIsInboundAcknowledgementEnabled instead of HasInboundReceipts.
        Use EventCapabilitiesIsTypingIndicatorDisabled instead of HasTypingIndicator.

If you don’t make required updates by Spring ’26 or if customers use a managed package version with
removed fields starting in Spring ’26, your implementation will break.

Accelerate service delivery and governance by deploying preconfigured request workflows and direct

  Benefit from prestructured attributes, intake forms, and automated fulfillment flows with templates

  Deploy service catalog items that use direct API integration with external systems, dramatically

    1061

Salesforce Release Notes Service

  Prioritize Issues Using Service Management Privileges
  Ensure critical employee issues receive immediate attention by using Service Management Privileges.
  Admins can now assign privileges to employees and set a specific access threshold to identify
  incidents requiring special handling. When an incident is created or reported by an employee whose
  access level meets this threshold, a banner is displayed on the Incident record page of the fulfillers.
  The distinct visual cue streamlines triage, ensuring your most important stakeholders receive
  prioritized resolution without manual intervention.
  Demote Major Incidents When Business Impact Changes
  Maintain flexibility in your support processes by de-escalating major incidents when impact and
  severity decrease. Authorized users can demote a major incident back to a standard incident without
  disrupting existing approval work items or ongoing resolution efforts. Align your IT help desk's
  response with the actual business needs, and allow for dynamic adjustments as situations stabilize.
  Do More with the Redesigned Agentforce Employee Self-Service Portal
  Transform your employees' interaction with the IT desk, making it faster, simpler, and more efficient.
  The redesigned Agentforce Employee Center portal introduces AI Search that provides instant,
  summarized answers and suggested next steps, helping employees resolve issues immediately without
  logging a ticket. The portal also unifies the service catalog, knowledge base, and asset management
  processes into a single, intuitive interface.
  Prevent Outages with CI-Based Change Conflict Detection
  Reduce change failure rates and ensure a stable IT environment by gaining early visibility into potential
  conflicts. When multiple change requests target the same configuration item (CI) during an
  overlapping implementation timeframe, conflicts are identified and captured automatically. Change
  fulfillers and managers can view these records to collaborate and resolve them. Replace manual cross-
  referencing and prevent IT teams from inadvertently disrupting the same CI simultaneously.
  Create Service Requests from Incidents when Appropriate
  IT teams can create service requests from incidents when the reported issue represents a user need,
  such as access or provisioning, rather than a service disruption. Creating a service request routes the
  request through the correct fulfillment workflow, and avoids incident-specific timelines and SLAs.
  Track IT Service Requests Using Dedicated Service Request Records
  Manage IT service requests using the new Service Request record instead of the generic Case record.
  IT teams can use a specialized data model that includes attributes designed specifically for request
  fulfillment, to manage high-volume, repeatable tasks efficiently. By distinguishing service requests
  from cases and incidents, you ensure the right process, SLAs, and reporting model is applied to every
  IT task.
  Access Comprehensive Employee Data with Employee 360 Insights
  Give your IT help desk a centralized, 360-degree view of all employee assets, service requests, support
  cases, and historical interactions to maximize operational efficiency. Support reps can quickly
  troubleshoot active issues, review past support trends, and access critical employee data without
  switching context. Reps can then use these details to create service requests for employees and deliver
  personalized support that drastically reduces resolution times.
  Strengthen Data Integrity with Default Field Validations for Changes and Releases
  Admins can now activate default field validations for change requests and releases to automatically
  prevent common errors, such as invalid date ranges or missing required fields. These preconfigured



    1062

  checks enforce data consistency during both record creation and updates. By safeguarding data

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience in Unlimited, Enterprise, and Performance Editions

Who: To manage major incidents, you need the Major Incident Fulfiller permission set group.

How: On an incident record that’s marked as a major incident, click Demote Major Incident. The record
is then treated as a standard incident but can be promoted or proposed as a major incident if the
situation escalates again. A banner is displayed on the incident record to notify the incident owner and

How: From Setup, enter CMDB in the Quick Find box and select CMDB and Service Graph under Feature
Settings. Review the Provisioning Status section. If the status shows Not Provisioned or Failed, click
Provision CMDB. Provisioning runs in the background and progresses through different stages. When the
status shows Provisioned, you can click Configure CMDB using Salesforce Go to complete setup.

  Extend Asset Coverage by Integrating Microsoft Intune with Salesforce CMDB
  Connect Microsoft Intune with Salesforce CMDB to bring device inventory data into your configuration

  completeness, and reduce manual effort during asset onboarding.
  Understand Asset Discovery Activity by Using the Discovery Sources Card
  View and analyze asset discovery activity by using the Discovery Sources card in a Configuration Item
  (CI) record. Use audit fields to understand when a configuration item was first discovered, last
  updated, or rescanned by each discovery source. The Discovery card on the CI record also displays
  timestamps for agentless scans, agent scans, cloud connectors, and API-based integrations. The fields
  give you insights into asset freshness and help verify that discovery jobs are running as expected.
  Analyze Installed Software and System Components with the New Components Tab
  Review and analyze installed software and system components by using the Components tab on a

  inventory into structured categories and provides a searchable, filterable table. You can also add
  components manually when required.

  reassignment.

  lifecycle.

    Agentforce Service Assistant

    Expand the capabilities of Agentforce Service Assistant by adding the Case Feed and Messaging Session
    and Voice Call records as grounding sources to improve service plan accuracy and relevance. We've also
    added translation support, allowing service plans to be presented in the service rep's preferred language.

     Draft Service Plans in Service Rep's Preferred Language
     Have service reps work Cases faster using service plans that are translated into their preferred
     language. When service reps draft a service plan, the plan is generated in your company’s preferred
     language. Additionally, when have Real-Time Translations enabled, the service plan is then translated



     1088

Salesforce Release Notes Service

   into the service rep's preferred language.
   Use Case Feed as the Latest Grounding Source to Strengthen Service Plans
   Adding Case Feed data to Service Assistant improves the accuracy and relevance of Service Plans. This
   richer, more contextual case activity enables the assistant to deliver more informed, relevant
   recommendations.
   Add More Context to Service Plans with Messaging Session and Voice Call Record Grounding
   Enhance the accuracy and details of service plans by grounding Service Assistant in Messaging Session
   and Voice Call records. When these records are attached to a case, Service Assistant analyzes the
   transcripts to create a case summary that summarizes what took place in the conversation and drafts a
   service plan that continues from where the conversation ended. The grounding process boosts rep
   productivity by ensuring the service plan continues exactly from where the prior interaction left off and
   avoids repeating steps and manual context gathering.
   Draft Comprehensive Service Plans with Expanded Data Access
   Service Assistant now drafts all service plans based on the permissions of the ServicePlanner User (the
   digital agent), rather than the individual service rep. This ensures that every service plan contains the
   most detailed information, regardless of an individual rep's field-level access or sharing rules.

Draft Service Plans in Service Rep's Preferred Language

Have service reps work Cases faster using service plans that are translated into their preferred language.
When service reps draft a service plan, the plan is generated in your company’s preferred language.
Additionally, when have Real-Time Translations enabled, the service plan is then translated into the
service rep's preferred language.

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience in Enterprise, Unlimited, and Developer editions.

• Translation of service plans into your company’s default language is available with Einstein for Service,
• Agentforce for Service, and Agentforce 1 editions.
   Translation of service plans into your service reps preferred language is available only with Agentforce
   for Service and Agentforce 1 editions.

Who:

• Translating and viewing service plans in your company’s preferred language is available for all users by
• default.
   To turn on Real-Time Translations for Service Assistant, Salesforce admins need the Service Planner
• Builder permission set.
   To view service plans in their preferred language, service reps need the Service Plan Translation and
   Service Plan User permission sets.

Why: Previously, service plans only supported English, which slowed down service reps who weren't
fluent in English. Now, service plans are translated to provide native-language clarity so service reps work
faster and efficiently. Specifically:

• Service Assistant automatically drafts service plans in your company's preferred language when the
   language is supported in Prompt Builder. See Supported Languages in Prompt Builder.

Add More Context to Service Plans with Messaging Session and Voice Call Record
Grounding

Enhance the accuracy and details of service plans by grounding Service Assistant in Messaging Session
and Voice Call records. When these records are attached to a case, Service Assistant analyzes the
transcripts to create a case summary that summarizes what took place in the conversation and drafts a
service plan that continues from where the conversation ended. The grounding process boosts rep
productivity by ensuring the service plan continues exactly from where the prior interaction left off and
avoids repeating steps and manual context gathering.

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience in Enterprise, Unlimited, and Developer editions
with Einstein for Service, Agentforce for Service, and Agentforce 1 editions.

When: This feature was originally released on December 18, 2025. We’ve included it in the Spring '26
Release Notes to increase the visibility of the feature.

Who:

• To set up Messaging Session and Voice Call record grounding for Service Assistant, Salesforce admins
• need the Service Planner Builder permission set.
   To ground service plans in Messaging Session or Voice Call records, the ServicePlanner User needs the
   Conversation Grounding Access custom permission set that has these permissions.
    -- App permission: Access Conversations Entries, View All Voice and Video Calls
     Messaging Session object permission: Read, View All Records



                                                       1092

Salesforce Release Notes Service

• To view Messaging Session or Voice Call information in a service plan, service reps need the Service
   Planner User permission set.

Why: By automatically grounding the case summary and service plan in the related conversation
transcript, Service Assistant limits the need for service reps to manually review and synthesize the
Messing Session or Voice Call record. In addition, the service plan starts from where the original
conversation ended, which speeds up case resolution and prevents the duplication of resolution steps
already taken the conversation.

Draft Comprehensive Service Plans with Expanded Data Access

Service Assistant now drafts all service plans based on the permissions of the ServicePlanner User (the
digital agent), rather than the individual service rep. This ensures that every service plan contains the
most detailed information, regardless of an individual rep's field-level access or sharing rules.

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience in Enterprise, Unlimited, and Developer editions
with Einstein for Service, Agentforce for Service, and Agentforce 1 editions.

When: This feature was originally released on December 18, 2025. We’ve included it in the Spring '26
Release Notes to increase the visibility of the feature.

Who: This change applies to the ServicePlanner User and service reps.

Why: Previously, plans were drafted based on the service rep's permissions, which could limit the
inclusion of relevant data based on field-level access, object access, and sharing rules. For example, by
using the ServicePlanner User's permissions for plan generation:

• Service plans now include all fields and object information set in your Service AI Grounding
• configuration, even if the service rep doesn’t have field-level access.
   Plan steps are always grounded in your relevant knowledge articles, even when the service rep doesn’t
   have access to the articles used to create the plan.

How: The feature is enabled by default, so no action is required. However, you should review your
configurations for all grounding sources. To learn more about how permissions determine data access for
each Service Assistant feature, see Service Assistant Grounding Data Access.

   Salesforce Help: Service Assistant Grounding Data Access

Gain Instant Case Context with Case Timeline

Give your reps a single, unified, and intelligent timeline component for cases. This new component
replaces the current fragmented collection of feeds and related lists with a single curated view of case-
related events. Reps get instant context with a proactive workspace that intelligently organizes customer
conversations, internal team collaboration, and key case milestones. The new timeline brings together
channels like emails, chats, and messages into a clean, threaded view.

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience in Enterprise, Performance, Unlimited, and
Developer editions where Industries Service Excellence is enabled.

Why: Reps spend too much time navigating disparate systems and sifting through data to find critical
information, which causes information fatigue and slower resolution times. Without immediate insight
into case progress or historical data, it’s hard for reps to prioritize effectively and identify root causes. The
new timeline gives a scannable, easy-to-understand view of all activity. It visually distinguishes owner
changes, SLA breaches, and escalations as clearly marked milestones. Pre-configured Timeline Templates
are available immediately for use in the Timeline feature, requiring no configuration.

How: In Setup, in the Quick Find Box, find and select Timeline. In the Timeline window, turn on the

Enhance Your Security of Organization-Wide Email Addresses

Organization-Wide Email Addresses (OWA) are now required to be verified before sending Case emails
with custom content. This security enhancement prevents unauthorized use of the
<noreply@salesforce.com> address and protects against potential phishing attempts.

Where: This change applies to all Salesforce editions that support Case email functionality.

Why: This security update ensures that all customers configure and verify their Organization-Wide Email
Address before sending Case emails containing custom content. Previously, some organizations could
bypass this requirement, creating a security risk where unauthorized users could potentially send
malicious emails using the trusted @salesforce.com domain. This enhancement closes that security gap
by enforcing verification requirements across all organizations.

How: If you've already configured and verified your Organization-Wide Email Address, no action is
needed. If you haven't set up your Organization-Wide Email Address or if your current setup wasn't
previously enforced, you must configure a verified Organization-Wide Email Address before sending
emails with custom content. For setup instructions, see Set Up Organization-Wide Email Addresses in
Salesforce Help.

Enable Translation for Case Comments

Give your support reps the ability to translate case comments into their local language and write
responses that translate to the customer’s language. The translation feature adds a translation button to
case comments. Reps can select a language for translation when creating a comment.

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience in Essentials, Group, Professional, Enterprise,
Performance, Unlimited, and Developer editions where Service Cloud Translations is enabled.

Why: Translation in case comments provides reps immediate context for the case without requiring
external translation tools. Reps can effectively reply to customers in their local language. This
functionality reduces effort and improves communication for reps.

Merge Cases from the Case Related List on Standard Objects

Enable your service reps to merge duplicate cases using the Merge Cases button from the case related
list of all standard objects. This allows reps to quickly merge cases without navigating to the case page.

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience in Essentials, Group, Professional, Enterprise,
Performance, Unlimited, and Developer editions.

Why: When reps discover duplicate cases they need to navigate to Cases to find and merge them. This
wastes time that can be better used elsewhere. Having the Merge Case button in the case related list of
all standard objects saves reps the time that they would use to navigate to the specific case pages and
merge the cases.

How: The Merge Case button will be visible in the case related list of all standard objects. You can select
up to 3 cases and use the Merge Case button to merge them into a single case. This feature is enabled by
default in all orgs including production environments.

Customize Close Case Actions by Record Type

You can now manage different close case layouts for various record types and profiles within Lightning
Experience. This update addresses a previous limitation where the standard close case button was
restricted to a single layout editor. By creating multiple actions, you provide your service reps the ability
to associate close case buttons with different record types and layouts.

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience in Group, Professional, Enterprise, Performance,
Unlimited, and Developer Editions.

How: To offer close case actions for different record types, create multiple Update Record quick actions
for the Case object. In Setup, in the Object Manager search for Case and select Case. In Case select
Buttons, Links, and Actions, and select New Action. In the New Action window, in Action Type select
Update a Record. In Standard Label Type, select Close Case. In Name, use the prefix CloseCaseLightning
for these actions to ensure that the status field only displays closed picklist values.

Entitlements and Milestones

Define rules to automatically pause milestone timers when the next step is outside a service rep's
control. Use Agentforce SLA Summary for comprehensive performance analytics. Get real-time visibility
into milestone status across parent and child records to ensure better coordination and alignment across
all teams contributing to resolution.

  Improve SLA Reporting by Using Rule-based Milestone Pause
  Free up your service reps from the manual overhead of stopping a record when the next step is
  outside their purview. Admins can set rules to automatically pause milestones when the defined
  conditions are met. For example, a milestone can be paused automatically if the case status is
  “Waiting for Customer.” The milestone timer stops during the pause duration and resumes when the
  pause conditions change. The target date is reevaluated when the milestone unpauses. This helps with
  more accurate SLA reporting and clearly highlights delays.
  Keep Departments Aligned on SLA Commitments with Bidirectional Milestone Visibility
  Get real-time visibility into Service Level Agreements (SLAs) and Operation Level Agreements (OLAs)
  commitments and status by viewing milestones across parent and child records. This feature enables
  transparent, real-time visibility into child and parent milestone statuses. This allows for better
  coordination and alignment on SLA and OLA commitments and timelines when departments or


                                                                                                                                                 1106

Salesforce Release Notes Service

  vendors besides the service reps also contribute to resolutions.
  Optimize SLA Compliance by Using Agentforce SLA Summary
  Get a complete view of Service Level Agreement (SLA) adherence with Agentforce SLA Summary. Track
  key metrics like SLA breach data and trends, milestone performance, service rep performance and
  workload, and risk indicators. You can also monitor average response and resolution times against SLA
  targets, and see which records are close to missing an SLA.

Improve SLA Reporting by Using Rule-based Milestone Pause

Free up your service reps from the manual overhead of stopping a record when the next step is outside
their purview. Admins can set rules to automatically pause milestones when the defined conditions are
met. For example, a milestone can be paused automatically if the case status is “Waiting for Customer.”
The milestone timer stops during the pause duration and resumes when the pause conditions change.
The target date is reevaluated when the milestone unpauses. This helps with more accurate SLA
reporting and clearly highlights delays.

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience in Professional, Enterprise, Performance, Unlimited,
and Developer editions with the Service Cloud.

How: From the SLA Policies page, select the SLA policy for which you want to create a milestone. On the
Milestones tab, click New Milestone. In the New Milestone window, go to the Pause tab and define your
milestone pause criteria. Save your milestone and activate the SLA Policy.

See Also
  Knowledge Article:Automatically Pause Record Milestones Based on Predefined Rules

Keep Departments Aligned on SLA Commitments with Bidirectional
Milestone Visibility

Get real-time visibility into Service Level Agreements (SLAs) and Operation Level Agreements (OLAs)
commitments and status by viewing milestones across parent and child records. This feature enables
transparent, real-time visibility into child and parent milestone statuses. This allows for better
coordination and alignment on SLA and OLA commitments and timelines when departments or vendors
besides the service reps also contribute to resolutions.

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience in Professional, Enterprise, Performance, Unlimited,
and Developer editions with the Service Cloud.

How: On the New Milestone page, select the Show this milestone on all child, parent, and related
records checkbox to show the milestone across all its associated records.

Enhance Survey Readability with Revamped Matrix Questions View

Improve survey readability on desktops and smaller screens with the revamped view for matrix
questions. The new design presents options for each question in a dedicated dropdown menu, making it
easier to read the full question and select an option.



    1108

Salesforce Release Notes        Service

Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience and Salesforce Classic in Enterprise, Unlimited, and
Developer Editions where Feedback Management - Starter or Feedback Management - Growth is
enabled.

Why: The prior tabular format used for matrix questions presented multiple challenges for users,
especially on smaller screens. The dense layout often required scrolling to view all selection options.
Longer question text sometimes crowded the options, making both elements difficult to read. The
redesigned view resolves these issues by giving each matrix question its own dropdown, which
significantly enhances readability and simplifies the process of selecting options on mobile and desktop
devices.

How: In the Survey Builder, click Add Question, and then select Matrix.

Strengthen Employee Trust with Confidential Case Reporting

Give your employees a secure channel to report confidential workplace issues, such as harassment,
discrimination, or misconduct. Employees can report these issues directly from the employee portal or

    1112

Salesforce Release Notes Service

Who: To use this feature, users need the Employee Hub Community User add-on permission set license,

• Employee Portal: On the Employee Portal, go to the Help Center tab and click New Confidential Case.
   Provide details, review, and submit the case for your case ID. A corresponding public complaint record
• is automatically created to route the issue discreetly to the right personnel.

    Get More Done in the Lightning Article Editor

    Write knowledge articles more efficiently with the improved "What You See Is What You Get" (WYSIWYG)
    Lightning Article Editor, which shows exactly how your content appears in real time. Take advantage of its
    streamlined features to create top-notch content.

    Where: This change applies to Lightning Experience in Essentials, Professional, Enterprise, Unlimited,
    and Developer editions.




          1114

Salesforce Release Notes Service

How: To help you write knowledge articles more efficiently, Lightning Article Editor has several key
improvements.

Here are the general improvements.

• You can now use Dark Mode in the article editor, making it easier to edit content in low-light
• environments.
   Editing articles on the iPad is now easier. The expanded toolbar in narrow layouts no longer blocks
• your editing space, allowing full access to toolbar options while you edit.
   The editor toolbar is now visually consistent. Split buttons now match the size and look of the other
• buttons.
   You can now edit smart links in bulleted or numbered lists in knowledge articles without affecting the
• formatting of the list.
   To improve article readability, nested ordered lists now default to a hierarchical style, replacing the
   previous numeric-only format. The first level defaults to numeric (1, 2, 3), the second level to
   alphabetic (a, b, c), and the third level to roman numerals (i, ii, iii). While you can still manually change
   styles for individual items, we recommend updating them one at a time while we to improve multi-
   selection behavior.
        Note For Knowledge articles created from the Spring '26 release through March 10, 2026, the
        ordered list numbering style will automatically update to the new hierarchical format. This
        automatic update applies only if you used the default numeric-only style. If you have set a
        different numbering style for sublists, your custom formatting will stay the same.
•• We've resolved general formatting issues with numbered and bulleted lists in the article editor.
   The format and alignment of bulleted lists are now the same in the draft version and the published
• article.
   Anchor links in Knowledge articles now smoothly scroll to the target section, giving readers a better
• experience in long articles.
   In Chromium browsers like Chrome, Edge, Opera, and Brave, dragging content in the article editor
• caused unexpected scrolling. This issue is now fixed, making drag-and-drop much better.
   The tooltips on toolbar buttons now disappear as expected when you move your mouse away.

Here are the accessibility-related improvements.

• Screen reader users can now give article feedback more easily. Screen readers correctly announce
• “Was this article helpful?” when they reach the Like or Dislike buttons on the article.
   We increased the contrast ratio for non-text elements like icons, buttons, and borders in the article
• editor to meet accessibility standards, making the interface easier to use for users with low-vision.
   The article editor now shows the word count and includes ARIA label, making it easy for screen reader
   users to track their word count as they write.

   Salesforce Help:Lightning Article Editor

Why: Proactive Service identifies customer-impacting issues before they are reported. The detection and
segmentation UI makes it easier for you to set up event-based and scheduled-based detection, define
affected customers, and prepare outreach and fulfillment plans more accurately. This enhancement
improves detection quality, expands use cases, and ensures timely, targeted communications.

How: From the Proactive Service Detection and Segmentation page, select an event or scheduled
trigger, define conditions, and generate the impacted-customer segment. In planning, configure the
resolution method and Unified Catalog automation. During outreach, customers receive the scenario
message and complete the linked fulfillment flow.

Guide Your Users Through Interactive Troubleshooting for Proactive
Scenarios

Help service reps proactively resolve customer issues by generating AI-driven troubleshooting plans
when no automation exists. Service reps define a scenario prompt during campaign planning, and
Agentforce Service agent uses it to guide customers through a tailored troubleshooting session after they
open an outreach. This approach broadens coverage of proactive issues, accelerates resolution, and
captures conversation traces to improve future troubleshooting plans.

Where: This change applies to Aura or LWR sites accessed through Lightning Experience and Salesforce
Classic in Enterprise, Professional, Unlimited, and Developer editions. Also, applies to Proactive Service
Add-on, Proactive Service For Community Add-on, and Unified Catalog Add-on.

Who: This change is available to users with the ServiceDeskUser or Service User license, and those
assigned Data Cloud or Service Cloud user licenses. Customers accessing Experience Cloud sites must
have Customer Community Plus licenses.

Why: Service reps can now guide customers through interactive troubleshooting when no prebuilt
automation exists. AI-driven plans walk customers through tailored steps to diagnose and resolve issues,



    1118

Salesforce Release Notes Service

reducing dependency on screen flows and providing conversation data to optimize future
troubleshooting.

How: In the scenario configuration, select guided troubleshooting as the resolution method and provide
a scenario prompt. When a customer opens the Experience Cloud site and the resolution type is
interactive troubleshooting, Agentforce Service agent begins the session using the provided prompt. All
interactions are captured automatically for analysis and optimization.

Give Your Users Personalized Self-Service with a Unified Customer Profile

Surface a real-time, unified customer profile to deliver personalized, context-aware self-service. You can
read up-to-date attributes, activity history, and insights like sentiment and automatically write new
activity data as users interact. Your users benefit from fewer forms to fill out, faster completion, and a
more relevant self-service journey.

Where: This change applies to Aura or LWR sites accessed through Lightning Experience and Salesforce
Classic in Enterprise, Professional, Unlimited, and Developer with Foundations or Agentforce 1 Editions.
Access to some standard agent actions requires additional add-on licenses.

Who: You must have access to the Experience Cloud site, Unified Catalog flows, or Agentforce Service
agent based on your existing site configuration.

Why: Self-Service journeys work best when they reflect each customer’s history and current context. With
access to profile attributes, behavioral activity, and computed insights, your Self-Service surfaces can
adapt UI elements, prefill forms, and guide users more intelligently. Agentforce Service agent and Unified
Catalog flows can draw on the same profile context to deliver consistent answers and reduce customer
effort.

How: From Setup, configure your Self-Service surfaces to use the unified profile data model. Map
customer profile fields to form inputs and enable activity writeback so new user actions appear in the
customer’s activity stream in real time.

Help Experience Cloud Site Users Track Their History with a Personalized
Activity Timeline Wrapper

Give your Experience Cloud site users a clear view of their activity history with an in-page timeline
wrapper that highlights logins, case updates, messages, Website Engagement, and Web Search
Engagement events. Site members can quickly understand what has happened, where they left off, and
what has changed since their last visit, without navigating multiple pages.

Where: This change applies to Aura sites accessed through Lightning Experience and Salesforce Classic in
Enterprise, Professional, Unlimited, and Developer editions.

Who: Experience Cloud site users with standard access to the site, permission to view their own activity
feed, and Manage Timeline. Customers accessing Experience Cloud sites require Customer Community
Plus licenses.


    1119

Salesforce Release Notes Service

Why: Customers often lose track of past interactions, leading to repeated questions and unnecessary
support cases. A consolidated timeline wrapper helps users orient themselves, review progress, and
resume tasks with confidence. By surfacing events such as logins, messages, case updates, Website
Engagement, and Web Search Engagement, the timeline provides transparency and strengthens trust by
giving users a full record of their engagement.

How: Create a Timeline on the User base object and configure it to show events from the user’s unified
profile, including logins, messages, case updates, Website Engagement, and Web Search Engagement. In
Experience Builder for Aura sites, drag the Timeline Wrapper into your site’s navigation area and select
the appropriate timeline from the Configuration dropdown.

Guide Experience Cloud Site Users with a Proactive Pending Task Banner

The personalized Pending Task banner on the Experience Cloud site homepage helps users see and act
on high-priority tasks as soon as they log in. These recommendations are based on the user’s profile,
recent activity, and AI-powered insights.

Where: This change applies to Aura or LWR sites accessed through Lightning Experience and Salesforce
Classic in Enterprise, Professional, Unlimited, and Developer editions.

Who: This change is available to users with the ServiceDeskUser or Service User license and those
assigned Data Cloud or Service Cloud user licenses. Customers accessing Experience Cloud sites require
Customer Community Plus licenses.

Why: A proactive Pending Task banner makes it easy by showing the most important action at the right
time, improving task completion rates and lowering support volume. With context-driven logic,
Experience Cloud site can guide users through critical steps automatically.

How: Add the Pending Task banner component to an Experience Cloud site homepage in Experience
Builder. Place the Pending Task banner in the header section of the page for optimal visibility. Place the
banner on an authenticated page when the site requires login to show personalized content. Set up rule
criteria or context mappings to show tasks based on unified profile data and recent activity. Turn on the
AI Experiences tile, including the Allow users to personalize the Self Service Experience toggle, to support
insight-driven task recommendations.

  Personalization for Self-Service

Bill AI Self-Service Usage More Accurately with Session-Based Tracking

Get more accurate billing for AI powered Self Service activity by tracking usage per authenticated login
session.This feature groups all AI interactions, like Knowledge Article Summary or Dynamic Q&A within a
single session, providing usage reports that reflect how customers engage with Agentic Portal features.

Where: This change applies to Aura or LWR sites accessed through Lightning Experience and Salesforce
Classic in Enterprise, Professional, Unlimited, and Developer editions.


    1120

Salesforce Release Notes Service

Who: This feature is available to authenticated users working in orgs that use Customer Community,
Customer Community Plus, Customer Community Login, Customer Community Plus Login, and the
corresponding unlimited login variants. Users must have access to Agentic Portal capabilities, including
AI Knowledge Article Summary and Dynamic Q&A.

Why: Agentic Portals introduce AI-driven features that are often used together in a single visit. Tracking
usage at the session level gives you clearer consumption data, reduces noise in billing reports, and aligns
with the broader Self-Service monetization strategy. You get transparent usage records, easier auditing,
and greater accuracy when customers operate within contractual AI usage limits.

How: Session based usage tracking records AI feature activity for each authenticated login session.
During a session, all AI interactions are collected and combined into a single usage record. Billing entries
are created on a daily or configurable schedule and include session details and aggregated activity. Usage
logs and reports provide visibility into feature consumption.

Improve Dynamic Q&A Performance with Persisted Questions and Answers
for Authenticated Users

Dynamic Q&A now loads faster and reduces Large Language Model (LLM) calls by persisting generated
questions and answers for authenticated users. Previously, Dynamic Q&A regenerated a new set of
questions each time an authenticated user viewed an article. The feature now stores the generated
questions, which improves performance and gives users quicker access to relevant answers.

Where: This change applies to Aura or LWR sites accessed through Lightning Experience and Salesforce
Classic in Enterprise, Professional, Unlimited, and Developer editions.

Who: Available to authenticated Experience Cloud users with Customer Community or Customer
Community Plus licenses. Also available to internal users with a Knowledge license when accessing
knowledge-related features. Experience Cloud site builders need permissions to add and configure the
Dynamic Q&A component in Experience Builder.

Why: In the previous release, Dynamic Q&A persisted questions and answers only for guest users.
Authenticated users received newly generated questions on every request, which required repeated calls
to the large language model and increased latency. With this enhancement, Dynamic Q&A now persists
generated questions for authenticated users as well, which reduces repeated processing, lowers overall
Large Language Model (LLM) usage, and delivers faster article-level answers.

How: Dynamic Q&A now stores the generated set of questions and answers for authenticated users.
When a user returns to the same article, the component shows the persisted questions instead of
generating new ones. This reduces load times and avoids repeated calls to the Large Language Model
(LLM). Component behavior and configuration in Experience Builder remain unchanged.
